[The Master] said, "The Eight Hundred Li of Dongting—this is not yet broad. [A monk] asked, "What is the essence of True Suchness?
He replied, "The yakṣa kneels; his eyes are black. [The monk] asked, "What is the function of True Suchness? He replied, "The vajra strikes, and the iron mountain crumbles."
Lingyun attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms. He offered this verse: "For thirty years I have sought the sword-wielder;
Time and again the leaves fall and sprouts emerge. Since that first glimpse of the peach blossoms, To this very day, I have had no more doubt.
He presented this to Guishan, who said, "One who enters through conditions will never lose what they have attained. You must guard and uphold it well. Xuansha remarked:
"It is true; it is most truly true. I dare say you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
Miaoxi said, "When one family has trouble, a hundred families are busy.
Master Yangqi addressed the assembly, saying, "When body and mind are pure, all objects are pure; when all objects are pure, the body..."
With a pure mind, do you still know where the Old Man of Yangqi fell? "Losing money in the river, one must fish for it in the river.
Master Deshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Sons, from morning until evening, what business is there?
Do not seek to flaunt your donkey lips and horse mouths. Would you ask this old fellow Deshan? "I am not afraid of you," he said. I wonder, do you sons have [any understanding]?
"What is there to doubt? Lately, in this age of the Dharma's decline, there have been many ghosts and spirits. They run about in groups near people's homes saying, 'I am a Zen Master.
I do not know how much of the Way of Zen they have learned; let them speak it to this old man.

You lot—those bald-headed slaves from all quarters who teach you to practice for the sake of becoming Buddhas—how many Buddhas have you actually become by running about near people's homes? If you have none..."
"You may learn. Furthermore, why do you run about? If there is anyone who has learned, bring what you have learned here and present it to this old man for inspection.
If even a single phrase does not accord with the truth, you must receive a severe beating before you are done.
You have been bewitched by those old bald monks from all quarters who act like demons; you then say, 'I am a practitioner,' and you strike out with forced rigidity and artificial posturing, as if..."

The countenance of one who has attained the Way: do not apply your mind haphazardly. For ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes, wandering through the cycle of rebirth within the three realms is entirely due to having a mind.

Why is this? When the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise. If you can remain for even a single thought-moment without arising, you will forever be liberated from birth and death, no longer bound by them. When you wish to walk, you walk; when you wish to sit, you sit. Furthermore...
"What is it, worthy one? I see that you all have resolved your minds everywhere to study under that old shaven-headed slave.
You bear the burden of the Buddha-dharma without sparing your own lives or bodies, yet you have all had the eyes of your own sons nailed shut and cut off the life-roots of your sons.
You three or four hundred people are like harlots who say, 'I am the king’s transformation; I establish the Dharma-banner' for the sake of posterity."

People open their eyes; can you save yourself? O worthy one, regarding such talk of "cultivating practice," have you not heard it said that the Old Barbarian (the Buddha) practiced for three great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas—where is he now? After eighty years, when you die, how will you differ from him?
My sons, do not be mad! I urge you: it is better to rest, to go where there is no concern. You...
The mere arising of a single thought is to belong to the family of Māra; you are but a layperson who has broken the precepts.
When you see Deshan appearing in the world, ten out of ten or five out of five all intend to gather together to challenge him with questions, hoping to leave him tongue-tied and speechless.
You are a clumsy fellow! Why do you not come forth now? It would be better for a needle to remain inside its worn-out cloth bag than to stick its head out.
[The Master] said, "Hand! I must ask you the truth; do not err. You, sir, have been running about from house to house, saying, 'I understand Chan, I understand the Way.
You pat your chest and ribs, praising Yang and Zheng. But here, you must vomit it all up before you can be at ease.
Simply let there be no attachment to sound or form externally, and no capacity for knowing or understanding internally. Realize that there is neither ordinary nor sage within. Furthermore...
What is there to learn? Even if you were to master hundreds of thousands of subtle meanings, you would still be nothing more than a "sore-eating ghost," a mere malevolent spirit.
This void of mine cannot be said to exist, yet it is not non-existent;
it cannot be said to be ordinary, yet it is not sacred. It cannot be fixed anywhere; it serves as the teacher of the ten thousand dharmas for you.

I, this old man, dare not slander him. Therefore, the Old Barbarian spat out so much expedient dregs to teach you how to go about with no concerns and not to seek outwardly. Yet you still refuse to comply;
you wish instead to gather superior phrases and store them in your breast to craft eloquent speech, seeking to achieve your ends with your tongue while wearing a fine robe over your coarse skirt.

People know me as a Chan master; they seek a way for me to emerge. If you hold such a view, you will one day be beaten on the back of your ghostly buttocks and cast into the Hell of the Plucked Tongue.

Everywhere you go, you seek people to say, "I am a disciple of the Patriarch," yet when questioned about the fundamental matter, your mouth becomes like a wooden stump, and you instead speak of Bodhi to them.

To cite extensively from the teachings of the Tripiṭaka regarding nirvāṇa, *tathatā*, and liberation as being "Chan" or "the Way," while deceiving the common folk—what possible connection has that to the truth?
Such talk slanders my ancestors. Old Hanshan De’s way of seeing it was not like this:
here there is no Buddha, there is no Dharma; Bodhidharma is an old barbarian, and the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages are dung-carriers.
The two types of awakening—the equal and the wondrous—are for ordinary people who break the precepts. Bodhi and nirvana are tethering stakes for donkeys.

The twelve divisions of the teachings are registers of ghosts and spirits, or paper used for wiping the pus from a sore. The four fruits, the three stages of worthiness, the initial mind, and the ten stages are ghosts guarding ancient tombs;
they cannot save even themselves. The Buddha is an old barbarian’s dung-stake. O worthy one, do not mistakenly allow your own body to be smeared with this filth.
Wearing clothes made of warts—what kind of business is this? Having eaten your fill, you speak of True Suchness and Nirvana; is there still blood beneath your skin?
You must be a true man before you can succeed. Do not crave the "saintly"—"saint" is but an empty name.

If, throughout the three realms and the ten directions of the world, there were even a single speck of dust or a single dharma to be grasped, you would seize it, give rise to interpretations regarding it, and cherish it as precious.

As for those who are grave, they have all fallen into the ranks of celestial Māras and external paths; these are those who have attained through study, yet are like spirits clinging to grass and trees or wild foxes.
My children, in this place of mine, there is not a single dharma to provide you with an intellectual understanding.
I myself do not understand Zen; I am no spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra). I understand nothing at all; I am simply a man who defecates.
Defecating, urinating, begging for food, and begging for clothes—what else is there to do? Old man Deshan, I urge you:
it would be better to go about with nothing at all; rest early and do not act like a madman.

Every person carries a corpse upon their shoulders as they wander about, everywhere swallowing the spittle from the mouths of old bald slaves. Then you say, "I am one who has entered the third [vehicle]..."
Obscured in their cultivation, they accumulate practices to nurture the "sacred embryo" with the wish to attain the fruit of Buddhahood.

When the old man Deshan sees such people as these, it is like a poisoned arrow piercing his heart or flower-needles disorienting his eyes; they betray their ancestors and bring disgrace upon our school.
They claim to me, "I am a renunciant," yet they squander the offerings of the donors of the ten directions in such a way that even water cannot wash them clean.
Do not presume to travel upon the lands of other kingdoms. If your parents do not receive sweet delicacies from you, how can you say there is no fault?
Do not misapply your mind; there will come a day when King Yama demands the price for your straw sandals.
He will pierce your nostrils and pin you to a stake to repay your past debts. Do not say that this old man has not told you; it is very much as you yourselves have done.
If you have the merit to encounter Deshan appearing in this world, he will untie your ropes for you, remove your headstall, and take off your yoke.
You shall become a true person; the three realms and six paths will be unable to constrain you. There is no other method besides this.
This is a magnificent, unobstructed, and sovereign void; it is not something you can adorn or construct.
From the Buddhas down to the Patriarchs, all have transmitted this Dharma and thereby attained liberation. The entire Great Canon of Teachings is merely its systematic arrangement.
You people of the present day, my sons, do not seek it elsewhere—even when the little blue-eyed barbarian monk Bodhidharma arrived.
Coming here, it is simply to teach you to be without affairs, to teach you not to engage in contrived activity. Put on your clothes, eat your food, defecate, urinate;
furthermore, there is no birth-and-death to be feared, nor is there any nirvana to be attained, nor any bodhi to be realized.
I am merely an ordinary person with nothing to do. First of all, do not fold your hands and pose as a Chan master, seeking a way to make a name for yourself.
With clever words, you bewitch the young, desiring that others call you an "Elder. Yet, in your own true nature, there is no connection whatsoever.
In vain, your consciousness runs wild, ceaselessly fabricating strange and monstrous things day and night, praising Yang and praising [others].
Zheng: "I am a follower of the Great Master Mazu from Jiangxi. The old fellow Deshan is not one of your own crew.
I saw that Master Shitou did not know good from bad, which is why the old fellow reviled him.
My sons, you must simply not become attached to sounds and forms, names and phrases, objects and conditions, mental mechanisms and principles, good and evil, or ordinary and holy beings."
Abandon all thoughts of grasping at objects, whether pure or defiled, bright or dark, existent or non-existent. Only when you can remain thus within this state are you truly a person of no affairs.
Even the Buddhas are not like you; even the Patriarchs are not like you. O worthy one, do not run about and tread upon your own feet until they become broad!
There is no other Chan or Way to be learned. If there were something to be learned, it would be nothing more than a second head or a third neck.
In your view of the Way, there is likewise no supernatural power (*abhijñā*) or miraculous manifestation to be found. You claim that supernatural power constitutes sainthood;
yet the devas, nāgas, spirits, the five-fold transcendent immortals (*pañcābhijña-ṛṣi*), non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*), and asuras also possess supernatural powers—should they not then all be Buddhas?

To dwell alone on a solitary peak, to eat but one meal at dawn, to sit perpetually without lying down, and to perform prostrations and recitations during the six periods of the day while doubting the cycle of birth and death—this is the "Old Barbarian."

Some say: "All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they are of the nature of arising and ceasing. If it is said that one attains this by entering meditative absorption (*dhyāna*), concentrating the spirit, and practicing tranquil contemplation, then the Nirgranthas and other teachers among the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*) also enter and attain the great concentration of eighty thousand *kalpas*. Are they not, then, Buddhas?
Know well that these are but evil views and malevolent spirits. O Benevolent One, the Old Barbarian is not a sage; the Buddha is but an old barbarian’s dung-stick.

For now, I wish for you to discern the good from the bad; do not cling to the notions of self and other, lest you be bound and submerged by the various "sage-sticks," the "bodhi-stick," and the wondrous meanings of the sublime terminology of liberation. Why is this? Because a single moment of deluded mind...
Exhaustion is precisely the continuity of birth and death. O worthy one, time does not wait for man; do not let the days pass by in negligence. Time is to be cherished.
This old man does not expect you, a rustic slave, to carry this burden. If you are willing, then believe and take it up;
if you are unwilling, every person has their own bowl of excrement to carry away—this old man does not seek it from you. There are many such elders throughout all quarters.
"Tunuo takes a certain place and speaks of Chan and the Way; you must go quickly to learn from him and copy his teachings.
In this place of mine, I ultimately have not a single dharma to give to you all. You gentlemen, go ask him and learn from him so that you may gain understanding.
This old man cannot enter the Hell of Plucking Out Tongues. If I were to show even a speck of dust or a single dharma to people and say that it exists—"
The Buddha has taught that there are dharmas and a triple world from which one may escape; these are all merely wild fox spirits and enchantments. You worthy ones, do you wish to recognize them?
They are simply empty space, wherein not even a speck of dust can be found. Everywhere is pure, luminous, and penetratingly clear;
inside and out are translucent, without affairs, without dependence, and without a place to rest. What business is there? This old man, since...
From birth until death, you are merely an old bhikṣu. Although born within the triple world, you remain unstained by defilement.
If you wish to attain liberation, where can you go? Even if there were a place to go, it would still be a cage, and Māra would find his opportunity.
O worthy one, do not employ the body or mind; there is nothing to be attained. You simply must not employ them at all times. Other sounds and forms will then naturally respond accordingly.
The path previously traversed is suddenly cast aside; one is instantly freed from fetters and shackles, forever departing from the veils and entanglements.
When not a single thought arises, the past and future limits are severed. Without thinking, without recollecting, there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind.
O worthy one, how do you intend to open your mouth? You possess much knowledge and understanding, but have you ever recognized his true face? Even for those who have left the household life...
When a Bodhisattva of the tenth stage reaches the fulfillment of the mind, they seek the traces of others but find no attachment.
For this reason, the various devas rejoice, the earth deities support their feet, the Buddhas of the ten directions offer praise, and the Mara King weeps. Why is this?
Because this space is so vividly alive—it has no roots and no place of dwelling. If one arrives at this point, the moment the eye-sockets stir, one is immediately submerged.
Sheshan said: "O benevolent one, do not seek the Buddha; the Buddha is a great murderous thief. How many people has he deceived into falling into the pit of the demon of lust?
Do not seek Mañjuśrī or Samantabhadra; they are but country slaves. What a pity for this truly majestic man!"
Having consumed another's toxic medicine, you intend to put on the face of a Chan master;
seeing spirits and ghosts, you will later go mad and run about to other houses seeking a sorceress to cast divinations with clay figurines.

Then some ignorant, old, bald slave will immediately provide a divination for you, telling you to bow to the ghost of the Patriarchs, the ghost of the Buddha, and the ghosts of Bodhi and Nirvana. This is no small harlot!
He understood. He then asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
That old bald monk immediately struck the meditation seat to create a dramatic effect, raised his whisk, and said, "Fine weather, fine rain, fine lanterns.

He skillfully composed words and forcefully created complications, speaking of mysterious paths and bird-tracks; he extended his hand as if to grasp something, speaking in such a manner as if placing a precious vessel inside [a box].
It is impure. It is like using human excrement to make sandalwood incense. O worthy one, since he is a man and I am likewise a man, with whom should I be timid?
All day long, you go to the mouths and beaks of various old, bald slaves from all quarters; having received their snot and spittle, you swallow it.
Lacking shame and lacking remorse! Alas, alas! You have driven yourself mad. Cause and effect are distinct and clear:
the water-buffalo plows and drags the harrow with its eyes bulging out, yet it lacks the strength to pull. A great club strikes your back; you have plundered the Buddha’s robes and food.

They say, "I have practiced the Way. Yet, if they do not understand the Great Principle, even if you were to pass through the Buddha’s belly, you would still be nothing more than a functional piece of excrement.
Having never encountered a true person, they immediately recognize the flickering shadows at the gates of the six sense faculties;
they speak from their mouths of proclamations, hidden words, and wondrous phrases, all of which are gaudy and sharp. How can this compete [with the truth]?
It is not for you to have a share in this, O worthy one. This is the spittle of others. Furthermore, there is another group, three or two together, huddling their heads to deliberate:
"Where can we find a place free from affairs to pass the winter and summer? Let us quickly discuss Zen and the Way;
let us possess knowledge and understanding, and comprehend the principles. Worthy one, you all hold such views merely to seek personal advantage. How could it be so?
This is the way of things. The day you enter hell is near. Do not say I did not tell you, my sons:

wherever you go, you will not be able to choose even a single stalk of vegetables, nor carry away even a single bundle of firewood. When your merit is exhausted in a single morning, you will simply have to eat grass.

You have consumed offerings in vain and falsely claimed to be a student of the Way, further assuming the guise of a Zen master; this has been of no benefit to others, and as for your own lot, it is already lost.

At that time, as he walked along his path, his mind was constantly attached to external objects. When seeing people, he desired only to act with seductive charm, wagging his tail and speaking of the east while pointing toward the west;
indeed, neither his eyes nor his mouth revealed anything of the truth. He sought only to use similar words to test and probe the depths of understanding.
How does this old man differ from you all? Gentlemen, do not seek momentary gratification for the sake of a fleeting glance;
you will consume his poisonous medicine. Like lustful women who do not observe the precepts, these blind shaven-headed slaves—monks like stray sheep—lead others astray into hell.
O worthy ones, do not casually consult your manuals, seeking out phrases and meanings to find victory or defeat.
Passing it from one to another, mouth to mouth—when will this ever cease? This old man’s exhortation is no evil matter;
you must truly bring your own eyes with you to distinguish the clear from the turbid, to discern what is the Buddha’s word and what is the Mara’s word. Do not allow yourself to be deluded by others.
Therefore, all these superior names and phrases are merely the skillful means established by the Old Barbarian for a time. You must truly cease and rest; do not rely on any single thing.
To grasp at the words of others and form interpretations based on them; to discriminate between the intimate and the distant, the superficial and the deceptive;
and to memorize the idle chatter and long-winded talk of others—all these are merely *anumāna* (inferential cognition).

O Benevolent One, this old man fears only that you, my sons, will fall into pits and ditches, perform deeds of meager merit, and—having lost your integrity through mere cleverness—be satisfied with little. You stand still in a quiet place and refuse to advance, thereby deluding yourselves.

All objects run about in confusion as others wander through the myriad dharmas; this is because they do not believe that empty space is fundamentally without affairs, and thus they cannot increase or decrease anything else.
You people are like old crows: though your bodies are in empty space, your minds are on piles of dung, seeking only to eat dead things.
My sons, do not say that this old man of Daoshan has never entered a monastic community to study.
[He] measured [him]. He shouted loudly, reviling him, saying: "You have no human feeling and do not fear karma!
It is only because my sons do not maintain their proper station, racing about in all directions and frequenting the doors of others, like female ghosts transmitting words and messages.

They interpret things according to their own whims, never forgetting their mental traces. They themselves remain unestablished, constantly carrying corpses, bearing shackles and fetters for five hundred and one thousand li."
He came before Deshan and stood there with his eyes wide open, as if he were in debt to him regarding the Way of Chan.
"Master, you must speak for me; instruct me! The old man [Deshan] manifested his total functioning with a great staff. Like armor against the insults of a rustic, it was like facing a thief;
yet this fellow with a face like a dung-hole did not recognize good from evil. When he reached this point, it was just like meeting a man from Lizhou who was cooking fish.
"A bowl of thick stew for one meal—this is merely to help you lay down your heavy burden and cast off your shackles, so that you may become a good person.
Are you willing? If you are willing, then stay; if you are not willing, feel free to depart as you please. Take care."
The National Teacher called to his attendant three times; the attendant responded three times. The National Teacher said, "I thought it was I who had failed you;
who would have known that it was you who had failed me?"
Miaoxi said, "Does the National Teacher see the attendant? Does the attendant see the National Teacher?
Master Xuedou addressed the assembly, saying, "A needle in a sack—if it does not poke its head out, it is a skilled hand. "Everyone, Xuedou’s needle-head has poked out!
Is there any guest-monk here who does not agree with this from the sidelines? After a long silence, he said:
Once everyone had thus shrunk their heads, let us listen as the various quarters conduct their investigations and reprimands. One day he asked a monk, "Have you bathed yet?
The monk replied, "I shall not bathe for the rest of my life. He said, "If you do not bathe, what are you aiming for? The monk said, "Today I have been exposed by the Master.
He said, "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor."
Master Linji addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who study the Buddha-dharma today must first seek a genuine understanding.
If you attain a genuine understanding, you will remain unstained by birth and death, and you will have freedom in going and staying. You need not seek excellence;

excellence will arrive of its own accord. You practitioners of the Way, it is just as with the former worthies of old, all of whom possessed a path for transcending the ordinary—just as this mountain monk does."
As for pointing out the place where one abides: as long as you are not deluded by others, when you need to act, act—do not hesitate.
Why is it that students today do not attain realization? The sickness lies in a lack of self-confidence.

If you cannot trust yourself, you will immediately be driven in a frantic rush to pursue all external objects; thus, you will be turned around and changed by those myriad circumstances, losing your freedom.
If you can bring to rest this mind that incessantly pursues and seeks, you will be no different from the Patriarchs and Buddhas. Do you wish to recognize the Patriarchs and Buddhas?
It is simply this person before you who is listening to the Dharma. If a student lacks faith, they will pursue outwardly;
even if they should find something through such pursuit, it will all be mere words, names, and forms, and they will never attain the living meaning of the Patriarchs. At such a time—

It is not encountered. For ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes, one transmigrates through the three realms, pursuing objects of likes and dislikes, and is born from within the bellies of donkeys and oxen.
O practitioners of the Way! According to my own view, it is no different from that of Śākyamuni. What is lacking in the manifold uses of our daily lives?
The divine light of the six paths has never ceased. If you can see it thus, that is it.
“O Great Virtue, you have been born as one who has no worldly affairs. The three realms offer no peace; they are like a burning house. This is not a place for you to dwell for long.
The demon of impermanence, in a single kṣaṇa, makes no distinction between noble and base, old and young.
If you wish to be no different from the patriarchs and Buddhas, simply do not seek outside. The light of the pure mind in a single thought-moment is the Dharma-body Buddha within your own house.”
The light of the mind of non-discrimination in a single thought-moment is the Sambhogakāya Buddha within your own house.

The light of the mind of non-distinction in a single thought-moment is the Nirmāṇakāya Buddha within your own house. These three bodies are the very person listening to the Dharma right now before you.
It is simply because you do not seek outwardly that these functions exist. According to the masters of the sūtras and śāstras, they take these three [bodies] as...
To regard this as the ultimate is not how I, this mountain monk, see it. These three kinds of bodies are merely conventional designations;

they are also the three kinds of supports. As the ancients said: "The body is established based on its meaning, while the land is discussed according to its substance. Thus, there is the Dharma-nature body and the Dharma-nature land.
"Venerable sir, you know well that these are but shadows; recognize them for what they are. The person who plays with the shadows is the fundamental source of all Buddhas.
Every place is the dwelling where the followers of the Way return. It is not your physical body of the four great elements that understands how to preach or listen to the Dharma;
it is not your spleen, stomach, liver, or gallbladder that understands how to preach or listen to the Dharma; nor is it empty space that understands how to preach or listen to the Dharma."
What is this that explains the Dharma and hears the Dharma? It is this very thing, vividly present before you—a single, solitary clarity.
This is what explains the Dharma and hears the Dharma. If you can see it thus, you are no different from the patriarchs and Buddhas.
Simply do not let it be interrupted at any time; it is everywhere before your eyes. It is only because emotions arise that wisdom is obstructed, and because thoughts shift that it is transformed.

Their natures are distinct; this is why they transmigrate through the three realms and undergo all manner of suffering. From the perspective of this mountain monk, there is nothing that is not profoundly deep and nothing that is not liberated.

O practitioners of the Way, the Dharma of the mind has no form yet pervades the ten directions. When it is in the eyes, it is called seeing; when in the ears, it is called hearing; when in the nose, it smells fragrances;
when in the mouth, it engages in discourse; when in the hands, it grasps and holds; when in the feet, it moves and runs. This is its fundamental nature.

This is one essence; when it is divided into six, they harmonize into a single mind. Since there is no liberation in accordance with any particular place, where does the mountain monk’s intention lie in speaking thus?
It is simply because the mind that rushes and seeks everywhere cannot rest, and thus you pursue the idle realms and conditions of the ancients.
You followers of the Way, adopt the mountain monk’s view: sit and cut off the heads of the Reward-Bodies and Transformation-Bodies Buddhas, and the ten stages will be fulfilled.
The mind is like a hired laborer; the two types of awakening—the Equal and the Wondrous—carry those bound by shackles and chains;
Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas are like filth in a latrine; and Bodhi and Nirvana are like stakes for tethering donkeys. Why is this so?

It is simply because you practitioners do not realize that the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* are empty; therefore, such obstacles arise. If one were a truly authentic person on the Way, they would never be like this.
One can simply follow conditions to exhaust past karma, letting things take their natural course as one puts on clothes. When it is time to walk, one walks; when it is time to sit, one sits.
Not for a single thought-moment does one harbor a desire for the fruit of Buddhahood. Why is this so? An ancient said:
"If you wish to act by seeking Buddhahood, that Buddha is but a great omen of birth-and-death. Great Virtue, time is precious; do not merely follow the bustling crowds of others.

In studying Chan and the Way, do not mistake the recognition of names and phrases for the truth; in seeking the Buddha, seeking the Patriarchs, or seeking a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), let your mental calculations not err.
O practitioners of the Way! You have but one father and mother; what more is there to seek? Reflect upon this yourself. As the ancients said: "Yajñadatta lost his head.
When the seeking mind comes to rest, there is nothing more to do. Venerable Sir, you must simply be at peace.

"Constantly! Do not act like those who put on a pretense. There is a certain breed of ignorant, shaven-headed soldiers who immediately see gods and ghosts, pointing east and drawing west, predicting fine weather or rain. Such types as these must all repay their debts;
there will come a day when they must swallow hot iron balls before King Yama. When the sons and daughters of good families are possessed by such wild fox spirits and demons..."
As soon as you grasp at something, you immediately become a blind, deformed, and deluded being; the day will come when you must pay the price for your food, O practitioner of the Way!
You must urgently seek the true and correct insight to roam freely throughout the world, so that you may avoid being deluded and disturbed in body and mind by this kind of spirit-demon.
Do not engage in any further contrived activity. It is simply ordinary: the moment you conceive a thought, you have already erred. For now, do not—do not!
To seek the Buddha. "Buddha" is a name and a phrase. Do you still recognize that which is being sought?
The Buddhas and Patriarchs of the three periods and ten directions appeared in the world solely for the sake of seeking the Dharma. Even now, those who study the Way likewise seek only the Dharma.

Only upon attaining the Dharma is one finished; if it is not attained, one will continue as before to transmigrate through the five realms. What is this Dharma? The Dharma is the mind-dharma. This mind-dharma...

Formless and penetrating the ten directions, it is manifest before one’s eyes; yet people’s faith does not reach this far, so they instead cling to names and phrases, seeking its meaning within words and texts.
This is worlds apart from the Buddha-dharma. O practitioners of the Way! When I, this mountain monk, preach the Dharma, what Dharma do I preach?
I preach the Dharma of the Mind-ground. By this, one can enter the pure and the defiled, the mundane and the sacred.
Truly entering the conventional. For now, it is not that you, as true or conventional, ordinary or holy, can bestow names upon all things true, conventional, ordinary, or holy;

when a person of depravity speaks true dharma, the true dharma follows along with their depravity. Elsewhere, it is difficult to see but easy to recognize;

Look at how my late master Yangqi asked the venerable teacher Ciming: "When the secluded birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the chaotic peaks, what is it like?
He replied, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, again, have entered a deep village. [Yangqi] pressed further:
"An official does not allow even a needle to pass; let me ask one more question. The Master struck him with a shout. The student said, "A fine shout!
The Master struck again. The former Master also struck. The Master then struck twice in succession. The former Master then bowed.
"Great assembly, you must know that one who has attained realization and encounters others may meet them on the crossroads of the street, yet remain atop a thousand peaks."
Shaking hands. We have met atop the peaks of a thousand mountains, yet we shake hands here on the crossroads of the street.
Therefore, I, this mountain monk, have often composed a verse: "Where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk, I do not walk.
It is not that I find it difficult to cohabit with others; it is simply that the distinction between the monastic and the lay must be clear. Now, as I depart, I shall explain this.
The mouth of the sack has been opened; it has all been scattered before you at once. Those with eyes, do not mistake this for a fault. Take care.
Master Zhēnrú of Dàyuì addressed the assembly, saying: "An ancient Buddha said: 'In the past, at Vārāṇasī, he turned the Wheel of the Four Truths.'"
The Wheel of Dharma. Having fallen into a pit or a ditch, you now turn the most wondrous, unsurpassed Great Wheel of Dharma—adding mud upon soil.
Is there anyone present who, without climbing the steps, can transcend directly beyond the mundane world? After a long silence, he said: "Look out from beyond the heavens;
who is that person within? A monk asked: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas. For what purpose...
"What prevents one from attaining the Buddha-way? He replied, "It kills people with suffering. He asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch?
He replied, "The hairs on his body stood on end. He asked, "What was it like after he saw him? He replied, "Sweat broke out on his forehead."
Master Huanglong Nan addressed the assembly, saying: "Where people dwell, I do not dwell; where people walk, I do not walk.
If you clearly understand this principle of luminous clarity, you must realize that your whole body enters a fire pit.
He drew a line with his whisk and said: "Stinking smoke billows and red flames blaze fiercely; those whose eyes are not yet clear are all within it. From—
The sages of antiquity were none other than those who entered the pit of birth and death to rescue sentient beings from within the flames of ignorance.
How, then, do you all enter? If one can enter, it may be said that they are not burned by fire nor drowned by water.
If one cannot enter, not only will they be unable to benefit themselves, but they will also be unable to benefit others. Since they cannot...
"Benefiting oneself and others—this shaven head and square robe provide no benefit at all. After a long pause, he summoned the great assembly;
as the assembly raised their heads, he said: "The ox-head comes out; the horse-head returns."
The Dialogue between Vice Minister Yang, Prince Li, and Venerable Tang Ming-song. Question: Amitābha expounds the transformation [of the Dharma] in the Western Land;
Bodhidharma transmits the Mind to the Eastern Soil. When the barbarian arrives, the Han appears; when the water reaches, the channel is formed. The Five Peaks stand majestic and still;
the hundred valleys flow toward the source, vast and boundless. The nature of the single spirit relies on conditions to manifest form. Three...
Zhaozhou asked, "In the midst of existence, upon what do you rely to establish your life? Shishuang Qingzhu said, "The immortal has no wife; the jade maiden has no husband.
Yangshan Huiji said, "A nun shaves her head and will never bear children again. Shishuang said, "The iron ox of Shanfu can roar; the Great Image of Jiazhou recites the *Mahā*.
Liangshan Liaoyuan said, "He leaps sideways to the mountain peak. Shishuang said, "Riding the ox, he does not wear boots. Guanghui Liaoyuan said: [The same as above].
"Advancing the elephant, they turned their spears back. Fenyang Shanzhao said, "Straightening the body, the face is split and broken.
Miaoxi said, "Watching a snow lion playing under the moon.
Question: Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not cross the river; and Sudhana visited fifty-three spiritual friends.
Huiyuan gathered eighteen monks, both black-robed and white-robed. Xuefeng went up to Touzi three times. Zhiyi lectured on the Lotus Sūtra for ninety days.
[The Master] blocked six Chinese men. Was this the howling of a jackal, or was it the roar of a lion?

Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Songyun said: "The water is swift, so the fish move with difficulty; the peak is high, so the birds do not perch. Yangshan said: "The Great Sage of Sizhou. Songyun said: [He is here.]
Yunmen said, "It is like adding another layer of mud upon the earth. Linji said, "It is like covering a gold coin with one's tongue.
Shishuang Qingzhu said, "At midnight, the music of song and dance stirs; who can understand its sound? Guanghui Lia said, "Songs and ballads fill the road, and all look on.
Fenyang Shanzhao said, "The person looking at the mural painting laughs."
Miaoxi said, "The jackal howls; the lion roars.
He asked, "Fengxue presented the seal; Nanyuan transmitted the robe. Master Zhao propagated the teaching in Xihe, and Master Song led his disciples at Binglei.
The principles of the Southern School flourished greatly in the northern lands. Now tell me, from whose grace and power did these two masters receive [their authority]? Song—

Yangshan said: "I do not enter the lotus pond to bathe; I am too lazy to travel to the Snowy Mountains. Fengxue said: "In the Cool and Refreshing Mountains, ten thousand bodhisattvas dwell. Songshan said:
"In the assembly of Vimalakīrti, all the sages have gathered. Linji said: "Carrying dry firewood on one's back, one encounters a wild fire.
Songshan said: "The mouth is the gate of calamity. Guanghui Lian said: "The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black. Fenyang Zhao said: "Heavenly proclamation!"
He pressed his hand against the ground and sighed repeatedly.
Miaoxi said, "A monkey riding on the back of a tortoise.
He asked, "The Trāyastriṃśa Heaven pierces above the sun and moon; the Fourth Dhyāna is free from the calamities of wind and fire; the Three Intersections harness the iron ox."
This carriage: facing you, he holds the seal of the total grasp. A macaque possesses a single-sided ancient mirror; a cat possesses divine light across ten thousand miles.
Who is it that directly accepts this? Songshan said: "In the morning look southeast, in the evening look northwest. Yangshan said:
"The cat and the white ox, however, know there is [something]. Songshan said: "They will rot away like the weeds on a tomb. Linji said: "The moon."
Li Zhi said, "A cooking oil cauldron. Chongyue said, "The waist-belt of a stone man. Guanghui Lian said, "An old straw sandal; Zhou the Diamond Man.
Fenyang Zhao said, "A monk’s robe meets a barbarian tailor once again."
Miaoxi said: "A small emergence meets with a great encounter. He asked:
[The circle with a tail] All Buddhas are entirely within this; to move is to lose one's body and life. To look at it is to have both eyes go blind.
At the moment of deliberation, there are thousands of mountains and ten thousand waters. Even if you understand it directly, you are still sitting inside a charcoal pit.
Dishi said, "There is one who does not begrudge his eyebrows; he has brought a message. Songshan said, "All shattered to pieces.
Yangshan said, "In my whole life, I have never spoken falsely. Songshan said, "One must still say it passes through. Linji said, "A rabbit emerging from its burrow encounters a snare.
Songshan said, "Unimpeded in the east and west, free and at ease in the north and south. Guanghui Liang said, "Holding his staff, he descends into the hells. Fenyang...
Zhaoyun said: "Piercing through mountains and penetrating stone walls, the nostrils are dripping with blood.
Miaoxi said: "One makes it oneself and receives it oneself.
Master Huanglong Xin addressed the assembly, saying: "An echo transmits through an empty valley; at every moment, one hears what has not been heard before. Within form..."
The essence of glue: seen everywhere yet not seen; since seeing is non-seeing, one hears what has never been heard before.

This is called the gate of the inexhaustible treasury samādhi, the gate of the inexhaustible treasury supernormal powers, the gate of the inexhaustible treasury wisdom, and the gate of the inexhaustible treasury liberation.
If one can thus know and see, thus believe and understand, thus cultivate and realize, and thus awaken and enter, [one attains this].
I say that such a person has penetrated the essence of the Buddha’s mind and entered the Buddha’s knowledge and vision (*jñāna-darśana*).
Now, having entered the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, is this the seeing of the seer, or is it the seeing of the seen? If it is the seeing of the seen, then what serves as the seer?
If it is the seeing of the seer, then what serves as the seen? If one creates the dualistic view of seer and seen, neither is the Buddha-vehicle. How so?
This gives birth to the Buddha-vehicle. Therefore, the Tathāgata is not the wisdom; those who possess skillful wisdom must take the Tathāgata as their fundamental principle.

The Patriarchal Teacher is not the wondrousness; those who have attained the wondrousness must take the Patriarchal Teacher as their essential intent. Once the fundamental principles are distinguished, clarity and turbidity reveal themselves naturally.
Once clarity and turbidity are distinguished, essence and function are both complete. Once essence and function are fully realized, one attains great sovereign mastery.

Having attained such mastery, the precious sword of the Spirit Peak is constantly manifest before one; it can kill, and it can also bring life. If you intend to advance, you will lose your body and forfeit your life;
if you intend to retreat, you will fail your own person. Now tell me: what is this single phrase of neither advancing nor retreating?
"How would you say it? After a long silence, he said: "The thousand-year-old pines by the mountain stream gather cranes; the vermilion cassia in the moonlight is the dwelling of the phoenix.
For a thousand years, the Mara-Obstructor and his retinue have followed the Bodhisattva Vajrasama, seeking the place where [phenomena] arise."
He could not find him. Suddenly, one day, he saw him and asked, "Upon what do you rely for your dwelling? For a thousand years, I have sought the place where you arise, but I could not find it.
The Bodhisattva said, "I do not dwell relying on existence; I do not dwell relying on non-existence. I dwell in this manner.
Fayen said, "The Obstructing Demon King did not see that Vajra-Equal One, and so he immediately followed him."
"Suppose, for instance, Vajrasama, do you still see the Mara who obstructs?
Miaoxi said, "Since you cannot find the place where he arises, who is it that has followed him for a thousand years?
Vajrasama replied, "I do not dwell by relying on existence, nor do I dwell by relying on non-existence; thus I dwell."
They dwell together, mutually mocking and deceiving one another. The Eye of the Dharma says: "Let us set aside for a moment that the King-Māra does not see the Vajrasama.
But does the Vajrasama still see the King-Māra? To pass judgment in such a way is like boring a hole and driving in a wedge.
Is there anyone here now who can know the place where Miaoxi arises? (He follows this with a shout: *Du!*).
[The Master] said, "What is this 'sleeping talk'?
The Venerable Zhou of Guangde in Xiangzhou addressed the assembly, saying: "Just now, before the bells and drums had sounded, you venerable seniors should have already known the time.
Why do you come forward here clutching your staff against your chest? This truly causes you, venerable seniors, to be deeply frustrated. Since..."
And so it is. I have scattered sand into the eyes of all you people. The Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the Great Wheel of Dharma upon the nostrils of you venerable seniors.
Look, look! After a long silence, he said: "Winter is practicing the ordinances of spring."
A monk asked Master Taizi Yi of Fenzhou, "What is the realm of Fenyang? He replied, "Clouds and mist gather atop Mount Helu;
the waters of the West River rush toward the vast ocean. "How is it with those within the realm? He replied, "The Prefectural Lord issues his commands;
take care not to offend his majesty. "What is the point of intimacy for a student? He replied, "Sitting upright, contemplate reality."
[The Master said: "Characteristics. What is the place where one turns the body? He replied, "At the head of the street and the tail of the alley.

[The Master asked: "What is the place where one exerts effort? He replied, "A thousand-jin burden swinging at both ends. The monk said, "I have already received the Master’s instruction on these three phrases.
I wonder, is there still something above this? [The Master] said, "There is. [The monk asked: "What is the matter above this? The Master then struck him. Question: "A single song has no..."
"How can the tones be brought into harmony? He replied, "Three times nine is twenty-seven; the whistling of a pipe at the fence.
A monk said, "The notes gong, shang, jue, and zhi have nothing to do with subtlety; the stone man claps his hands and laughs heartily. [The Master] said, "Only those on the same path know."
A monk asked Master Guo of Dacheng in Tangzhou, "What is the matter transmitted from of old? He replied, "A golden platter held out for all to see.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "When the sky is clear, the sun shines.
The monk said, "I do not understand. He replied, "When it rains, mud grows."
Master Dayu Zhi addressed the assembly, saying: "Vertically exhausting the three periods of time, horizontally pervading the ten directions—when picked up, even Śakra is startled;
when put down, even the Earth Deity trembles with fear. What do you call it when neither picked up nor put down? He then said himself:
“Frog. He then addressed the assembly, saying: “The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; the cat and the white ox, however, do know it exists.
He then picked up his whisk and said: “The cat and the white ox are both here, emitting light and shaking the earth.
Why is this so? Because there are two different aspects.”
Miaoxi said, "If Dayu had not spoken those final words, he would have surely had his eyes plucked out by a stray cat or a white ox.
Nevertheless, even so, he still could not avoid the 'scales-weight dipped in vinegar.'"

Master Bazhao addressed the assembly, saying: "Suppose a person is walking along and suddenly encounters a ten-thousand-foot-deep pit ahead, while a wild fire presses from behind and thorny thickets flank both sides.
If he moves forward, he will fall into the pit and tumble over the precipice."
If you retreat backward, wild fires will burn your body; if you turn to the side, you will be obstructed by thorny thickets.
At such a time, how can you escape? If you can escape, you must possess a way to emerge from this state.
If you cannot escape, you are a man who has fallen and died.
Master Linji asked the temple steward, "Where have you been? The steward replied, "I went to the city to sell yellow millet.
Linji drew a line with his staff and said, "Can you sell this too? The steward gave a shout, and Linji struck him.
When the kitchen steward arrived, Linji presented the matter to him. The steward said, "The head of the monastery does not understand the Master's meaning.
Linji asked, "And what about you? The steward bowed. Linji struck him again. Huanglong Nan said: "When the head of the monastery shouted, he should not have let him go.

When the kitchen steward bowed, he should not have let him go either. Linji enforced his command; Guizong let him go. These two [approaches]—one is Linji’s exercise of authority, the other is Guizong’s letting go."
Ten years later, someone exposed the truth.
Nanquan asked the presiding lecturer, "What sutra are you lecturing on? He replied, "The *Sutra of Maitreya’s Descent to Be Born*. Nanquan asked, "When will Maitreya descend to be born?
He replied, "He is currently in the heavenly palace and has not yet come. Nanquan said, "There is no Maitreya in heaven, and there is no Maitreya on earth."
"Maitreya," Dongshan raised this question for Yunju. Yunju said, "There is no Maitreya above the heavens; there is no Maitreya below the earth.
I wonder who gave him his name? When Dongshan was thus questioned, his meditation seat shook violently, and he said, "Master Ying!"
"When I was at Yunyan, I once questioned the old man until the brazier shook. Today, having been questioned by you, my whole body breaks into a sweat.
Ming'an said, "Now, as this old monk raises [the matter], if there is anyone who can ask a question, bring forth one! He then said, "The earth shakes."
Miaoxi said: "It is not that the meditation seat moves, the brazier moves, or the earth moves;
however, as for these three old fellows wanting to see Nanquan, they must wait until Maitreya descends to be born before it can happen.
Suddenly, if a monk were to come forth and say, "There is no Maitreya above in heaven, and there is no Maitreya below on earth," then who would you have descend to be born?
Furthermore, how would you respond? Simply say to him: "This old monk is at fault.
Master Xuedou cited an ancient saying: "One must not let sand enter the eyes; one must not let water enter the ears.
If there were a person who could truly believe this and maintain it, not being deceived by others, what then would the teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs be?
With the sound of the hot bowl clinking, he immediately hung up his alms-bag and broke his staff, ensuring he would be a man of the Way with nothing to do.
Furthermore, an ancient said: "To have Mount Sumeru fit within one's eyes, and the great ocean fit within one's ears—such a person is fit to be discussed by others.
The teachings of the Patriarchs and Buddhas are like a dragon finding water, or a tiger relying on its mountain."
One must nevertheless lift up the alms-bag and carry the staff across the shoulder; this too makes one a man of the Way who has nothing to do. Yet it is further said:
"It is not to be attained in this way, nor is it to be attained in any other way. Only then is there no further connection [to conceptualization].
Among these three men of the Way who have nothing to do, one must choose a single person to be one's teacher.
Miaoxi said, "Among these three men, which one is fit to serve as a messenger? I wish to summon him to wash my feet.
Xuedou acts in this way, while Miaoxi does not act in this way. Suppose a monk were to come forward and say, "I shall gladly accept this formal document," then one could not blame him.

The twenty-seventh patriarch, Prajñātāra, presented the priceless jewel bestowed upon him by King Śrīcandana of South India to Bodhidharma and asked, "This jewel is perfectly round and luminous; is there anything that can equal it?

Bodhidharma replied, "This is but a worldly treasure and cannot be considered supreme. Among all treasures, the Dharma-treasure is supreme. This is but a worldly light and cannot be considered sufficient."
Among all lights, the light of wisdom is supreme. This worldly illumination is not yet sufficient to be considered supreme. Among all forms of clarity, the clarity of the mind is supreme.
This radiance of the jewel cannot illuminate itself; it must rely upon the light of wisdom to discern it.
Once it has been discerned, one knows it is a jewel; once it is known to be a jewel, its preciousness is made manifest. If it is thus manifested...
That treasure does not treasure itself; if one discerns that jewel, the jewel does not discern itself as a jewel.

That the jewel does not discern itself as a jewel means that it must rely upon the jewel of wisdom to discern worldly jewels. That the treasure does not treasure itself means that it must rely upon the treasure of wisdom to illuminate the Dharma-treasure.
"Thus, when a teacher possesses the Way, his treasure immediately manifests; likewise, when sentient beings possess the treasure of the mind of the Way, it is the same.
The Venerable One praised his eloquence and wisdom, and then asked again: "Among all things, what thing is without marks? He replied:
"Among all things, that which does not arise is without marks. He asked again: "Among all things, what thing is the highest? He replied: "Among all things..."
"Among men, I am the greatest. He asked again, "Among all things, what thing is the greatest? [Nanquan] replied, "Among all things, the *dharmatā* (the nature of phenomena) is the greatest.
The Venerable One knew him to be his Dharma heir and subsequently entrusted to him the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. He spoke in verse: "The mind-ground gives birth to all seeds;
Due to conditions, they in turn give rise to principles. When the fruit is full, Bodhi is perfected; When the flower blooms, the world arises."
Miaoxi said, "Your reasoning is excellent. Take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.

Chan Master Yangqi Zhentu addressed the assembly, saying: "The myriad spirits share a single source; this is provisionally named 'Buddha. Though its substance is exhausted and its form dissolves, it does not perish;
though the gold flows away and the ingot disperses, it remains ever-present. In the ocean of nature where there is no wind, the golden ripples surge forth spontaneously; such is the mind."
The spiritual resonance is absolute, its myriad signs illuminating all forms simultaneously. Those who embody this principle traverse as many worlds as grains of sand on the Ganges without speaking;

they accomplish their work through non-action, furthering the profound transformation of the universe. How can one turn one's back on awakening and instead conform to worldly toil, falsely imprisoning oneself within the realms of the five aggregates?
One day, Master Shitou asked Layman Pang, "Since you first met me, how have you conducted yourself in your daily life?
The Layman replied, "If you ask about my daily activities, there is no opening for words at all. Shitou said, "I knew you were like this;
that is why I am asking you now. The Layman then presented a verse: "In daily life there is nothing different; it is only I..."
Spontaneously in harmony; at every turn there is neither grasping nor rejecting. In every place, do not create discord. Who assigns the titles "Red" or "Purple"?
Hills and mountains are free from even a speck of dust. Spiritual powers and wondrous functions—carrying water and hauling firewood. Thus said Shitou.
Master Fahua raised his whisk and addressed the assembly, saying: "One, two, three, four, five—let you enumerate them in whatever inverted order you wish.
As for the pillar and the lantern, when have they ever become Buddhas or patriarchs? Those who do not begrudge their eyebrows will speak directly right now.
A monk asked, "I wonder, what does he say? The Master said, "You have already packed your light gear; your water jar, alms bowl, and woolen robe are all there. The monk said, "Exactly."
"At such a time, how is it? He replied, "The solitary moon is cold at night; a single cloud rises high at dawn. When the monk hesitated, he asked, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Baizhang then composed a verse for him and showed it to him, saying: "Thirty-five or fifty—what need is there to mention them further?
Square and round, changing and adapting, they remove even Buddhas and Patriarchs. Before his name was revealed, I could not take hold of him."
When the Venerable Yuan of Jingshan went to visit Changqing, Changqing asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Mingyuan. Changqing said, "How is it with that which lies beyond?
Mingyuan stepped back two paces. Changqing said, "Why did you step back two paces without cause? Mingyuan was speechless.
Changqing spoke on his behalf, saying, "If you had not stepped back, how could one have known Mingyuan? At this, Mingyuan attained realization. Later...
A monk asked, "When not a single dharma stands before one and application is without deficiency, how is it? Yuan struck the fire with his hand;
the monk attained realization.
The long-nailed Brahmacārin sought to debate with the World-Honored One, saying to him, "I shall debate the principles of the Dharma with the World-Honored One. I...
"If my argument falls into error, I shall cut off my own head. The World-Honored One asked, "What is the tenet of your argument?
Zhi replied, "I take 'not accepting anything' as my tenet. The World-Honored One asked, "Is this view itself accepted? Zhi then brushed his sleeves and departed.
Having traveled halfway, he suddenly realized the truth and said to his disciples, "I must go back to cut off my head and apologize to the World-Honored One. His disciples said:
"Before this assembly of devas and humans, it would have been fortunate to achieve victory. Why then did you behead me?
Zhì said, "I would rather be beheaded before a person of wisdom than achieve victory before one who lacks wisdom. He then sighed, saying, "In both respects, my principles have failed."
If this view is accepted, my position falls into a gross error; if this view is not accepted, my position falls into a subtle error.
No humans, devas, or followers of the two vehicles can know where my meaning falls; only the World-Honored One and the great Bodhisattvas know where my meaning falls.
Returning before the World-Honored One, he said: "My meaning falls into error in both respects; therefore, I shall behead myself to apologize to the World-Honored One."
The Buddha said, "In my Dharma, there is no such thing. You should turn your mind toward the Way.
Thereupon, he and his five hundred followers simultaneously threw themselves before the Buddha, left the household life, and realized arhatship. Master Tiantai Yihuai’s verse says:
If this view were to accept it, it would destroy the family lineage; if this view does not accept it, with whom could one debate? The carrying pole snaps in the middle, falling off at both ends;
within the tip of a single hair, the universe appears.

Dongshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Brothers, as the end of summer retreat approaches and you travel east and west, you must go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass.
He further asked: "But how does one go to such a place where there is not a single blade of grass?
Later, a monk cited this to Shishuang, who said: "As soon as you step out the door, it is already grass."
Miaoxi said: "Have you not heard the saying: 'A single drop of a lion’s milk scatters ten *hu* of donkey’s milk'?

There was a Master Paozhuo (Broken Hearth Fall), whose name and lineage were unknown and whose conduct was unfathomable. He lived in seclusion on Mount Song. In a mountain valley there was a shrine that was extremely efficacious;
beneath its roof stood only a single hearth. Offerings from far and near never ceased, and they slaughtered living beings for the cooking.
One day, Master [Linji] led his attendant monks into a temple. Striking the hearth three times with his staff, he said, "Tsk!
This hearth is merely composed of clay and tiles. From where does the 'saint' come? From where does the 'spirit' arise?

Yet you cook and slaughter living beings here! He struck it another three times, and the hearth collapsed. The Master said, "Broken! Collapsed! A moment later, a man in blue robes appeared, towering...
The deity performed a prostration before the Master. The Master asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am originally the hearth god of this temple.

Having long endured the retribution of my karma, I have now been fortunate enough to hear the Dharma of non-arising from the Chan Master and have attained liberation from this place to be reborn in heaven. I have come specifically to express my gratitude."
The Master said, "This is your own original nature; it is not my forced words. Shen bowed twice and vanished.

The attendant monks asked, "We have long served at your side, yet we have never received any skillful instruction. By what path or principle did the stove-god obtain [liberation] to be reborn in heaven?
The Master said, "I simply told him that he was composed of clay and tiles. From where would a 'saint' come?"
"From where does the numinous spirit arise? There is no other principle for it. The attendant monks stood there reflecting. The Master asked, "Do you understand? They replied, "We do not understand.
The Master said, "Why do you not understand this nature that is inherently possessed? The attendant monks then prostrated themselves.
He said, "It is breaking, it is falling away; it is breaking and it is falling away. At these words, the attendant monks attained simultaneous enlightenment.
Later, Chan Master Yifeng brought this up to National Teacher An, who sighed in admiration, saying, "This man has realized that all things and the self are one and the same."
It may be said that he is like the bright moon suspended in the sky, such that there is nowhere it does not reach.
It is difficult to fathom the pulse of his speech. When Linji asked Xingshan, "What is the white ox on the open ground?
Shan replied, "Hūṃ, hūṃ. Linji said, "Shut your mouth! Shan asked, "What about you, elder brother? Linji said, "You beast! Shan then desisted.
A junior disciple had attended Master Jiashan for a long time. The master sent him away to travel and visit various Chan monasteries.
Later, hearing that the Master’s reputation for gathering assemblies had spread far and wide, the disciple returned to pay his respects and asked, "Master, you possess such extraordinary qualities;
why did you not tell me of them sooner? Jiashan replied, "When you were steaming rice, I was adding the fire; when you were serving the soup, I was ladling it out."
"I am setting down my bowl. Wherein have I failed you? At these words, the junior master attained awakening.
Chan Master Chang went to visit the Sixth Patriarch. The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? What do you seek?
He replied, "I recently went to White Peak Mountain to pay respects to Master Datong. I was shown the principle of seeing one's nature to become a Buddha, yet I have not yet reached a resolution."

With lingering doubt, he prostrated himself and waited for the Master to show compassion and receive him. The Patriarch asked, "What words did he say? Try reciting them to me, and I will provide you with proof.
Chang said, "I arrived there three months ago but have not yet received any instruction. Because of my intense longing for the Dharma, I entered the abbot’s quarters alone to pay my respects.
I pleaded with him, asking, 'What is the original mind and original nature of this person? [The Patriarch] said, "You..."
"Do you see space? He replied, "I see it. He asked, "Do you see that space has any form or characteristics? He replied, "Space is formless; how could it have any characteristics?
He said, "Your own fundamental nature is like space. When you turn back to observe your own nature, you find there is not a single thing that can be seen;
