But if you bite three times or twice and still cannot break through, you will, as before, be cast into the society of the antiquated;
when will there ever be a time for you to emerge? Dongshan, having no other choice, provides this aid for you from the sidelines.

[The Master] said, "Power. When Tiantong Qian asked Heshang, he asked, "Where have you come from, Layman Fulong? [Fulong] said, "I have come from Fulong. [Qian] asked, "Have you been able to subdue the dragon?

[Fulong] said, "I have never subdued this beast. [Qian] said, "Go and drink tea. Furthermore, when Jian Daode asked: *Note: This passage consists of two distinct dialogues concerning the Chan master Tiantong Qian (Tiantong Jue) and his encounters with two lay practitioners, Fulong and Jian Daode.*
The student Zuo Zuo stepped forward and requested, "I ask the Master for the direct point. The Master said, "Here, I simply defecate once and that is all. What is there to be 'direct' about?
Zuo Zuo said, "If you, Master, answer questions in such a manner, you had better buy some more straw sandals and go traveling.
The Master said, "Come closer. Jian came closer. The Master said, "Just as I have answered you like this, where does the fault lie? Jian [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "No match. He then struck him.
Jia Shan addressed the assembly, saying, "Sever the host; do not fall into a secondary view.
Abbot Tong of Beiyuan stepped forth from the crowd and said, "One must know there is a person who does not keep company. Jia Shan said, "That is still a secondary view. Tong overturned [the seat].
Tong overturned the meditation bench. Deshan asked, "Old brother, what do you say? Tong replied, "My tongue would have rotted away before I could speak it to you, Master.
On another day, Tong asked again, "'There is no dharma before the eyes; the meaning lies within the eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment;
it is beyond the reach of ears and eyes. Is this not your own words, Master? Deshan said, "Yes. Tong then overturned [the bench].
Dazhu stood on the ground with his hands folded in *añjali* before the meditation seat. When Shishuang rose and struck him with a staff, Dazhu immediately went down.
Fayan said, "When he overturned the meditation seat, why did he not go down immediately? He had to wait for Shishuang to strike him once more before leaving.
Where does the meaning lie?"
Liaochao the Monk went to visit Yongquan. One day, returning from burning a clearing in the hills, Yongquan asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "I have come from burning a clearing. Yongquan said, "What about the state of affairs after the fire? He replied, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it."
The monk asked Master Hanguan Yunge, "What is the surging waves atop the mountain peak? He replied, "Mañjuśrī is making a commotion.
The monk asked, "What is it like when he is making a commotion? He replied, "I do not display Great Compassion before the trigger."
Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying, "If you raise one, you may not; if you raise two, you are let pass. To take up even one thing is to fall into the second.
Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan. Qianfeng said, "Tomorrow there shall be no communal labor (pusqing)."
Miaoxi said, "Both sides are airing their family’s dirty laundry; fortunately, there were no bystanders.
Master Ciming addressed the assembly, saying, "The Dharma-body has no form, yet it manifests forms according to objects. He then held up his staff and said:
"This here is the staff; which one is the Dharmakāya? Let us set aside this entanglement for now.
The monks' hall and the Buddha hall have entered through the nostrils of all of you. The waters of the four great oceans are upon your heads."
"The Dragon King of the Sea is beneath your fingernails. Do you all perceive him? If you perceive him, then by day you travel three thousand [li] and by night eight hundred;
smoke rises from beneath your feet and fire blazes from atop your heads. If you do not even know this, then when hungry you eat and when weary you sleep.
He struck the meditation staff once.
Master Wushi Guanzhuo often sat alone with his door closed. One day, Xuefeng knocked on the door, and as soon as it was opened, Xuefeng grabbed him and asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage?
Guanzhuo spat at him and said, "You wild fox spirit! He then pushed him out and shut the door again.
Fengyun said, "It simply requires that you recognize your elder brother.
The Venerable Zhen of Shuangling asked Wodu, "Why is it that the tracks of a bodhisattva who possesses no supernatural powers are difficult to find?"
I said, "Only those who share the Way will know. He asked, "Does the Master know? I replied, "I do not know.
He asked, "Why do you not know? I said, "Go away; you do not understand my words."
When Master Daowu was first at a village estate, he heard a shaman playing music for the gods and saying, "The conscious spirit is non-existent.
At these words, the Master suddenly attained awakening. Later, he went to see Master Chang of Guannan, who certified his understanding.

He then traveled to the school of Deshan, where whenever he ascended the hall to instruct his disciples, he would wear a lotus-patterned straw hat, don a monastic robe, and hold a ritual tablet; he would beat drums and blow flutes while chanting, "Lu San! (The Third of Lu).
Lang once said: "The drum of Guannan is struck; the song of Deshan is sung. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
he would simply bow with his fan and say, "Yes. He once asked Guankui, "How is it? Guankui replied, "No-position.
Lang said, "Is it like empty space? Guankui said, "This butcher! Lang said, "If there were a living being to be killed, I would not grow weary."
A monk asked Master Yin of Jingshan, "What is it like when one's breath is stilled like ashes? He replied, "That is still the effortful achievement of people of this age.

The monk asked, "And after that achievement, what then? He replied, "The farmer tills the field but does not sow. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? He replied, "When the grain is ripe, he does not go to the market."
Master Yangqi Hui addressed the assembly, saying: "Snow, snow! Everywhere it shines with brilliant purity.
The Yellow River is frozen and locked, cutting off even the slightest flow; yet within the blazing light of the sun, it must burst asunder. It must burst asunder! Nanda eats thorns upon his head;
from beneath Vajrapāṇi’s feet, blood flows forth. He again addressed the assembly, saying: "Treading upon the steely weight, hard as iron—mute!"
The Master asked, "To whom did you tell your dream? [The boy replied,] "Waves surge to the heavens atop Mount Sumeru; the ocean floor at the bottom of the great sea is scorched by fire.
Venerable Huaihai asked the youth, "Where do you come from? He said, "My mind does not go anywhere. The Master said, "Where do you dwell?
He said, "My mind does not stay anywhere. The Master said, "Are you not settled? He said, "All Buddhas are likewise so. The Master said:
"You are not the Buddhas. He replied, "The Buddhas are also not [the Buddhas]. Dayu Zhi said: "The Patriarch asked one question and the boy gave one answer;
both are deficient in their realization. How do you people of today understand this?"
Miaoxi said: "Even if you were to understand it right now, you would still have to practice for sixty kalpas over three lifetimes.
Yaoshan asked Shitou: "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.

However, I have heard that in the South there is the 'Direct Pointing to the Human Mind to See One's Nature and Attain Buddhahood,' which I truly do not yet comprehend. I humbly hope that the Master will compassionately grant me instruction. Shitou—
Baizhang said, "It cannot be attained by being thus, nor can it be attained by not being thus; it cannot be attained by being both thus and not thus.
How will you do it? Deshan paused for thought. Baizhang said, "Your karmic conditions do not lie here.
There is Master Mazu in Jiangxi; go there, and he will surely explain it for you. Deshan went there and inquired as before. Mazu said, "I..."
"Sometimes I instruct him to raise his eyebrows and blink; sometimes I do not instruct him to raise his eyebrows and blink.
Sometimes my instructing him to raise his eyebrows and blink is correct; sometimes my instructing him to raise his eyebrows and blink is incorrect.
At these words, Xuanshan had an awakening and prostrated himself. Mazu asked, "What principle have you seen? Xuanshan replied, "I, this humble one—"
While [Shishuang] was at Shitou, it was as if a mosquito were perched upon an iron ox. The Patriarch said, "Since you are thus, you should maintain this well.
One day the Patriarch asked, "How have you been lately, my son? Shishuang replied, "The skin and flesh have fallen away entirely; there remains only the true reality.
The Patriarch said, "What you have attained may be called being in harmony with the essence of the mind and spreading it through the four limbs. Since you are already able..."
"So be it," [the master] said. Taking three strips of rattan, he bound them around his belly and departed for a mountain to dwell.

He asked, "What kind of person am I that I dare say I shall dwell on a mountain? The Patriarch said, "It is not so. There has never been one who travels far without dwelling, nor one who dwells long without traveling.
To seek benefit without actually benefiting, or to seek to act without actually acting—this is like trying to cross over without a boat."
"Do not remain here for long. Thereupon, the Mountain (Shitou) paid his respects and took leave to return once more to Shitou.
One day, while he was sitting, Shitou came upon him and asked, "What are you doing here? He replied, "I am doing nothing at all. Shitou said, "If that is so, then you are just sitting idly.
He replied, "If it were idle sitting, then I would be doing something. Shitou asked, "You say you do nothing; what is it that you do not do?"
Mo said, "Even the thousand sages do not recognize it. Tou then offered this verse: "From the beginning we have dwelt together, yet its name is unknown;
Moving along spontaneously, we simply proceed as we are. Even the ancient worthies of the past did not recognize it; How could ordinary people in their haste ever understand it?"
Miaoxi said: "The goods are at their true value; the coins are full mace.
Master Fojian addressed the assembly, saying: "The matters prior to the fifteenth day are like adding flowers upon brocade.
The matters after the fifteenth day are like a single bubble arising from the sea. On the fifteenth day itself, it is much like a one-foot mirror reflecting a thousand [images]."
Regarding the image of Li: although it is true that ultimate emptiness leaves no trace, how can one deny the radiance of the Ocean Seal? Let the incense pillar blossom as it will;
what need is there to speak of the hundred uglinesses on the Buddha’s face? Why is this so? In the end, the frosty night moon falls naturally into the stream before us.
Master Dayu Zhi addressed the assembly, saying: "The *śrāmaṇera* horizontally swallows the vast ocean; the old monk carries Mount Sumeru on his back.
Tell me, how far apart are the *śrāmaṇera* and the old monk? Do you understand? The royal decree is strict: no shoving aside others or seizing the market.
A monk asked, "What is the one phrase by which the Master benefits others? He replied, "Four corners and six sides. [The monk] said, "..."
“What is the essential meaning? [The Master] said, “Eight concavities, nine convexities. “Question: What is the Buddha within the city? [The Master] said, “The stone pillar at the crossroads.
“Question: What is the Way? [The Master] said, “Eight pecks and four bushels. [The student] asked, “What is one who is on the Way? [The Master] said, “Cooking porridge and boiling rice.
“Question: What is the Buddha? [The Master] said, “A hammer split by a saw. [The student] asked, “What is...”
[The Master] said, "The meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West is: by day one burns upon the ground; at night one sleeps upon the ground.

[The student] asked, "The ancients distinguished the field by its sprouts and recognized people by their words. A student has come here to request that the Master distinguish them for us. [The Master] said, "Flowers shine upon the land.

[The student] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [The Master] said, "The weather is cold and the days are short. [The student] said, "It is as if Bodhidharma had not yet come."
"What? he asked. "In the Western Heaven," [the other] replied. "After you have come here, what then? "In the Land of Tang," he replied.
Master Zhenjing addressed the assembly, saying: "A lion does not eat the remains left by a vulture; a swift falcon does not kill a dead hare. Let loose the great dragon of Linji;
pull out Yunmen’s single glance. He then took up his staff and said: "When the dragon moves, the rain arrives."
Regarding the "three types of grass and two kinds of trees":
One day, while Master Guishan was standing in attendance upon Baizhang, Baizhang asked, "Who is there? He replied, "Lingyou.
Baizhang said, "Is there fire in the hearth? Guishan stirred it and said, "There is no fire. Baizhang rose personally, probed deep within, and finding a small amount of fire, held it up.
He pointed it out to him, saying, "This is not fire. Thereupon, Shanguan attained awakening and prostrated in gratitude, explaining his understanding.
Baizhang said, "This was merely a temporary crossroads. As the Sutra says: 'If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season.

When the time and season arrive, it is like suddenly awakening from a dream or suddenly remembering what was forgotten. Only then do you realize that your own property is not obtained from another. Therefore...

The Patriarch said: "Awakening is the same as non-awakening; being without mind, there is also no dharma. This simply means that there is no deluded mind regarding such categories as ordinary or sagely beings.
The fundamental mind and dharma have been complete from the very beginning. Since you are now thus, protect and maintain them well yourself.
Furthermore, one day while attending Baizhang on a mountain excursion, they reached a grove. Baizhang asked, "Has the head cook brought fire with him?"
Shan said, "I am bringing it here. Baizhang asked, "Where is it? Shan then picked up a stalk of firewood, blew on it twice, and handed it to Baizhang.
Baizhang said, "Like a worm gnawing through wood."
Miaoxi said: "If Baizhang had not spoken those later words, he would have been thoroughly deceived by the head cook.
When the Monk of the Boat was parting from his fellow practitioner Daowu, he said to him, 'In the future, if there is a sharp-witted master of the Dharma, bring one here.
Thereupon, he floated a small boat on the Huating River; thus he was known at the time as the 'Boatman'."
Later, when Dao-wu arrived at Jingkou, he encountered Jia-shan ascending the hall. A monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? Shan replied, "The Dharma-body is formless.
The monk asked, "What is the Dharma-eye? Shan replied, "The Dharma-eye is without flaw. Dao-wu could not help but let out a laugh.
Shan then descended from his seat and invited Dao-wu to ask him about it, saying, "My response to the monk’s question just now must surely..."
"There is something incorrect about this, which has caused you, Venerable Elder, to laugh. I hope the Venerable Elder will not withhold his compassion.
I said, "The Master is of one rank with those who have appeared in the world, yet he has no teacher remaining. He went to visit the Boatman Master at Huating. [The Master] asked, "Did you find him?
I replied, "This man has not a single tile to cover his head above, nor a place to plant a staff in the ground below; he has simply changed his mountain."
Fú went directly to Huating. As soon as Chuánzǐ saw him, he asked, "Virtuous One, in what monastery do you reside?
He replied, "If it were like residing, I would not be residing; if it were residing, it would not be like that. He asked, "What is it that is neither like nor unlike?

He replied, "It is not the dharma before one's eyes. He asked, "Where did you learn this? He replied, "It is not something reached by the ears or the eyes. He said, "A single phrase that fits the head..."

"For ten thousand kalpas, you will be tethered to a donkey hitching post. He asked again, "A thousand feet of line hang down; the intent lies in the deep pool. When it is three inches from the hook, why do you not speak?
As Shanshan was about to open his mouth, the boatman struck him with his oar, knocking him into the water.

Just as he climbed back onto the boat, the boatman said, "Speak! Speak! As soon as he was about to open his mouth, the boatman struck him again. At that moment, Jia Shan suddenly attained great enlightenment and nodded his head three times. The boatman—
The Master said: "The thread on the tip of the fishing pole is for you to play with; as long as you do not disturb the clear waves, the meaning is naturally distinct.

Shan then asked: "When the line is cast and the hook is thrown, what is the Master’s intention? He replied: "The thread hangs over the green water; floating, it contains the meaning of both existence and non-existence.

Shan said: "Your words carry the profound yet leave no path; your tongue speaks, yet it does not speak. He replied: "When the waves of the river have been fished out, the golden-scaled fish finally appears."
Yunyan then covered his ears. The boatman said, "So it is, so it is. He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, you must vanish where there is no trace of the body;
do not hide the body where there is no trace. For twenty years at Yaoshan, I have clarified nothing but this matter.
Now that you have attained it, you must not dwell in cities, prefectures, or villages. Go only to the deep..."
"Seek out one or two [successors] by the mattock in the mountains to ensure that the lineage continues without interruption.
Having said this, Jiashan took his leave. As he frequently looked back, the boatman called out, "Dharma-teacher! Dharma-teacher! Jiashan turned his head;
the boatman raised his oar and said, "You thought there was something else. He then capsized the boat and entered the water, passing away.
Master Baiyun Dan addressed the assembly. He cited Yunmen’s verse on Sanping, which says: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing;
what do you call seeing and hearing? There are no further sounds or forms to present to you; what sounds or forms are there for the mouth?
If one understands this point, there is nothing at all; what business is there? Essence and function do not hinder one another, whether they are distinguished or not."
Speech is the essence; the essence is speech. Again, he held up his staff and said, "The staff is the essence; the lantern is the function. Are these distinct or not?
Have you not heard it said that "the wisdom of all wisdoms is pure"? "Great assembly, Yunmen only knows how to copy a beauty’s eyebrows by following the model.
Yuan Tong, however, is not like this: 'This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; there is no other sound or form.'"
Presented to you: The eye is the eye; the ear is the ear. If one understands this point, there is nothing at all; essence and function neither obstruct nor divide.
In four or five hundred lanes of flowering willows and poplars, and two or three thousand pavilions of pipes and strings.

A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "In the boiling cauldron, there is no place for cold. "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? He replied, "Pressing a gourd-bottle to the bottom of the water."
Lu asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Lu said, "The crow flies and the hare runs.
Nan-yuan asked Feng-xue, "How do you deliberate upon a single blow in the South? Xue said, "I deliberate upon it as something extraordinary.
Xue then asked Nan-yuan, "How do you deliberate here? Nan-yuan took up his staff, held it crosswise, and said: [The staff].
"Under the staff, there is no patience with birth; facing the situation, one sees not the teacher.
Miaoxi said, "At that time, Fengxue should have fully spread his sitting cloth and performed three prostrations;
otherwise, he should have overturned the meditation seat. He then looked back at Chongmi and said, "Tell me, was Fengxue's prostration at that time correct?"
"Overturning the meditation seat is it. Chongli said, "The bandits have been utterly defeated—excellent! Miaoxi said, "Look at this blind fellow," and struck him.
Master Fahua went to see Master Dayu Zhi. Dayu asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients seeing peach blossoms?"
"How is it? he asked. [The monk] said, "Crookedness does not conceal the straight. He said, "That one may be set aside for now; as for this one, how is it?
[The monk] said, "Picking up gold on the main street—how could the four neighbors know of it? He said, "Does the Senior Monk know?
[The monk] said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one's sword; if one is no poet, one does not offer a poem. He said, "A master poet! [The monk] said, "A single red thread."
The two men held hands. [The Master] said, "Xuan Sha said, 'It is most true, it is extremely true. But how about this? He replied, "When the sea dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;

when a person dies, their mind remains unknown. [The Master] said, "But that is precisely it. He replied, "The pavilions tower above the clouds; the peaks and ridges layer upon layers of emerald green.
Then he presented a verse: "The phoenix returns and soars away into the Milky Way; On Lingyun’s peach tree, an old crow perches. [The Master] said, "Ancient..."
For now, I shall set aside the meaning of the peach blossoms; they cannot be accompanied by either heaven or the human realm.
Master Zhaozhou addressed the assembly, saying: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire;
the clay Buddha does not pass through water. The true Buddha sits within. Bodhi, nirvana, suchness, and buddha-nature are all but garments worn upon the body."
"Afflictions" are also called *kleśas*. If you do not give rise to them, there are no afflictions. Furthermore, within the ground of the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), where would they be placed?
When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault. You need only investigate the principle and sit thus for twenty or thirty years.

If you do not realize it, cut off the old monk’s head and take it with you! Dream-like illusions and empty flowers are but vain grasping. If the mind does not differ [from its true nature], the myriad..."

The Dharma is one and such; since it cannot be obtained from without, what is the use of further clinging and grasping? It is like a sheep that indiscriminately picks up things and puts them into its mouth.

When I saw Master Yaoshan say, "If someone asks you something, simply tell them to shut their dog’s mouth," I also told them to shut their dog’s mouth. To grasp at a self is defilement; not to grasp at a self is purity.
It is like a hunting dog that knows nothing but the desire to eat; where is the Buddha-dharma in such a state?
Here, though there may be thousands or tens of thousands of people, they are all merely seekers of the Buddha—seeking a single "man of the Way" who can serve as a disciple of the Empty King.
Do not let it be said that the sickness of the mind is the most difficult to cure. This nature existed before the world was formed;
when the world perishes, this nature does not perish. Since you first met this old monk, you have been none other than this very person—the true host.
Why then do you seek it elsewhere? At this very moment, do not turn your head or change your countenance. If...
To turn one's head and change one's brain is to lose it immediately. At that time, a monk asked: "I have heard your teacher say that when the world is destroyed, this nature is not destroyed.
What is this nature? He replied: "The four great elements and the five aggregates. The monk said: "These are still things that can be destroyed.
What is this nature? He replied: "The four great elements and the five aggregates. Fayan said: "One is the same as two."
"Is it destroyed or not? For now, how do you understand this? Try to judge it.
Miaoxi said, "A Heavenly King within a military camp.
Master Zhiren of Daomiao addressed the assembly, saying, "Fenzhou said: 'If you recognize the staff, the matter of traveling on pilgrimage is settled.'"
Having finished, he then took up his staff and said: "This here is the staff; what, then, is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage?
Even if you were to see it right here, in the gate of this patch-robed monk, you would still be nothing more than a novice monk (śrāmaṇera) who has just shaved his head.
If you do not recognize it, then for now go to the villages of three families to cast divination sticks east and west; even if you should suddenly hit upon the right one, it is not certain."
Under the master Zihu, a signboard was erected. Inscribed upon it were these words: "Zihu has a dog.
It takes people’s heads above, takes people’s hearts in the middle, and takes people’s feet below. To hesitate is to lose one's body and life.
A monk asked, "What is Zihu’s dog? The Master said, "Bark! Bark! Two monks from the Linji lineage came to visit him. Just as they—
He lifted the curtain. The Master said, "Look at the dog. The two monks looked back, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters.

He then said to the assembly,

[The Master] said, "You. [The outsider] asked, "Who are you? [The Master] replied, "I. [The outsider] asked, "Who am I? [The Master] replied, "Heaven. Thus they exchanged words back and forth seven times.
The entire assembly of outsiders realized they had been defeated by their own conceit. They reported this to the King, who again sounded the bells and drums to greatly propagate the Buddha-Dharma.
Master Huayao Ying addressed the assembly. Suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "I now guarantee for you that this matter shall never be in vain.

The Great Awakened World-Honored One is one who speaks the truth, who speaks reality, who speaks as it is, who does not speak deceptively, and who does not speak otherwise. He will not deceive you all—do you believe this? *He lets out a shout.*"
Above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to; below, one’s own self is severed. The void and the great earth both emerge from within the mind.
Ten thousand *li* away, in the eighth or ninth month, a single person encounters a northwest wind. Strike! Strike!
Master Dadian was once asked by Master Shitou, "Which of these is your mind? He replied, "The one that perceives speech. Shitou then shouted at him and sent him out.

After ten days had passed, Dadian asked again, "Since the former was not it, apart from this, what else is the mind? Shitou said, "Setting aside your raising of eyebrows and twinkling of eyes, bring forth your mind.
Dadian said, "There is no mind to be found; I will bring it forth. Shitou said, "If there is no mind to be found, what is it that you bring forth? Dadian was struck with realization.
The visitor came forward. Tou said, "So you have a mind; why do you say you have no mind? To say you have no mind is nothing but slander.
At these words, Dadian attained enlightenment. Miaoxi said, "Tell me, what exactly did Dadian realize?"
Master Yai of Baima Mountain was asked by a monk, "What is the pure Dharma-body? He replied, "A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon.
He was further asked, "What is the true eye of Baima? He replied, "Facing south, one looks at the Big Dipper."

Master Baoning Yong addressed the assembly, saying: "The Great Square has no exterior; the Great Circle has no interior. With neither interior nor exterior, saints and ordinary beings gather universally.
Even tiles and pebbles emit light, and Mount Sumeru is pulverized. The immeasurable Dharma gates and hundreds of thousands of samādhis [are all present here]."
Holding up his staff, he said: "It is all right here. Do you understand? *Suru suru siri siri*. He further addressed the assembly, saying: "The True Form has no shape;
it manifests form to reveal its appearance. A thousand wonders and ten thousand transformations are made manifest from this.
When joyful, light radiates from his entire face; when angry, his two eyebrows stand bolt upright. He is neither ordinary nor holy, and may be either right or wrong. Man—"
The gods of Immeasurable Light cannot fathom it. To grasp it directly below is not yet to be called a true man. If he does not turn his head when called, do not mistakenly resent him.
A monk asked Shishuang: "Why is it that within the span of a few feet, one does not behold the Master’s countenance? Shishuang replied: "I say it pervades the entire world."
"It has never been hidden. Later, a monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the meaning of 'It has never been hidden throughout the entire world'? Xuefeng said, "Where is it not Shishuang?
When the monk returned and reported this to Shishuang, Shishuang said, "This old fellow—what kind of desperate hurry is he in?
Xuansha remarked, "The old fellow on the mountainhead has missed it."

Master Yunju Deng addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who attain it do not regard it as trivial; those who see clearly do not despise its application. Those who recognize it do not sigh in lamentation;
those who understand it have no aversion. To descend from heaven results in poverty; to spring forth from the earth results in wealth and honor.
It is easy to emerge from within the gate, but difficult to exit from within the body. To move is to bury oneself ten thousand fathoms deep; to remain still..."
Then sprouts will grow in their proper place. A single word can transcend and stand alone above the times; there is no need for many words. If they are too many, they are useless.
Master Fang of Jiangshan addressed the assembly, saying: "To pierce the clouds, one does not cross the water; to cross the water, one does not pierce the clouds. The universe..."
"Grasping it or not grasping it—empty space permits it to proceed but does not permit it to proceed. Transverse and vertical, just parting and just joining;
using the long to compensate for the short is certainly not non-existent. You people, rice is made from grain—a single phrase that is difficult to speak.
After a long silence, he said: "Private matters shall not be recompensed by official means. A monk asked: "What is 'one speck of dust entering right concentration'?"
[The Master] said: "A snake bites the tail of a rat. [The student] asked: "What is the arising of the samādhi of all sense-objects?
[The Master] said: "A turtle bites a fishing pole. [The student] said: "If that is so, then east and west cannot be distinguished, nor can north and south.

[The Master] said: "A bowl of luminous lamp before the hall; several stalks of green, withered bamboo outside the curtain. [The student] asked: "How was it before the Buddhas had appeared in the world? [The Master] said: [Silence].
The one known as Jiǔwàngzǐ did not recognize [the Master]. [Jiǔwàngzǐ] asked, "What is it like after you have left the world?
He replied, "On the fishing boat, I bestow three blows. Master Dēshān Yuánmíng addressed the assembly, saying: "Only study the living word; do not study the dead word.

If you can gain realization under the living word, for thousands and tens of thousands of kalpas you will forever be free from doubt and stagnation. Every speck of dust is a Buddha-land; every leaf is a Śākyamuni."
"This is a dead word. Raising the eyebrows, blinking the eyes, pointing a finger, or holding up a whisk—these are dead words.
The mountains, rivers, and the great earth, being without further ambiguity—this is a dead word. At that time, a monk asked, "What is a live word? He replied, "A Persian looks up.
The monk said, "If that is so, then it is not mistaken. Yuanming then struck him.
Master Yunmen asked a newly arrived monk, "Master Xuefeng said, 'Open up the road; Bodhidharma is coming.
I ask you, what do you say? The monk replied, "I strike the Master's nostrils. Yunmen said, "The Earth Deity loses his temper."
He gave Mount Sumeru a slap, leaped up to the Brahma Heaven, and crushed the nostrils of Śakra. Why then do you hide yourself within the land of Japan?
The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people. Yunmen said, "When you bump into the old monk's nostrils, what then?
The monk was speechless. Yunmen said, "I know that you are merely someone who parrots the words of others."
This is the kind of thing they do. Miaoxi said: "One load of bewilderment is exchanged for a load of antiquities;
weighed on a scale with no markings, it is handed over to an ignorant lacquer tub. Tell me, what use will this ignorant lacquer tub be? If you..."
If you can utter a phrase that is truly alive and free, I grant that you have personally seen Yunmen.
Master Zhizhe of Kaixian addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dharma and the Teaching are provisional paths; the Buddha and the Patriarchs are merely forced names."
To receive the teachings and transmit the mind is both equally false and illusory; seeking the true and searching for the real only leads to greater discrepancy.
If one takes one's own mind as the ultimate, there will inevitably be other things and other people acting as counteragents. At that time, a monk asked, "What is it then?
He said, "If it were 'it,' there would be 'not-it. The monk asked, "How can one enter? He said, "In what kalpa have you been outside? The monk asked again.
"What is the Buddha? He replied, "Which one do you call a sentient being? He said, "In that case, there is neither Buddha nor sentient being.
He replied, "That very sentient being. [The Master] asked, "What is the ordinary mind? He replied, "Bees, scorpions, wolves, and greed.
He said, "In that case, it is entirely the mind of a sentient being. He replied, "Tell me, which one is the ordinary mind? He said, "I do not understand. He replied, "..."
"You will understand it later. [The student] asked: "By what cause do the four great elements possess form? [Dongshan] said: "Tell me, by what cause does empty space lack any image?
[The student] said: "At this point, I do not understand. [Dongshan] said: "I, too, do not understand. He continued:

"When you say you do not understand and when I say I do not understand—do these two constitute one or two? [The student] said: "I beg the Master's compassion. [Dongshan] said: "When have I ever [known such a thing] morning or evening?"

[The Master] reviled him. [The monk] asked, "What is the Great Way? He replied, "I have no minor paths. [The monk] said, "What is a minor path? He replied, "I do not know there is such a thing as a Great Way.

[The monk] asked, "What is your realization, Master? He replied, "It is not within your realm. [The monk] said, "What is the student's realization? He replied, "How could you take my instructions and claim them as your own?
[The monk] said, "I beg the Master for instruction. He replied: *Note: This passage is from the *Wumenguan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 15, involving Mazu Daoyi and a monk.*
"I have never deceived you throughout these long kalpas.
Master Wuzu Yan addressed the assembly, saying: "Yesterday, when I entered the city, I saw a stage of puppet plays.
Unable to resist, I drew near to watch them. Some appeared dignified and extraordinary; others appeared ugly and repulsive as they moved, turned, walked, and sat."
He saw each of the colors—blue, yellow, red, and white—clearly. When he looked closely, he realized there was actually a person behind the blue cloth curtain.
Unable to restrain his amusement, the mountain monk asked the Chief Secretary his surname. He replied, "Old Monk, if you have seen him, let it be."

[The Master] asked, "What is your surname, O assembly? Because of that one phrase of his, this mountain monk has reached a point where there are no words with which to respond and no principle by which to argue.
Is there anyone who can speak for this mountain monk? "Yesterday you fell at that point; today I pull up the roots here.
He further addressed the assembly, saying: "White Cloud does not know how to speak of Chan. The triple gate opens toward both sides. There was [a pause].
When a person touches the pivot, the two leaves fan eastward and westward. Again, he cited Lingyun’s verse on awakening to the peach blossoms:
"For thirty years I sought a swordsman; / Several times the leaves fell and branches sprouted. / Since seeing the peach blossoms once, / To this very day I have had no more doubt.
Xuansha said, "How perfectly true! How perfectly true! I can truly guarantee it for you, elder brother."
"You have not yet penetrated it. What do you mean by 'truthful' (di-dang)? You must investigate further for thirty more years before you will attain it.
Master Muzhou addressed the assembly, saying: "Have you all found a point of entry?
If you have not found a point of entry, you must find one. If you have found a point of entry, you must never again neglect it hereafter."
"Deceiving me, old monk! he said. He continued, "I have already told you clearly and you still do not understand; how much less could I possibly conceal anything from you?
At that time, a monk came forward and bowed, saying, "I, this person, shall never dare to deceive you, Master.
The Master replied, "You have already deceived me."
Miaoxi said, "Tsk! Have you grasped the entanglement yet?
Master Longya addressed the assembly, saying, "A seeker of the profound must penetrate beyond the patriarchs and Buddhas before they can succeed.
Master Xinfeng said, "The teachings of the patriarchs and Buddhas are like born enemies; only then does one have the capacity for study. If you cannot penetrate them, you will be..."
"The Patriarchs and Buddhas deceive people. The monk then asked, "Do the Patriarchs and Buddhas have a mind that deceives others?

Baizhang said, "Tell me, do rivers and lakes have the intention to obstruct people? He continued, "Although rivers and lakes have no intention to obstruct people, because people of the present age cannot cross them, they become an obstruction to those people. One cannot say that rivers and lakes do not obstruct people. Thus spoke the Patriarch.
Although the Buddha had no intention of deceiving people, because those of his time could not penetrate it, the Patriarchs and Buddhas appeared to deceive them.
One must not say that the Patriarchs and Buddhas did not deceive people; if one can penetrate beyond the Patriarchs and Buddhas, such a person has transcended them.

Only when this is so does one begin to embody the intent of the Patriarchs and Buddhas, at which point one is equal to those of the "upward" lineage. If you have not yet penetrated this, you remain behind.

"If you merely study the Buddhas and seek the patriarchs, then for ten thousand kalpas there will be no time of liberation. The monk then asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by the patriarchs and Buddhas?
He replied, "A seeker must realize it for themselves before it can be attained. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
He replied, "Wait until the stone tortoise learns to speak, and then I shall tell you. The monk said, "The tortoise speaks! He replied, "I shall [tell you] to you..."
"What do you say? [The Master] asked. "What did the ancients obtain that they simply ceased [to speak]? He replied, "It is like a thief entering an empty house.
Master Baoci Yu was asked by a monk, "When the eye and mind meet, what is it like? He replied, "What would I say to you?"
Question: "What is the place of true seeing? He said: "Not separated by even a hair’s breadth. The questioner said: "If that is so, then I see it. He said:
"Nanquan had a most excellent way of going. Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? He said: "Last night at the third watch, it was sent across the river."
Question: "How is it when one employs [the teaching] according to the immediate occasion? He said: "In the land of海东 (Haidong) there is a fruit tree;
at its head is the heart. The monk asked West Chan (Xichan) of Xichuan: "The Buddha was descended from Māyā; I wonder, from whose family are you, Master?
He said: "A red banner planted upon the water. Question: "Of the thirty-six paths, which single path is the most wondrous? He said: [Silence].
"It does not go beyond the first hand. [The Master] asked, "What is it like when it suddenly emerges? He replied, "It is not difficult for the spine to touch the ground.
Upāśaka Fu of Taiyuan was in charge of the bathhouse at Xuefeng. Once, while he was paying his respects to Master Xuansha, who was visiting Xuefeng, [Xuansha asked him about this].
Feng said, "I have a mouse here; it is currently down in the bathhouse. Sha said, "Wait, let me examine it for you, Master.
He went there just as he saw Upādhyāya Fu washing his feet, so he said, "The newly arrived one comes to pay his respects.
Fu said, "We have already met. Sha said, "In what kalpa did we ever meet? Fu said, "Do not nod off to sleep. Sha—
Again, he went to Xuefeng and said, "I have already investigated and resolved this. Xuefeng asked, "How did you investigate it? Shaoyan recounted the previous story.
Xuefeng said, "You have been robbed by a thief."
Miaoxi said, "Another has been thoroughly exposed.
Once, Zhusiying, the Preparedness Official, sent a letter to Zen Master Zhenjing asking: "The Buddha-dharma is most subtle and wondrous;
how should one apply the mind in daily life? How should one investigate it? I hope you will compassionately provide instruction. Zhenjing replied: "The Buddha-dharma is most subtle and wondrous..."
There is no duality; however, as long as one has not yet reached the sublime state, there will be mutual variations in length and brevity.

If one truly reaches the sublime state, then the person who awakens to the mind knows, according to reality, that their own mind is ultimately and fundamentally a Buddha. Thus, they are in accord with reality in their mastery and in their peace and bliss.
It is liberation as it truly is; it is purity as it truly is. In daily life, one employs only one’s own mind.

One grasps what the mind transforms and uses it directly, without questioning whether it is right or wrong. If you attempt to deliberate with the thinking mind, you have already lost it; yet, if you do not direct the mind toward it, it is likewise lost.
Each and every one is naturally true; each and every one is luminous and wondrous. Each and every one is like a lotus flower, unsullied by water; the purity of mind transcends even that.
Thus, because of delusion regarding one's own mind, one becomes a sentient being; because of awakening to one's own mind, one becomes a Buddha.

Sentient beings are themselves Buddhas, and Buddhas are themselves sentient beings; it is only due to delusion and awakening that there is a distinction between "this" and "that. Nowadays, many who study the Way...

They do not believe in their own mind; they do not awaken to their own mind. They fail to attain the luminous and wondrous enjoyment of their own mind, and they fail to attain the peace and liberation of their own mind.
Seeking the path of *dhyāna* outside the mind, they falsely establish what is extraordinary and falsely give rise to grasping and rejecting.

Even if they practice, they fall into the realms of external paths, the *śrāvaka* and *pratyekabuddha* vehicles, or the views of nihilism and quietism. This is what is meant by the fear that practice may fall into the extremes of annihilationism or eternalism.
The pitfall for those with the view of annihilationism (*uccheda-dṛṣṭi*) is that they sever and extinguish the fundamentally wondrous and luminous nature of their own minds,

persistently clinging to emptiness outside the mind and becoming stagnant in meditative stillness. The pitfall for those with the view of eternalism (*śāśvata-dṛṣṭi*) is that they fail to awaken to the emptiness of all phenomena, instead grasping at the various conditioned (*saṃskṛta*) dharmas of the world as being ultimate.
The Venerable Xitang Zang was asked by a layman, "Is there heaven and hell? He replied, "There is. The man asked, "Are there the Triple Gems—the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha?
He replied, "There are. The man posed many further questions, and he answered them all by saying, "There is.
The man then said, "Venerable Sir, in saying this, are you not mistaken? He replied, "Have you ever met a venerable elder? The man said, "I have studied under the Venerable Jingshan."
[The Master] said, "Come forward. He asked, "How did Jingshan speak to you? [The monk] replied, "He said that everything is entirely non-existent.

[The Master] asked, "Do you have a wife? [The monk] replied, "I do. [The Master] asked, "Does the Reverend Jingshan have a wife? [The monk] replied, "He does not. [The Master] said, "It is only because the Reverend Jingshan has none that he can say 'there is nothing'."

Minister Li asked a monk, "What were Master Mazu’s teachings? The monk replied, "The Master sometimes said 'This very mind is Buddha,' and sometimes he said 'Neither mind nor Buddha. Minister Li said, "Both of those are on this side of the barrier.
Li then asked West Hall Master Zang, "What were Master Mazu’s teachings? Zang called out, "Minister! Li responded, "Yes? Zang said:
The drums and horns were sounding.
When Master Xing of Lestam saw Nanquan arrive, he was sitting facing a wall. Nanquan patted Xing on the back. Xing asked, "Who are you?
Nanquan replied, "Puyuan. Xing said, "How is it? Nanquan said, "It is just as usual. Xing said, "Why do you trouble yourself so much?"
Miaoxi said, "I must verify this myself.
Chan Master Niutou Shan’an was a lieutenant general during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty. He habitually hung a water-strainer from his bow and used it for drawing water wherever he traveled.
He repeatedly followed generals on military expeditions and frequently established martial merit. During the Wude era of the Tang dynasty...
At forty years of age, he subsequently requested ordination. He entered Mount Wangong in Shuzhou to become a disciple of Chan Master Baoyue.
Once, while he was in meditative absorption within a valley, the mountain waters surged violently; yet he remained serene and unmoved, and the waters receded of their own accord.
Formerly, there were two men who had served together in the military; hearing that Dao’an was living in seclusion in the mountains, they entered the mountains together to seek him out.
Upon seeing him, they said to Dao’an, “Are you mad, General? Why do you dwell here? He replied, “My madness desires to awaken, while yours has truly begun to manifest.

Those who indulge in lustful sights and lewd sounds, and who covet glory and overstep their station, wander through birth and death—by what means can they escape on their own? The two men [were moved].
Having gained realization, he sighed in admiration and departed. Later, Huiyan entered Mount Niutou and paid his respects to Master Daorong to clarify the Great Matter.
Daorong said to him, "I have received the true instructions of the Great Master; that which I have attained has entirely vanished.

Even if there were a dharma superior to Nirvana, I would say it is like a dream or an illusion. Indeed, a single speck of dust flying can obscure the sky, and a single mustard seed falling can cover it."
"Di, you have now already transcended these views; what more need I say?
When the Sixth Patriarch heard a monk recite the verse by Wōluán, he said: "Wōluán has his skills; he can cut off a hundred thoughts.
Facing objects, his mind does not arise, and Bodhi grows day by day. The Patriarch said, "This verse does not clarify the ground of the mind. If one were to rely upon it..."
To practice [in such a manner] is to further bind oneself. To illustrate this, he spoke a verse: "Wisdom can eliminate all artifice; It does not sever the hundred thoughts.
When encountering objects, mental states arise; How then can Bodhi grow?"

When Master Shushan had a monk complete the construction of his funerary stupa and the monk came to inform him, Shushan asked, "How much money did you give to the craftsmen? The monk replied, "Everything was at the Master's disposal.
Shushan said, "Did you give the craftsmen three coins? Or two coins? Or one coin? If you say..."
"I have come to build a stupa for my kinsman with you. The monk had no reply. At that time, Luoshan was staying in a hermitage on Mount Dayu.
When the monk arrived, Luoshan asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Shushan. Luoshan asked, "What sayings or phrases have been circulating there lately?"
The monk recounted the previous conversation. Luoshan asked, "Has anyone been able to say it yet? The monk replied, "No one has been able to say it.

Luoshan said, "Go back and report this to Shushan. Later, when Daling heard this report, he said, "If you give three coins to the craftsman, Master, you will certainly not receive a stupa in this life. If you give two coins to the craftsman..."
The man said, "The Master and the craftsman must act with one hand. If you give a single coin to the craftsman, it will cause his eyebrows and beard to fall out.

The monk then returned and reported this to Shushan. Upon hearing these words, Shushan prepared his formal robes and prostrated toward Mount Daling, sighing, "I thought there was no one; Mount Daling has an ancient Buddha! He then released [the dog].
A ray of light shot toward this place. He then said to the monk, "Go and tell the one at the Great Ridge: 'It is just like a lotus flower in midwinter.
The monk took these words back and reported them to Luoshan. Luoshan said, "Long ago, the hair of a tortoise was already several zhang long."
Once, there was a monk who went to visit Cuiyan. Finding him away, he went to see the administrative official (shishi).

The official asked, "Have you yet paid your respects to the Master? The monk replied, "No. The official then pointed to a dog and said, "If you wish to see the Master, simply prostrate yourself before this dog.
The monk was speechless. Later, when Cuiyan returned and heard of this, he said, "How could one have avoided being given this?"
The monk remained silent. Yunmen said, "If you wish to examine the teacher, first examine the disciple.
Miaoxi said, "At that time, had I been that monk, I would have prostrated once to the dog."
The eighteenth patriarch, Gayasata, arrived at the kingdom of Yuezhi and saw the nineteenth patriarch, Kumāralata. He asked, "Whose disciples are you?
The patriarch replied, "We are the disciples of the Buddha. Upon hearing the name of the Buddha, his spirit was struck with awe;
he immediately closed the door. After a long while, the patriarch knocked on the door. The other said, "There is no one in this house. The patriarch asked, "Who is it that answers?"
Upon hearing these strange words, he hurriedly opened the door. Fenzhou Shaodai said, "I have simply forgotten.
Master Shushan Ren held a wooden snake in his hand. A monk asked, "What is that in your hand? Shushan raised it and said, "A daughter of the Cao family.
The monk asked, "What is the house style of your monastery? Shushan replied, "A headcloth five inches wide. The monk asked, "How is that so?"
"This is a one-and-a-half-foot head-wrap," he said. "It is called 'taking from within the circle,' yet it cannot be grasped.

He then cited the words of Xiangyan and asked Jingqing, "How do you understand the one who 'accepts the weight' but 'cannot be fully realized'? Jingqing replied, "The whole returns to what accepts the weight.

[Xuedou] said, "What about 'accepting the weight' yet 'not being fully realized'? Jingqing replied, "Within this, there is no path of acceptance. [Xuedou] said, "Only then does it satisfy the sick monk's intention."
When Nanquan Puyuan was at Mount Shao, he met Cuiyun Zun on the mountain slope. Zun asked, "Where does the road to Mount Shao lead?
Puyuan pointed with his finger and said, "O! It goes toward that dark, lush green place.
Zun stepped forward, seized him, and said, "I have long heard of Mount Shao; is it truly like this? Puyuan replied, "It is indeed so. But what business do you have, Reverend?"
[The monk] said, "I intend to pose a question. Will you answer it, Master? The Master said, "I suspect you are not made of *jintaya* (gold-tooth);
how could you know how to draw the bow to shoot Wei-chi? The monk said, "The phoenix soars directly into the misty heavens; who fears the wild sparrow in the woods?

The Master said, "The great drum before the hall is for you to strike as you wish; try to display your family style before an old monk like me. The monk said, "A single phrase transcends a thousand [miles]."
