Minister Li, whose name was Ao, admired the spiritual influence of Yaoshan and entered the mountain specifically to pay his respects, observing the formal etiquette of a guest with solemn dignity.
He went straight to the front of the seat. Nanyue was sitting upright reading a sutra and did not look at him at all.
Li said, "Seeing you in person is not as good as hearing of your reputation," and he brushed his sleeves and departed. Nanyue called out, "Minister! Li turned his head back.
Nanyue said, "How can you value the ears and despise the eyes? Li then bowed; rising, he asked, "What is the Way? Nanyue pointed to the sky and then to the ground.
[Daowu held up] a water jar. Li [Yun] said, "I do not understand. Daowu said, "The clouds are in the azure sky; the water is in the jar. Li then bowed in gratitude and presented a poem, saying:
Refined is my physical form, like that of a crane; Beneath a thousand pine trees, two cases of scripture. I have come to inquire of the Way, with no other business;
The clouds are in the azure sky; the water is in the jar.
Master Zhì of Shǒushān asked Master Niàn: "Regarding the staff of Dēngshān and the shout of Línjì, I do not yet understand their underlying meaning.
Niàn said, "Try to say something about it. Zhì then let out a shout. Niàn raised his staff. Zhì pointed at the staff and said, "Do not act recklessly."
Nian threw down his staff and said, "A person with clear eyes is difficult to deceive. Zhi said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "A three-foot staff and a broken tile bowl.

He asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "The bottom of the bucket has fallen off. He asked, "What were the words and phrases of all the sages of the past? He replied, "Thus have I heard. The monk said, "No."
[The assembly] said, "We believe, receive, and practice [this teaching].
A monk asked Master Baishui of Jiazhou, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? He replied, "The four oceans have no dwelling place."
A single drop moistens heaven and earth. When asked, "What do you discuss along the path of Caoxi? he replied: "In the mountain stream, pines of a thousand years gather cranes;
beneath the moon, fragrant cassias welcome the phoenix."
Miaoxi said, "It is also said that at Caoxi there were no worldly discourses.
National Teacher Yanshou of Gushan addressed the assembly, saying: "If one is truly sharp and perceptive, they will leave as soon as they are touched by it.
As for people like this [who linger], even if they travel a thousand or ten thousand miles, what remedy can there be? Advancing or retreating, they merely accept a state of..."
What? You are like a drunkard; what trace of a monk is there in you? Since this is so, then as for the matter of the Gate of the School—how is it?
Even when you venerable masters reach this point, you must be a true man before you can succeed;
it is not at all easy, brothers. Drumshan does not begrudge his verbal karma in speaking to you all: do not rely on remembering a single word. Furthermore—
Do not employ a single effort; do not blink your eyes; do not exhale your breath. Sit firmly and directly, and you shall immediately succeed. O monks, tell me: what is it that you succeed?
Do you succeed in the Buddha, or in the Dharma? Do you succeed in Zen, or in the Way?
Do you succeed in the matter beyond the Buddha—the phrase after nirvana? If you were to succeed in this phrase, you would commit a great falsehood; it would be called "reaching for the heights."
The mind does not cease. It has no connection whatsoever with his brothers. Regarding the portion of all people, how can one succeed to it?
Everyone is invited to examine and see what it is: is it ordinary or is it sacred? Is it the Dharmakāya Lord Vairocana?
In what place does it reside? In what year and month did it come into being? Is it square, round, wide, narrow, long, short, large, or small?
Try to say so! Is there anything as small as a hair that can cover it? Is there even a gap the size of a speck of dust?
Where do you copy it from? Where do you write it down? O monks, it is thus manifest before you.
How pitiful! Why do you not simply accept it right here and now? Yet you further thrust your head into the tracks of others' words and learn within the consciousness of conceptualization;
what connection can there be between this and the truth? Have you not heard it said that "the mind is the thief and consciousness is the wave"?
To run about in pursuit is never to find rest. If you do not possess the eye yourself and instead rely on others to discern for you, you are merely copying from scrolls and books.

To write it down within the belly of a child—even if one were to swallow all the hundreds of thousands of phrases in the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury at once—it would still be entirely another's work and have nothing to do with oneself;
this too is called relying on learning and supernatural powers. It is like a water jellyfish borrowing a shrimp for eyes.
There is no portion of freedom; it is like a blind person discerning colors. Because one relies on the words of others, one truly cannot discern the true characteristics of color.
If one studies the Sūtras, Vinaya, and Śāstras, there are already others present for that purpose. Therefore, Mount Gu shan usually says:
The Sūtras have Sūtra masters; the Vinaya has Vinaya masters; the Śāstras have Śāstra masters. There are cases and titles; there are sections and volumes.
By day they sit before the window, and by night they rely on lamps and candles; there are those who maintain these traditions through oral transmission.
What about you, Meditation Master? Is there anyone who can speak of this? Come forth and try to say something! At that time, a student asked: "What is the present moment?"
Manifesting his fundamental capacity, he asked, "What do you say? When the monk asked again, the Master shouted him out.
Guo Hu asked the great virtuous ones, "In walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, what ultimately constitutes the Way?
They replied, "The one who knows is it. He said, "It cannot be known by wisdom; it cannot be cognized by consciousness. How can you say 'the one who knows is it'? Another replied:
[Someone] said, "Non-discrimination is it. He replied, "One who is well able to discriminate the characteristics of all phenomena remains unmoved within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*).

How could such a person be 'non-discriminating'? Another said, "The four dhyānas and eight samādhis are it. He replied, "The Buddha-body is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and does not fall into any numerical categories.
How could it reside in the four dhyānas and eight samādhis? At that time, the entire assembly remained speechless.
Miaoxi said, "If you scold me, I allow you to jab at my mouth; if you spit at me, I allow you to splash water.
Yangshan asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "I am from Youzhou. Yangshan said, "Do you ever think of that place? The monk replied, "I think of it constantly.
Yangshan said, "In that place, there are multi-storied pavilions, groves and gardens, and crowds of people and horses. Why do you, on the contrary..."
"Is there still much more to contemplate? The monk had an awakening upon these words and said, "When I reach this point, I do not see anything at all.
Yunmen said, "Your understanding is still within the realm of objects; you are merely at the stage of faith."

"The human position is precisely not it. The monk asked, "Does the Master have no other instruction to give? The Mountain said, "To say there is something else or that there is nothing else is not the way.
According to your current understanding, you have attained only one mystery. Once you have attained the seat and donned the robe, look for yourself hereafter."
Master Panshan addressed the assembly, saying: "The one path leading upward has not been transmitted by the thousand sages;
those who study it exhaust their bodies like a monkey grasping at reflections. Langye Jue said: "The lectures and praises offered above constitute boundless roots of goodness."
When Wuye first arrived at Shitou’s place, he said, "If there is a single word that accords with me, I shall stay; if it does not accord, I shall depart. Shitou sat with his legs crossed.
Wuye was about to leave when Shitou called out, "Dharma Master! Wuye turned his head back. Shitou said, "From birth until death, it is only this very thing.
Why do you turn your head and look around? At these words, Wuye attained great enlightenment; he then snapped his walking staff in two.
Master Yunju You addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who study the Way must attain awakening and clarify the ground of the mind.

If you awaken to the Lord of the Dharma-body, then all the grasses and trees throughout the great earth take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. If you awaken to the Master Vairocana..."
"The world of empty space takes refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. Now tell me, what do you call the Lord of the Dharmakāya?
What do you call the Master Vairocana? Do you wish to understand this directly? Within the eyes, light is emitted and auspicious signs appear; within the ear-cavities, the Great Dharma Wheel turns.
Furthermore, in the summer retreat, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Within the light of formlessness, there is a true person of no station..."
People appear and disappear within the three realms, wandering through the five paths. They do not abandon the ten evil karmas, nor do they fall away from the body of the five aggregates.
They do not eliminate the obstacle of afflictions, nor do they realize the mind of nirvana. They do not loathe those who break the precepts, nor do they revere those who uphold them.
Without passing through winter, they do not exceed summer. Do you all know where they go? After a long silence, he said: "Within the mirage of the ninety-day summer retreat."
The fivefold Dharma-body is perfected.
Two verses on Master Duan looking at the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*: When the mind was sought in seven locations, it was not found; Ānanda was bewildered and failed to have a sudden awakening.
Even if one were to seek until seeing the absence of mind, it would still be like washing a clod of earth in the mud. Regarding the "eight returns":

The teaching has been transmitted for a long time. Since antiquity, various masters have each analyzed and explained it. Even if one were to attain the state where there is neither coming nor returning, it would still be like a shrimp leaping out of a measuring bucket—it cannot escape.
Master Yaoshan asked Yunyan, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Baizhang. Yaoshan said, "What did Baizhang say?"
[The Master] said: "At one time I addressed the assembly, saying: 'I have a single phrase that possesses a hundred flavors.
Guishan said: 'Salty is the flavor of salt; bland is the flavor of blandness; neither salty nor bland is the ordinary flavor.
What is this phrase that possesses a hundred flavors? Yan had no reply. Guishan smiled and said: 'What can you do about birth and death right before your eyes? Yan said: 'Right before my eyes...'"
[Zhaozhou] said, "There is no birth and death. [Dongshan] replied, "For twenty years at Baizhang’s place, you have not removed your worldly airs.
The next day, [Zhaozhou] asked again, "Brother Hai, what further Dharma do you speak? [Dongshan] said, "Sometimes I say: 'Realize it beyond the three phrases; let go beyond the six phrases.'"
Mount [Shan] said, "I am glad you have no connection to it. He asked again, "What further Dharma do you speak?
[Shan] replied, "Sometimes, when I ascend the hall and the assembly has gathered, I strike them down with my staff. Then I call out to the assembly; when they turn their heads, I ask, 'What is this?
Mount [Shan] said, "Why did you not say so earlier? At these words, Yan attained realization.
Miaoxi said, "If you eliminate it, it is not non-existent; yet how can you avoid remaining within the thicket of entanglements?
The Monk Jue of Langye addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you who are spending the summer retreat here with me, I shall point out five kinds of illnesses for you:
first, do not go to a place ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass; second, do not remain alone..."
Sleeping alone on the peak: third, you must not draw a bow or set an arrow; fourth, you must not settle yourself outside of things; fifth, you must not stagnate in life or death. Why?
If there is stagnation in even one place, it is difficult to save oneself; if all five places are unobstructed, only then may one be called a true guide.
If any of you go to various regions and encounter those with clear eyes who are true practitioners, convey this message to them for me.
Rest. It is precious that the ancestral wind not fall into decline. If one were an ordinary person, they would simply need to sleep; why?
To flaunt finery in a land where people go naked—surely you are greatly ignorant of the times. Furthermore, he spoke a verse on the story of the Cypress Tree:
The cypress tree in front of Zhaozhou’s courtyard— No monk can fathom it. The assembly of cloud-and-water monks Are all guests from the ten directions.

Emperor Zhongzong of the Tang dynasty dispatched the inner attendant Xue Jian to deliver an imperial edict, inviting the Sixth Patriarch, saying: "We pray that you, Master, will look upon us with compassion and hasten to the capital.
The Patriarch submitted a memorial declining on the grounds of illness, expressing his wish to remain in the mountain forests until the end of his days.

Xue Jian said, "The virtuous practitioners of Chan in the capital all say that to realize the Way one must practice seated meditation and cultivate concentration. If one can attain liberation without relying on Chan and meditative concentration, such a thing has never been heard of."

"I have heard that you possess this [Dharma]. I do not yet know how the Dharma you preach is. The Patriarch said, "The Way is realized through the mind; how could it depend on sitting? The Sutra says:
'If one perceives the Tathāgata as either sitting or reclining, this is practicing a deviant path. Why? Because he comes from nowhere and goes nowhere.
If there is neither arising nor ceasing, this is the pure dhyāna of the Tathāgata. That all dharmas are empty and still—this is [the true state]."
“The Tathāgata sits in purity. Since there is ultimately nothing to be realized, how could there even be sitting? Jian said, “When I return to the capital, the Sovereign will surely question me.

I pray that you, Venerable Master, will compassionately point out the essential heart of the Way. The Patriarch said, “The Way has neither light nor darkness; light and darkness are merely the meaning of succession and alternation.
Even ‘bright brightness’ is inexhaustible, yet it is also exhaustible. Jian asked, “Light is a metaphor for wisdom; as for darkness—”

How much more so regarding afflictions! If those who cultivate the Way do not use wisdom to illuminate and shatter the afflictions, by what means can they escape the birth and death that has no beginning?
The Patriarch said: "If one uses wisdom to illuminate the afflictions, this is the limited view of the Two Vehicles."
Those of the capacities of the sheep and the deer, as well as those of superior wisdom and great faculties, are not like this at all.
Jian asked, "What is the insight of the Mahāyāna? The Patriarch said, "The nature of clarity and ignorance is non-dual; this non-dual nature is the true nature.

As for the true nature, it does not diminish when dwelling among the foolish and ignorant, nor does it increase when among the worthy and holy; it remains undisturbed even while abiding within afflictions."
Abiding in meditative concentration yet not being quiescent; neither interrupted nor eternal, neither coming nor going; not situated in between nor within or without;
neither arising nor ceasing, its nature and characteristics are suchness (*tathatā*); eternally abiding and unchanging—this is called the Way (*mārga*). Jian said:
The Master said, "Neither arising nor ceasing—how does this differ from the non-Buddhists?

The Patriarch said, "What the non-Buddhists call 'neither arising nor ceasing' involves using cessation to stop arising and using arising to manifest cessation; they claim that although there is cessation, it is not truly ceased, and that although there is arising, it is said to be non-arising.
What I call 'neither arising nor ceasing' is that which is fundamentally without birth and is now likewise without cessation. This is why it differs from the non-Buddhists. If you..."
If you wish to know the essential point of the mind, simply do not deliberate upon any good or evil whatsoever.

You will naturally enter the essence of the pure mind, which is profoundly still and eternally tranquil, yet possesses wondrous functions as vast as the sands of the Ganges. Having received your instruction, I have attained sudden and great enlightenment.
Master Xiangyan delivered this teaching: "It is like a man climbing a tree, with his mouth clutching a branch, his hands not grasping another branch, and his feet not treading upon the trunk.
Suppose someone beneath the tree asks him about the meaning of the Westward Journey. If he does not answer, he violates the questioner’s intent;
if he does answer, he loses his life. At such a moment, what should be done? Thereupon, the Venerable Houtou said:
Once he had climbed the tree, he did not ask. Before climbing the tree, he requested the Master to speak. Yanguan laughed heartily. Xuedou said: "To speak from atop the tree is easy;
to speak beneath the tree is difficult. Even this old monk would climb the tree to bring forth a question."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: The ancient adept devised many expedients; How could there be branches growing upon branches?
It is like a fine horse glimpsing the shadow of the whip; Chasing clods of earth is not the way of a lion’s cub.
Miaoxi said: "To swallow the thorny chestnut and penetrate the diamond ring—look at this kind of talk;
it is like a person from Sizhou seeing the Great Sage."

When Chan Master Yongming Shou had two monks come for an audience, he asked the head monk, "Have you ever been here before? He replied, "I have. He then asked the second senior monk, "Have you been here before?
He replied, "I have not. Shou said, "One has gained; one has lost. A short while later, an attendant asked, "Regarding those two monks just now, I do not know which one lost and which one gained.

Shou said: "Both gained and both lost. The first gained because he was already here; The second lost because he was not yet here. If you wish to understand this matter, Do not seek it within the scriptures."
"Did you ever know those two monks? [The monk] replied, "I never knew them. Shou said, "Those who share the same pit have no different soil. Layuan Nanheshang addressed the assembly, saying:
"Great wisdom appears like folly; great skill seems like clumsiness. Do not think that this is merely the Mid-Autumn festival today;
throughout the eight directions the wind is the same, and across a thousand ponds the moon is one. For thirty years, the reeds have reflected the snow."
To awaken in such a way is for one’s skull to split into a hundred pieces. Again, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The chrysanthemums at the base of the fence are a brilliant yellow;

The wondrous discourse on the meaning of the Western Patriarch rings out clearly. I know not who can understand hearing these words— They are fit to establish the pillars of the School of the Lineage."
Then one sees the Arhat’s whisk manifest great supernatural powers, transforming itself into Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, piercing through the skulls of all people.
If it truly knows their origins, it can be said that within a single breath of inhalation and exhalation, it makes offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
If it does not know, then hand it over to Deshan and Linji to strike it once!
Changqing said, "It would be better to say that an Arhat possesses the three poisons than to say that a Tathāgata has two kinds of speech.
It is not that the Tathāgata has no speech at all; it is simply that he has no 'two kinds' of speech. Baofu asked, "What is the speech of a Tathāgata?
Changqing replied, "How could a deaf person hear it? Baofu said, "I knew you would speak from the second head. Changqing said, [I know].
"What is the speech of the Tathāgata? Fuyun replied, "Go drink tea.
Master Jinfeng Zhi picked up a pillow and said, "Everyone calls this a 'pillow,' yet Jinfeng says it is not.
A monk asked, "In that case, what do you call it, Master? Zhi picked up the pillow. The monk said, "It is [a pillow]."
"If that is so, then one should practice according to it. [Xuedou] asked, "What do you call this? [The monk] said, "A pillow. [Xuedou] said, "It has fallen into the nest of Jinfeng.
When Master Xuansha wished to travel throughout all quarters to seek out spiritual friends, he took his bag and left the mountain pass; as he stepped forward, he struck his foot against something.
Blood flowed from his finger. In his agony, he sighed, saying, "This body does not belong to me; from where does this pain come? He then returned to Xuefeng.
One day, Xuefeng asked, "Which one is the Bhikṣu Bei? He replied, "I would never dare to deceive anyone. On another day, Xuefeng called out to him, "Bhikṣu Bei!
Why do you not go to travel extensively and seek instruction? He replied, "Damo did not come to the Eastern Land; the Second Patriarch did not go to the West."

He traveled to India and studied under Master Huifeng. Furthermore, he read the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra* to clarify the nature of the mind; consequently, his responses to the needs of sentient beings were so swift and nimble that they accorded perfectly with the *Sūtras*.
Master Huifeng sighed and said, "Tuduo Bei is truly a person who has come back for a second birth."
One day the Sixth Patriarch said to his disciples, "I wish to return to Xinzhou; you should quickly prepare our boats.
The disciples asked, "When the Master departs from here, when will he return? The Patriarch replied, "Leaves fall and return to their roots; when one comes, there are no words."
Fayun Xiu said: "Not only was he without a mouth when he came, but he was also without nostrils when he went.
When Zhaozhou heard the śrāmaṇera shout "Assembly dismissed," he said to his attendant, "Tell him to leave. As soon as the attendant told him to leave, [the śrāmaṇera departed].
The śrāmaṇera then said, "I take my leave. The Governor remarked to the monks standing nearby, "The śrāmaṇera has entered the gate; the attendants remain outside.
Master Guanghui Lian asked Master Nian, "When a student reaches the Treasure Mountain but returns empty-handed, what then?
Nian replied, "A torch before every door. At these words, Lian attained great enlightenment and said, "I, this humble one, no longer..."
Yinian said, "I suspect that even the tongues of the old monks of the world [would fail you here]. He asked, "How is it at your place of realization?
Speak and let me see. Lia replied, "It is simply the water-garnet sand on the ground. Yanian said, "You have realized it. Lia then prostrated.
Miaoxi said: "Tell me, do you think that Master Nian would have approved of Guanghui?
If you say he approved, why did he not give him a blow? If you say he did not approve, why did he not give him a blow?
If anyone can provide an answer to this, Miaoxi will give them a blow."
Master Yongguang Zhen addressed the assembly, saying: "If there is even the slightest deviation at the tip of the verbal spear, the home village lies ten thousand miles away.

You must let go completely from the edge of a precipice; only through self-acceptance can you take it up. To revive after death is not something that can deceive the world. As for this extraordinary principle, how could people fail to see it?"

When Chan Master Zhang of Mount Xi was serving as a wood-gatherer at Touzi, during a tea break, Touzi said to him, "The myriad phenomena of the universe are all contained within this single bowl of tea.
Zhang immediately turned the bowl upside down and said, "Where, then, are the myriad phenomena of the universe?
Touzi remarked, "What a pity—that bowl of tea! Later, Zhang went to visit Xuefeng, who asked, "Are you not..."
"Zhang, do you understand? Zhang then made the gesture of a wheel and mallet; Feng approved.
When Master Xiangcheng first visited Master Tong, he asked, "When one is like two, what then? Tong said, "One person deceives you. Xiangcheng then attained realization.
A monk asked, "The bag lacks the thread to tie even an ant; the kitchen lacks the meat to gather even a fly..."
Regarding the time of scattering [the grain]: Cheng said, "If one gives it away daily without seeking it, one thinks of obtaining it from delusion.
Master Mingzhao asked Shushan, "Of the seven cubs born to a tiger, which one has no tail? Shushan replied, "The seventh one has no tail."
While Yaoshan was strolling with Daowu and Yunyan, they saw two trees, one withered and one flourishing.
Yaoshan asked Yunyan, "Which is it? The withered one, or the flourishing one? Yunyan replied, "The flourishing one.
Yaoshan said, "If that is so, then clearly everywhere is radiant and brilliant. He then asked Daowu, who said, "The withered one. Yaoshan remarked, "..."
"If that were so, then everything would certainly become withered and desolate everywhere. After a short while, the novice Gao arrived. The Mountain (Dongshan) asked him again.
Gao said, "That which is withered withers of its own accord; that which flourishes flourishes of its own accord. The Mountain turned back and said to Yunyan and Daowu, "Not so, not so."
When National Teacher Let of Nanyue first visited the Sixth Patriarch, the Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from?

He replied, "From Mount Song. The Patriarch asked, "What kind of thing comes like this? He replied, "It cannot be described as a thing. The Patriarch asked, "Is there still anything to be cultivated or realized?
He replied, "There is nothing that is not to be cultivated or realized; it simply cannot be defiled. The Patriarch said, "Precisely this non-defilement—"
"This is the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas. As you are thus, so am I.
Master Zhimen Zu addressed the assembly, saying: "Xuefeng rolls the ball; Luohan writes characters; Guizong slays the snake."
"The Great Sui burns the slash-and-burn fields. Now tell me, what matter does this clarify? Is there anyone who can clarify it? Try saying something. If you cannot clarify it, therefore it is said:
"To slay a snake, one must have the hand that slays snakes; to burn slash-and-burn fields, one must be the person who burns slash-and-burn fields.
When a flicker of emotional dust arises, deluded views are born. "If there is no sinew in the eye, one is poor for a lifetime. A monk asked: "What is..."
Regarding the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū, it is said: "Words do not echo twice. Question: What is meant by "sitting at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas"?
Answer: "Calamity does not travel alone. Question: What is meant by "the Buddha-dharma does not manifest before one"? Answer: "Though gold dust is precious... Question:
What is meant by "one cannot attain the path of Buddhahood"? Answer: "It cannot be placed within the eye."
Master Puhua usually went into the marketplace shaking a wooden clapper and said: "If it comes from the bright side, I strike the bright side; if it comes from the dark side, I strike the dark side;
if it comes from the four quarters and eight directions, I strike with a whirlwind; if it comes from empty space, I strike with a continuous barrage.
One day, Linji ordered a monk to seize him and asked, "What if it does not come in any of these ways? Puhua pushed him away and said, "Tomorrow."
In the Great Compassion Monastery (Dabei Yuan), there was a monk named Qi. When the monk returned, he related this to Linji. Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow.
Once, when a monk traveling to Mount Tai asked an old woman, "Which way does the path to Mount Tai go?
the woman replied, "Go straight ahead. As soon as the monk had walked three or five paces, the woman said, "What a fine monk! And yet, you act like this..."
"Where have you been? He reported this to the Governor (Zhōu). The Governor said, "Wait; I shall go and examine this old woman for you.

The next day he went there and asked the same question; the old woman answered in the same way. Upon returning, the Governor said to the assembly, "I have thoroughly examined and seen through this old woman of Mount Tai.
Daguī Zhé’s verse says: "The elder of the monastic grove has no peer in the world; His stern majesty..."
The wind blows across four hundred states; a single strike shattered the iron barrier. Such great kindness is difficult to repay even with rain and dew.
National Teacher Yao once had a monk ask Fayan, "What is the single drop of water from Cao’s source? Fayan replied, "It is the single drop of water from Cao’s source.
Upon hearing these words, the Master attained realization. Later, while residing at Lotus Peak, he composed this verse:
It says: "At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this world; outside the mind there is no dharma—before one's eyes are the green mountains.
When Fayen heard this, he said, "With just this single verse, he will naturally continue our school."
Miaoxi said: "The extinction of the Fayan school was solely due to this one verse.

The Sixth Patriarch addressed the assembly, saying: "All you good friends, each of you should purify your minds and listen to my preaching of the Dharma. You...
All such people should realize that their own minds are the Buddha; do not harbor further doubt. There is not a single external thing capable of being established;
all are the original mind giving rise to myriad phenomena. Therefore, a sutra says: "When the mind arises, all phenomena arise; when the mind ceases, all phenomena cease.
If you wish to accomplish the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), you must attain the Samādhi of the Single Characteristic and the Samādhi of the Single Practice. If, regarding...
Not dwelling on the marks of any place, one does not give rise to aversion or affection within those marks, nor is there any grasping or rejecting.
One does not contemplate matters such as benefit, success, or failure; remaining at ease, tranquil, empty, harmonious, and serene—this is called the Samādhi of the Single Mark.

If, in all places—whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—one maintains a purely upright mind without wavering from the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), one truly accomplishes the Pure Land;
this is called the Samādhi of Single Practice. If a person possesses two or three such samādhis, it is like the earth which, having seeds, can contain, nurture, and bring them to fruition;
the single mark and single practice are likewise so. My preaching of the Dharma now is just like the [proper] season.

for in the mere interval of deliberation, one has already fallen into the realm of dust and delusion. It requires the functioning of the person themselves, meeting [the truth] at the moment of encounter.
Sometimes he uses a staff, sometimes a shout; sometimes he raises his fist or brushes away with his sleeve.
This eye of his is like a spark of fire or a flash of lightning. Or he says, "The cypress tree in the courtyard—what else is there?
Zhaozhou speaks directly to people with words that hit the mark: when hungry, eat; when tired, sleep. Every movement and action is entirely [this].
To take this for one's own personal use—such a view is as common as millet or hemp seeds. It belongs entirely to the lineage of celestial demons and the heterodox schools of external paths.
Merely grasping at the discriminations of consciousness and employing the mind to accept or reject, they forcibly fabricate their own views and transmit them from mouth to ear to deceive others.
Driven by a desire for fame and profit, what kind of karma is this? It defiles the ancestral tradition. Why do you not travel to seek the Way elsewhere?

Traversing everywhere in search of a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) to resolve the nature of body and mind, you have become roughly like a monk. Since ancient times, there has naturally been the patriarchal model of our school;
within this Buddha-mind lineage, even Śakra and Brahmā, along with all the devas, fold their hands in respectful faith, while the Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones cannot fathom its source.
Then, raising his whisk, he said: "If you awaken here, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are yours."
[The Master] said, "A fellow practitioner. He then looked to his left and right and said, "How would Daolin dare to suppress the worthy and treat them as lowly?
A monk asked Yunfeng, "Does this steep mountain and rocky cliff possess the Buddha-dharma or not? Yunfeng said, "It does.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of this steep mountain and rocky cliff? He replied, "A monkey climbing a tree upside down."
Miaoxi said, "If a person believes, accepts, and practices this, the task of a lifetime of study will be completed.

Master Jue of Langye addressed the assembly, saying, "I, this mountain monk, while studying the ninth chapter of the *Huayan Jinshizi Zhang*, titled 'The Door of Skillful Accomplishment through the Turning of the Mind,' saw it further explained thus: 'It is like a one-foot mirror that receives layer upon layer of reflections.'"
"An elephant! If it is so, one may attain the Way through existence; one may attain the Way through non-existence; one may attain the Way through what is not; one may attain the Way through what is.
Nevertheless, even though this is so, you must further know that there is a single aperture at the top of the staff.
If you do not understand this, the staff will pass through the lantern and enter the Buddha hall, striking Śākyamuni and knocking over Maitreya, while the pillar claps its hands and laughs."
He laughed loudly. "Tell me, what is it that you laugh at? He struck the ground once with his staff.
National Teacher Shao asked Longya, "Why is it that the majestic and honored one cannot be approached?
Longya said, "It is like fire meeting fire. [Shao] asked, "What if water suddenly encounters it? Longya said, "Dharma teacher, you do not understand. Next, he asked:
Shushan said, "A hundred circumferences and a thousand layers—what kind of realm is this? Sanshan said, "Twisting straw ropes on the left to bind the sons of ghosts.

Jin said, "Since it does not fall within the categories of past or present, I ask the Master to explain. Shushan said, "I will not explain. Jin said, "Why do you not explain? Shushan said, "Within this, existence and non-existence cannot be distinguished."
Master Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "I have no choice but to speak to you all. To say that there is 'nothing' directly before you is already to obscure the truth.
Yet you still wish to step forward, seeking understanding by chasing after words and phrases, raising myriad distinctions and setting forth countless difficulties;
you merely gain a slippery tongue, which only serves to distance you further from the Way."
When does it cease? It is simply this very matter. If it were found within words and language, how could the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings not possess language?

For what reason, then, is it said that "the Way is transmitted separately outside the teachings"? If it were derived from scholarly understanding or intellectual ingenuity, consider even the holy ones of the Ten Stages who preach the Dharma like clouds and rain;
they are still rebuked for their realization of nature as being "like looking through a fine gauze."
By this, one knows that although all who possess a mind are vastly different from heaven and earth, nevertheless, for one who has attained it, the fire of the Way cannot burn their mouth;
though they speak of matters all day long, nothing ever touches their lips or teeth, nor have they uttered a single word.
Though they wear clothes and eat food all day long, they never touch a single grain of rice or hang upon a single thread of silk.
Even so, this is still merely talk from the school gate; one must actually attain such realization before it is truly so.

From the standpoint of the Zen monks' tradition, to present one's insight within the words is but a vain labor of waiting and pondering. Even if one were able to take responsibility for a single phrase, [it would still not suffice].
They are still drowsy fellows. At that time, a monk asked about this one phrase, to which [Zhaozhou] replied, "Lift it up.
Miaoxi said, "A drowsy fellow.
Master Duan Shizi ascended the seat at Huating and said, "The lion of Vulture Peak roars in the clouds; there is no Buddha-dharma to be found."
"Let us deliberate. It would be better to perform a somersault. He then leaped down from his seat.
Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the golden-brocade *kāṣāya* robe that the World-Honored One transmitted, what other Dharma did he transmit?
Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded. Kāśyapa said, "Throw down the banner-pole in front of the gate! Fenyang said:
"How can one know it without asking? Wuzu Ke said, "Exposed. Cuoyan Zhi said, "A thousand-year-old shadowless tree;
a bottomless boot of the present age.
Master Zhenjing addressed the assembly, saying, "Is there anyone who would like to ask a question? After a long silence, he said, "For thirty years I have been playing with..."

A horseman was thrown by a donkey, whereupon he leaned on his knee and said: "It would have to be such that Mount Sumeru trembles, the waters of the sea surge in waves, the Heaven of the Thirty-three simultaneously vacate their thrones, and the eighteen great hells completely cease their bitterness. Do you see?
If you can see it here, Śākyamuni folds his hands and Maitreya frowns; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra serve as his attendants."
If you do not see it, look at me as I move freely in all directions; for now, seek realization within this tangle of vines.

A-he-he! Venerable elders, tell me: what am I laughing at? Alas! I laugh at the firefly-like brilliance and the mosquito-like understanding of the ancients—Yunmen, Linji, Deshan, and Yantou. One of them said, "I revile the Buddhas and scold the Patriarchs."
One person said, "I have attained the final word. Another said, "Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not so much.
A third said, "When the Great Awakened World-Honored One was first born, he pointed one finger to heaven and one finger to earth, declaring, 'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him with a single blow of my staff and fed him to a dog. This is like such a thing.
This band of plunderers who seek the void all merely claim supremacy in places where there is no Buddha.
If they were summoned here today, I would immediately subject them all to a thorough interrogation. As for the rest, it would be unacceptable to let them off.
Have you not heard the monk ask Qianfeng: "The Bhagavans of the ten directions all enter the single path to Nirvana; I wonder where the beginning of that path lies?"
"Where? Gāngfēng held up his staff, drew a line, and said, "It is right here. But as for Gāngfēng acting like this—have you ever even dreamed of it?
If it were I, I would not do so. "The Buddhas of the ten directions / Have but one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa.
I wonder where the beginning of that path lies? [I] would strike him across the spine and then ask him, "Where is the beginning of the path?"
Where? As soon as he was about to open his mouth, [Yunmen] gave a hot shout and drove him out.

Furthermore, there was that old, crippled monk Yunmen, who could not distinguish black from white nor discern the right from the wrong. He held up a fan and said: "Leaping up to the Thirty-three Heavens, he strikes the nostrils of Śakra;
a blow to the carp of the Eastern Sea, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. It is just like this.
"A man who mixes mud with water—what fault is there if ten or five of them are buried in a heap of refuse?
Aha-ha! Is it joyful or not? Is it sufficient or not? Now, fortunately facing the mountains, as green peaks and lush valleys come year after year, let all these matters rest at once.
Trusting in the body and mind, be free from constraint. Everyone, do not be drowsy!"
Master Suīyán Yàn asked Yàntóu, “What is the fundamental, eternal principle? Yàntóu replied, “Movement. Yàn asked, “What is it like when there is movement?
Yàntóu said, “That is not the fundamental, eternal principle. Yàn reflected deeply for a long while. Yàntóu said, “If you accept this, you have not yet escaped the root and dust;
if you do not accept it, you will sink forever into birth and death. Yàn subsequently attained realization. Later, he visited Jiāshān. Jiāshān—
The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from Sleeping Dragon. The Master said, "When you came, had the dragon already risen or not? Yan then looked back at him.
The Master said, "This is like applying moxa to an old burn wound on top of another. Yan said, "Why does the Master trouble himself so much? Thereupon, the Master ceased.
Miaoxi said, "If it were not for shooting the stone tiger at Lan-tian, I might have nearly killed General Li by mistake.
Nan-yuan asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Pu-chan. Nan-yuan said, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered a dung-pestle?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Nan-yuan then struck him.
The Venerable Master Nanzhuo Lohan addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas did not appear in the world; Bodhidharma did not come from the West.
The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox; thus it seals the sky. When the sun and moon sink their radiance and heaven and earth grow dark, it seals the sky.
It seals the water: when the waves contract and the billows surge, fish and dragons lose their lives. It seals the mud: when the waters recede across the great earth, the sage [remains]."
When the road is cut off, if it is this very seal, who would dare even look upon it? Yet, alas, everywhere people are merely copying patterns and drawing outlines.
If it were to fall into the hands of an Arhat, he would surely smash it to pieces.
Zhaoqing Heshang addressed the assembly, saying: "Tonight, Zhaoqing shall speak all at once for you all. Do you understand where it lands?
At that time, a monk came forward and said: "If the entire assembly were to disperse at once, would that accord with your intention, Master?"
He said, "I like to give a staff. The monk bowed. Qingsong said, "Though you have the intent of the blind turtle, you lack the journey of the bright moon.
The monk asked, "What is the journey of the bright moon? He replied, "This is the intent of the blind turtle. He asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa?
He replied, "Not practicing, yet not not practicing. He asked, "What is the meaning of the West? He replied, "A mosquito."
Ascending the Iron Ox:

Master Deshan’s lifelong vocation was the lecturing on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāraṃitā Sūtra*. Later, hearing that the Chan school was flourishing greatly in the South, he could not fathom its origins.

He consequently ceased his lectures, dispersed his disciples, and took his commentaries and sub-commentaries to travel south. Arriving first at Longtan, he had only just stepped across the threshold when—
He then asked, "I have long heard of Dragon Pond. Now that I have arrived, neither the pond nor the dragon is to be seen.
The Pond replied, "You have come personally to Dragon Pond. Baizhang bowed and withdrew. That night, he entered the room and stood in attendance until late;
the Pond said, "Why do you not go out? Baizhang then said, "Goodbye," lifted the curtain and went out. Seeing it was dark outside, he turned back.
He said, "It is dark outside. Baotang then lit a paper candle and handed it to him. Just as Shanshan was about to take it, Baotang blew it out.
At this, Shanshan suddenly attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself. Baotang asked, "What have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
Shanshan replied, "From this day forward, I shall no longer harbor doubts regarding the tongues of the old monks throughout the world. Upon reaching the following... [text continues]
On the day of the Dragon Pond (Rītanyāṅga), Shishuang ascended the hall and said: "There is a man among you whose teeth are like a forest of swords and whose mouth is like a basin of blood;
he would not turn his head even if struck with a staff once. At some time in the future, he will stand atop a solitary peak and propagate my Way.
Shishuang then took the commentaries from before the Dharma Hall, raised up a torch, and said: "Exhaust all profound dialectics..."
He placed a single hair in the vast void and exhausted the pivotal mechanisms of the world, like a drop cast into a great abyss;
he then took his commentaries and sub-commentaries and burned them, whereupon he paid his respects and took his leave.
Deng Yinfeng took his leave of Mazu. Mazu asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to Shitou. Mazu said, "The path at Shitou is slippery.
He replied, "Carrying my staff and wood with me, I shall perform my play wherever the stage appears," and he departed.
As soon as he arrived at Shitou, he circled the meditation seat once, shook his monk’s staff once, and asked, "What is your fundamental teaching? Shitou said, "Heaven! Heaven! Yinfeng was speechless.
He returned and reported this to Mazu. Mazu said, "Go back again. When he says, 'The blue sky! The blue sky! you should then sigh twice.
Feng went back again and followed the previous instructions exactly. When he asked the question, Tou sighed twice; Feng remained speechless once more. Upon his return, he reported this to Mazu.
Mazu said, "I told you that the path of Shitou is slippery."
One night, Zhao Bunan pointed to a crescent moon and asked Elder Puhua, "Where has that other piece gone?
Puhua said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. Zhao replied, "I have lost a piece."
Miaoxi said: "To rise by oneself and to fall by oneself.
When Master Guanghui Lian arrived at Shoushan, Shoushan asked, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From Hanshang.
Shoushan held up his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Hanshang? He replied, "What is this? It is the sound of a clanging bowl. Shoushan said: [This is so].
"Blind! [The monk] said, "Exactly so," gave a single slap, and then departed.
The Monk Long-Zi went to visit Shitou. Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan.
Shitou said, "Has the one set of merit at the head of Mount Dayu been completed yet? He replied, "It has been completed long ago; it simply lacks the dot in the eye."
Shitou said, "Do you not wish to have your eyes opened? Mazu replied, "I request it at once. Shitou lowered one foot, and Mazu immediately prostrated himself.
Shitou asked, "What did you see that you prostrate yourself? Mazu replied, "Like a single drop of snow upon a red-hot furnace."
Yangshan asked Nantuo, "How does this old monk compare to a donkey? He replied, "Even a Buddha does not compare. Yangshan said, "If even a Buddha does not compare, then what does he resemble?
He replied, "If there were anything with which he resembled [the donkey], how would he differ from a donkey? Yangshan approved of this.
Yangqi Huayan asked a monk, "The autumn colors are lingering; where did you depart from this morning? The monk replied, "Last summer I was at Shanglan.
Yangqi said, "How do you speak a phrase that does not involve the journey? The monk said, "A double case. Yangqi said, "Thank you, Venerable, for answering my question.
The monk then gave a shout. Yangqi said, "Where did you learn such empty affectation? The monk said, "To the clear-eyed one..."
Xu Nanman said, "In that case, Yangqi is following you, Venerable. As the monk hesitated, Yangqi said, "I have pity for you, a fellow countryman here;
I let you off thirty blows. He asked, "What is the Buddha? Yangqi replied, "The sound of the staff-blowing at the steps."
When Master Muzhou saw a monk approaching, he said, "This is a case already settled; I grant you thirty blows.
Yunfeng Yue remarked, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive."
Miaoxi said, "I have added one more. Having finished speaking, he asked Chongmi, "Do you think there is any fault in my saying this?
Chongmi replied, "The heart of a thief is naturally fearful. Miaoxi said, "There are three of us [who are guilty]."
Master Daowu Zhen addressed the assembly, saying: "The ancients said, 'To recognize it is as before, yet it is not. This is truly difficult to comprehend.
The soil-dweller has a profusion of beard and whiskers beneath his chin; the Persian has deep-set eyes and large nostrils—how extraordinary!
In a sudden flash, he passes through the borders of Silla. He further addressed the assembly, saying: "The sun and moon of old, the mountains and rivers as they were. If you can understand this...
"Go! The Buddhas of the ten directions share one single path to the gate of Nirvana. If you do not understand this clearly, you will slander this sutra and incur such retribution as this.
Master Jia Shan addressed the assembly, saying: "One does not know by daybreak; awakening does not depend on a teacher. To leap over the Dragon Gate with one's scales intact—"
It has fallen into the hands of a fisherman. Yet, the mind does not dwell on private attachments, and the tongue does not cling to the profound essence (*xuanzhi*).

This is precisely the moment for one who knows the sound; this is called the "congenital dialogue. If you harbor doubt regarding the profound essence, you will surely bring ruin upon yourself, O Master. A weary fish stays in the shallows; a dull bird perches in the reeds.
The wandering clouds and waters are not the Master; the Master is not the wandering clouds and waters. It is I, the old monk, who have attained [this state] within the wandering clouds and waters.
"Master, how about you, Acharya? Master Muzhou addressed the assembly, saying:
"To tear it open is up to me; to fold it back together is also up to me. A monk asked, "What is tearing it open?
He replied: "Three times nine is twenty-seven. Bodhi, Nirvana, Suchness, and Liberation..."
"The mind is itself the Buddha. I speak thus for now; how would you speak? A monk said, "I do not speak in this way.
[The Master] said, "When the cup falls to the ground, the bowl shatters into seven pieces. Yunfeng Yue said, "If you scold me, I will let you have the last word;
if you spit at me, I will let you splash me with water."
Master Cuiyan Zhi addressed the assembly, saying: "To seek oil from sand is a pitiable matter; Cuiyan is chewing up his own food to feed an infant.
When you understand the ultimate reality of good and evil at that time, you will realize for the first time that your face has been covered in ashes all along."

Aṅgulimāla, carrying his alms bowl, arrived at the gate of a certain elder’s house. At that moment, the woman of the household was in the throes of labor, and mother and child had not yet been separated.
The elder said, "Disciple of Gautama, you are considered a most holy being; what dharma do you possess that can spare one from the perils of childbirth?
Aṅgulimāla replied to the elder, "I have only recently entered the Path and am not yet acquainted with this dharma. Please wait for me to return."
He questioned the World-Honored One and returned to report it; upon his return, he related the matter in detail. The Buddha told Aṅgulimāla, "Go quickly and tell him:
'Since I followed the Dharma of the Worthy and Holy Ones, I have never killed a living being. Aṅgulimāla, following the Buddha's instructions, went to inform the elder.
Upon hearing this, the woman was immediately released from her peril.
Caoshan Huisheng addressed the assembly, saying, "Everywhere else they all employ restrictive barriers; why not simply tell them the truth so that they may be free from doubt?
Yunmen came forward from among the assembly and asked, "Why is it that within the most profound secrecy one does not know what exists?
Caoshan said, "Precisely because it is so profound and secret, one does not know what exists. Yunmen asked, "How should one approach such a person? Caoshan said, "Do not."
"Approach the place of intimacy. [The Master] asked, "When one does not approach the place of intimacy, how is it?
He said, "Only then does one understand approaching. The Gatekeeper said, "Yes, yes."
Miaoxi said: "It is like adding wet lamp-wick to already turbid oil.
Master Yuanming of Deshan addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who come this way meet with a settled case;
those who do not come this way find themselves blocked and struck by an arrow. Even if one comes neither of these ways, it is like Xu Liu meeting the board-carrying man—a swift and sharp edge."
He remains a dull-witted fellow. Ten thousand *li* away there is not a cloud, yet the blue sky still remains. A monk asked, "What is it like when one is bold and unerring?
He replied, "A hitching post for donkeys. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? He replied, "One does not notice the stench of one's own excrement.
The monk said, "It is fine for you, Master, to speak thus. He replied, "A dung beetle rolling a ball of manure. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person who leaves no trace and no footprint?"
Regarding the place of practice, he said: "A thief who steals oxen. Question: "What is it like when one attains the Dharma-body without passing through the *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*?

He said: "Also standing beneath the signpost. Question: "What is it like before the antelope has hung its horns? He said: "A dog that hunts excrement. Question: "And what about after it has hung its horns?
He said: "A dog that hunts excrement. Question: "What is the path of the ancient Buddhas? He said: "The divine tree by the roadside."
Master Qingliang Fayan addressed the assembly, saying: "For those who have left the household life, it is sufficient simply to accord with the times and seasons.
When it is cold, it is cold; when it is hot, it is hot. If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the causes and conditions of time and season.
The skillful means of past and present masters are not few. Have you not seen how Master Shitou, upon reading the *Zhao Lun*, said: 'He who realizes all things as himself...'"
"Think of the Sage! Other teachers simply say: 'The Sage has no self, yet there is nothing that is not his own.
He has a single phrase which he calls the *Cantong qi* (Token of the Agreement of the Three). At the end, it says: 'The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of India does not exceed these words.
In between, he was merely speaking according to the occasion, Upasaka. Now, if you wish to realize all things as yourself, you must exhaustively encompass the Great."
"In this ground, not a single dharma can be seen. He further instructed the people, saying, "Do not let your time be spent in vain. He had just said to the Venerable Upādhyāya:
"It is sufficient simply to act according to the occasion and the season. If you miss the timing and lose the opportunity, that is precisely what it means to let one's time be spent in vain.
To form a conceptualization of form within that which is not form—Venerable Upādhyāya, to form a conceptualization of form within that which is not form is precisely to miss the mark.
At that time, the opportunity was lost. Now tell me, if you interpret form as non-form, is that correct or not? Elder, if you understand it in this way, there is no connection at all;
it is precisely like a madman running back and forth between two extremes—what use is there in that?
Elder, simply maintain your station and pass the time according to the season.

A monk asked Master Guangde Zhou of Xiangzhou: "I have heard it said in the teachings that Ajita does not sever afflictions nor cultivate meditative concentration, yet the Buddha prophesied that this person will undoubtedly attain Buddhahood. How is this principle to be understood? The Master replied: "The salt is exhausted."
"There is also no charcoal. [The Master] asked, "When the salt is exhausted and there is no charcoal, what then? He replied, "Do not speak of one's sorrows to a sorrowful person;
to speak of them to a sorrowful person is to kill that person with sorrow."
Miaoxi said, "When the ancients answered questions in such a manner, it was called 'washing one's feet and then boarding the boat.
When the Second Patriarch asked Bodhidharma, 'May I hear the Dharma-seal of all Buddhas? [Bodhidharma] replied, 'The Dharma-seal of all Buddhas is not obtained from another.

[The Patriarch] said, 'My mind is not at peace; I beg the Master to pacify my mind. [Bodhidharma] said, 'Bring forth your mind and I will pacify it for you. [The Patriarch] said, 'I have searched for it, but..."
"The mind cannot be apprehended. He said, "I have finished putting your mind at rest for you. Baizhao remarked, "It is like a diamond rubbing the back of a clay figure.
Master Xianglin Yuan was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of 'hiding one's body within the Northern Dipper'? He replied, "The moon is like a bow."
A bow. Little rain, much wind. Question: "What is the single lamp within the room? Answer: "Three people witness a tortoise being turned into a turtle.
Question: "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Answer: "The mountains are burned by fire in the twelfth month. Question: "What is it like when a fish swims on dry land? Answer:
"When one speaks, there must be a subsequent rescue. The monk said: "But what about when it descends back into the green depths? Answer: "The head..."
Valuing the tail over the head.
When Chan Master Hai of Shaoyang first met the Sixth Patriarch, he asked: "Regarding 'this very mind is Buddha,' I pray you will grant me an instruction and illustration.

The Patriarch said: "The non-arising of the preceding thought is the mind; the non-extinguishing of the succeeding thought is the Buddha. The manifestation of all phenomena is the mind; the departure from..."

All phenomena are identical to the Buddha. Were I to explain this in full detail, it would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon. Listen to my verse: "That which is the mind is called wisdom; that which is the Buddha is concentration.
When concentration and wisdom are held in equal balance, the mind becomes pure. To awaken to this Dharma-gate is due to your own cultivated nature."

Since they are fundamentally non-arising from the beginning, practicing both together is the correct path. The sentient beings receive this with faith, and he praised it in verse: "The mind itself is originally the Buddha;
Failing to realize this, one merely humbles oneself. I know that through the causes of concentration and wisdom, One practices both together, free from all phenomena."
Master Yaoshan had not ascended the hall for a long time. One day, the head of the monastery said, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instruction;
please strike the bell. Just as the assembly had gathered, the Master descended from his seat and returned to his quarters.
Miaoxi said, "There is no small amount of entanglement.
The head monk followed up by asking, "The Master promised to speak for the sake of the assembly; why do you not utter a single word?
He replied, "For the sutras there are masters of the sutras; for the treatises there are masters of the treatises. How can one blame this old monk?"
Miaoxi said, "It makes people laugh to death.
When Master Ximù was ascending the hall, a layman raised his hand and said, "The Master is nothing but a donkey."
He said, "The old monk has been mounted by you. The scholar was speechless. Three days later he returned and said, "I was robbed by bandits three days ago.
Yunmu took up his staff and drove him out.
One day, Master Xing of Ye County was reciting [the verse]: "To call it a bamboo stick is to encounter obstruction; not to call it a bamboo stick is to turn one's back.
[Master Nian] asked, "What should it be called so that it is correct? At these words, Xing attained great enlightenment.
He then seized the bamboo stick from [Nian’s] hand, snapped it in two, and threw it down the steps, asking, "What is this? Nian said, "Blind!"
He went to pay his respects. Because a monk requested instruction on Zhaozhou’s “Cypress Tree” koan, Xing said, "I do not refuse to explain it to you, but will you believe me?
The monk replied, "Since the Master speaks with such gravity, how would I dare not believe? Xing asked, "Do you hear the sound of raindrops falling from the eaves?
At that, the monk was suddenly enlightened; unconsciously letting out a cry of realization, he exclaimed, "Aha! Xing asked, "What have you seen?"
"What principle is this? The monk then replied with a verse: "The raindrops at the eaves drip clearly and steadily;
the universe is shattered, and in that very moment, the mind comes to rest. [Zhaozhou] was moved to joy and realization.
Master Fahua addressed the assembly, saying: "To speak of the gradual is to return to the ordinary and accord with the Way.
To discuss the sudden is to leave no trace behind. Even if one were to discuss the sudden and return to the ordinary, this would still be to force it upon them.
Fahua then went to Master Gong’an Yuan. Yuan asked, "What is the monastery? Fahua replied, "A lone tiger hides in the deep mountains; the shallow..."

"Grass and dew conceal the multitude of snakes. [The Master asked: "What is it like to be among those within the monastery? [The monk] said: "Green pines cannot cover it; how could yellow leaves possibly shield it?
[The Master asked: "What did you say? [The monk] said: "In youth, one plays with the moon at the edge of the heavens; in old age, one is dazed as the sun sinks behind the floating mulberry trees.
[The Master asked: "One phrase, two phrases—clouds parting to reveal the moon and dew. What is it like? [The monk] said: "It illuminates Buddhas and patriarchs."
The Fifth Patriarch, Master Yuan, addressed the assembly, saying: "Take the waters of the four great oceans as a single inkstone; take Mount Sumeru as a single writing brush.

If there were someone who could write the five characters 'The Meaning of the Patriarch’s Coming from the West' in the midst of empty space, I would descend from my seat, spread out my sitting cloth, and prostrate myself before him as my teacher.
If he cannot write them, then the Buddha-dharma has no efficacy. There was [a monk present].
"Is there? Is there? He then descended from his seat, and the assembly dispersed. The Master called out loudly, "Attendant! The attendant responded with a "Yes.
The Master said, "Gather up your sitting cloth (kaṣāya). He then asked the attendant again, "Have you gathered up the sitting cloth?
The attendant held up the sitting cloth. Yunyan said, "I knew long ago that you would act like this. He further addressed the assembly, saying, "Above is heaven; below is earth."
North, south, east, and west remain as they were; old Śākyamuni is merely playing with his own spirit. Since Bodhidharma came from the West, there has been much avoidance and hesitation.
Suppose a man were to come forth and say, "Monk, speak in a low voice. To him, you should simply say: "I only wish to throw a brick to draw out a jade."
When Yunmen saw a monk coming to visit him for instruction, he held up his *kāṣāya* and said:
"If you can speak, you fall within the circle of my *kāṣāya*; if you cannot speak, you remain sitting in a ghost cave. What will you do? He then spoke on his behalf: [He held up the robe.]
"So-and-so has no strength.
Miaoxi said, "In the Western Heavens they cut off heads and sever arms; here, you must go out and take charge yourself.
Master Xuansha addressed the assembly, saying, "The Buddha-way is leisurely and vast, with no fixed path; it is liberation through the gateless."
This is the Gate. It does not intend to convey the meaning of others, for it does not abide within the three periods of time;

thus, it cannot be ascended or sunk. Its establishment deviates from the True, yet it does not belong to the realm of conditioned creation. To move is to give rise to the root of birth and death; to be still is to be intoxicated in the land of dullness and torpor.

When both movement and stillness are extinguished together, one falls into a void. When both movement and stillness are gathered together, one is muddled regarding Buddha-nature. One must directly face dust and confront objects.
Like withered wood or cold ashes, they are applied as needed at the moment without failing their propriety. A mirror reflects all images without its radiance being disturbed;

a bird flying through the air does not become mixed with the color of space. Thus, throughout the ten directions there are no reflected images, and within the three realms there are no traces of movement.
One does not fall into the mechanism of coming and going, nor does one abide in a mind of the middle way. Within the bell there is no sound of the drum; within the drum there is no sound of the bell.

Sound: the bells and drums do not intersect; phrase follows phrase without priority or sequence. Like a strong man extending his arm, he does not borrow the power of another; like a lion roaming, how could he seek a companion?
In the ninefold heavens, free from obscuration, where is there a need for penetration? This single segment of radiance has never been dimmed.
If you arrive here, the essence is tranquil and still, eternally distinct and clear. Blazing with the brilliance of the sun, it is without limit or boundary.

Perfect enlightenment remains unmoving within the void; it swallows and illuminates heaven and earth with a transcendent radiance. Now, as for the Buddha appearing in the world, there is fundamentally no coming or going.
Names and forms have no substance; the Way is inherently suchness (*tathatā*). It is the natural state of reality, not something to be attained through cultivation or realization.

It requires only emptiness and leisure—never obscuring its functioning, yet never entangled in the mire of the mundane. Within this, not even a single hair’s breadth can be fully described; this is precisely what constitutes [the Way].
The retinue of the Mara King—the preceding and following phrases of a sentence—is a difficult point for the student. Therefore, a single phrase can encompass the whole;

through eighty thousand gates, birth and death are forever severed. Even if one attains a state like the moon’s reflection in an autumn pond or the sound of a bell in a still night—unimpaired by being struck and undispersed by touching the waves—this is still merely a matter on the shore of birth and death. This is the way of the Path-farer.
Wherever one treads is like fire melting ice; it never turns back into ice again. Once an arrow has left the bowstring, it has no power to return.
Therefore, they do not abide where they are caged, nor do they turn their heads when called. The ancient sages made no arrangements, and thus to this day there is no fixed location.
If you reach this point, you ascend the profound with every step, beyond the categories of heterodoxy and orthodoxy; consciousness cannot perceive it, and wisdom cannot comprehend it.

To know is to lose the fundamental source upon movement; to perceive is to become deluded regarding the ultimate intent. Those of the Two Vehicles tremble with fear, and those of the Ten Stages are struck with terror.

The pathways of speech are cut off, and the sphere of mental activity ceases. Thus, Śākyamuni remained silent in Magadha, Vimalakīrti closed his mouth in Vaiśālī, Subhūti proclaimed "non-explanation" to manifest the Way, and Śakra and Brahmā ceased listening as flowers rained down. If it is thus—
Manifest before you—what more is there to doubt? Having vanished from any place of dwelling, it is beyond the boundaries of past, present, and future;

it cannot be grasped by the mind or reached by thought. It is not produced by adornment, being primordially true and pure. Whether in movement, speech, or laughter, it is clearly manifest in every situation, lacking nothing whatsoever.
People of today do not awaken to this underlying principle; they recklessly involve themselves in worldly affairs and sensory dust, becoming defiled everywhere.
Attached to every single thing, one is bound by fetters. Even if you attain awakening, the sensory realms remain in chaotic confusion; names and forms are not real.

Consequently, you intend to settle the mind and withdraw thoughts, to subsume phenomena into emptiness. You close your eyes and hide your gaze; as soon as a thought arises, you immediately break it down, and as soon as a subtle perception emerges, you suppress it.
Such a view is precisely that of an externalist who has fallen into nihilism—a state where the soul is lost.
Scattered corpses lie in darkness and obscurity, devoid of sensation or cognition; they plug their ears and steal the bell, merely deceiving themselves.
Here, however, discernment is not like that. It is not a matter of hiding behind doors or leaning against walls.

Every phrase is manifest before one, beyond deliberation, untouched by literary ink, fundamentally severed from the realm of dust, and inherently devoid of rank or position. For the sake of convenience, such a person is provisionally named a "renunciant."
Ultimately, there are no traces. True Suchness—whether the stages of ordinary beings or sages, or hell or heaven—is merely a method for guiding the deluded child.
Since even empty space undergoes no change, how could the Great Way have any rising or sinking? To awaken, one moves freely in all directions without ever departing from the fundamental limit.
If you arrive here, there is no place for either ordinary beings or sages to stand. If you direct your attention toward the words, you will be drowned and destroyed.
If a student seeks outwardly, they fall into the realm of Māra. Above suchness, there is nothing to be contrived;
it is just like a blazing furnace that harbors not even a mosquito. This principle is fundamentally level—what need is there to clear it away? To stir or to manifest it...
The eyebrows are true liberation. The Way does not consist in forcefully employing the intellect to establish a position that deviates from the truth.

If you reach this point, you must not admit even a hair’s breadth of conceptualization; to apply the mind is to err. Even if a thousand sages were to appear here, they could not place a single character upon it.
"Having stood for a long time, take care.
When Zen Master Zhaozhou arrived at Zhunyu, he took his staff and walked from east to west and from west to east across the Dharma Hall.
Zhunyu asked, "What are you doing? Zhaozhou said, "Probing the water. Zhunyu replied, "There isn't even a single drop here."
"What is there to seek? He leaned his staff against the pillar and went out. Langye Jue said: "When the power departs, the servant insults the master;
when one's years decline, the ghost toys with the man."
Miaoxi said, "The hook is in the ground of non-doubt.
Master Yangshan once responded when Guishan asked, "The karmic consciousness of all sentient beings in the great earth is vast and boundless; they have no fundamental basis upon which to rely."
"How do you know whether he has it or not? Yangshan replied, "I have a way to test it. At that moment, a monk passed by in front of him.
Yangshan called out, "Acarya! The monk turned his head. Yangshan said, "Master, this is precisely what is called 'the vast expanse of karmic consciousness, having no fundamental basis to rely upon.
