"What can be done about me? Xuedou said, "It may be so, but these two are evil thieves; they only know how to cover their ears while stealing a bell.
National Teacher Wuye said to his disciples Huitin and others: "The nature of your seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing is coeval with the great void;
it is neither born nor extinguished. All realms are fundamentally empty and still from the beginning; there is not a single dharma that can [be grasped]."
It is attained. Those who are deluded do not understand this and thus take it as an object of confusion. Once one is confused by taking it as an object, one wanders through saṃsāra without end.
You all should know that the nature of the mind exists inherently from the beginning; it is not produced through artificial effort.
It is like a vajra, indestructible. All phenomena are like shadows and echoes; they possess no reality. Therefore, a sutra says: "Only this one thing is real; all else..."
The second is not the truth. If you realize that all is empty and that not a single thing exists to engage the mind, this is the sphere of the Buddhas' mental activity;
you should practice it with diligence.
Master Guishan addressed the assembly, saying: "The mind of a practitioner of the Way is straightforward and sincere, without artifice.
It has no 'back' and no 'face,' and is free from deceitful or false thoughts. In all activities at all times, seeing and hearing are ordinary, with no further complications.

Nor does it involve closing one's eyes or stuffing one's ears; it simply requires that the emotions do not cling to external objects. All the sages of the past have merely spoken of the faults on the side of turbidity."

As for afflictions: if one were free from such numerous evil thoughts, emotional views, perceptions, and habitual tendencies, one would be like the autumn waters—tranquil, pure, unconditioned, limpid, and unimpeded.
Such a person could be called a practitioner of the Way, and might also be called a man of no affairs. At that time, there was a monk who asked:
"Does one who has attained sudden enlightenment still have further cultivation to perform? He replied: "If one truly awakens to the source, they will know for themselves when it is so."

Cultivation and non-cultivation are dualistic expressions. Although one’s initial resolve now attains everything through conditions and realizes the fundamental principle all at once, there still remain the habitual tendencies accumulated over beginningless kalpas that cannot be purified instantaneously. One must therefore teach them to purify and eliminate the flowing consciousness of present karma;
this is what cultivation is. I do not say there is some other dharma to teach them to practice and pursue; it begins from hearing.
Entering into principle, one hears that the principle is profound and wondrous, and the mind becomes naturally luminous and perfect. One no longer dwells in the realm of delusion;
even if there are hundreds or thousands of subtle meanings being extolled or suppressed at that moment, this is like sitting down and putting on one’s robes, spontaneously resolving one's livelihood.

To state the essential point: within the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not a single speck of dust is admitted; within the gateway of Buddha-activity (*buddhakārya*), not a single dharma is abandoned. If it were a single-bladed sword...
Entering directly, the sentiments of both ordinary beings and sages are exhausted; the essence reveals true permanence. When principle and phenomena are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness.

Chan Master An Guo Ting was standing in attendance when a monk from Chang’an, who had been lecturing on the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, came to ask the Fifth Patriarch, “What is the meaning of ‘true nature as dependent origination’?
The Patriarch remained silent. At that time, Master Ting said, “Virtuous One, this is precisely...”
When the thought of inquiry arises, it is dependent origination within the true nature. At these words, the monk attained great enlightenment.
Miaoxi said, "Even when a single thought has not yet arisen, dependent origination cannot be absent.
Someone asked, "When a single thought has not yet arisen, what do you call dependent origination? Miaoxi replied, "I simply want you to speak in this way."

When Master Yue-shan first visited Xuefeng, he merely "dipped his finger" [into the water]. Later, while attending a vegetarian feast at Qingfeng Lou at the invitation of the King of Min, he sat for a long time;
suddenly, as he raised his eyes and beheld the sunlight, he attained sudden enlightenment. He then composed a verse, saying: "At Qingfeng Lou, I attended the official banquet;
On this day, the eyes of my entire life were opened wide. Only now do I believe that the matters of the distant Putong era [are no different from those of today]."
He brought it from the Pamir Mountains (Congling) and presented it to Xuefeng, who approved of it. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha-body? He replied, "Which Buddha-body are you asking about?
The monk said, "The body of Śākyamuni Buddha. [Xuefeng] said, "His tongue covers the three thousandfold world-system.

At the time of his death, he gathered the assembly and showed them this verse: "The visual faculty perishes along with forms; Auditory consciousness vanishes following sounds. Returning to the source is no different [from what it was]."

The Essential Meaning. Today and tomorrow, at Guoqing Temple, the Venerable Master was asked by a monk, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? He replied, "Śākyamuni is the Ox-Headed Jailor;
the Patriarchs are the Horse-Faced Attendants. He was further asked, "What is the meaning of the [Patriarch’s] coming from the West? He replied, "Hitting the eastern wall."
On the western wall, [a monk] asked, "What is the phrase that cannot be broken? He replied, "Not separated by even a hair’s breadth.
At that time, people looked up to him from afar. Master Luopu addressed the assembly, saying: "The final phrase reaches the ultimate barrier;
it blocks the essential ford, allowing passage neither to the mundane nor to the sagely. I have always told everyone: 'Let the world rejoice as it pleases,' yet I alone do not consent."
Why is this? It is like the numinous tortoise bearing the divine chart, which brought about the omen of its own destruction;
or like the phoenix caught in a golden net, wondering when it might soar to the clouds and mists. You must clarify the source beyond the literal meaning; do not seek patterns within words.
Therefore, if the stone man’s mechanism were like yours, he too would know how to sing the *ba* song; if you were like the stone man, you should also respond to the *xue* melody.
A monk asked Master Jia Shan, "When one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha, what then? He replied, "If you wish to know this matter, you must brandish the sword.
If you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will take up residence in the nest. When the monk asked the same question of Shi Shuang, Shuang said, "He has no land;
where would one meet him? The monk then related this to Jia Shan, who said, "This is the establishment of the gateway."
Without Jia Shan, even a profound discourse on entering the principle would still fall short of Shi Sang by a hundred paces.
Master Ledu Yan addressed the assembly, citing the Patriarch’s words: "The nature of all sentient beings is pure;
from the beginning it is unborn and there is nothing to be extinguished. This very body and mind are illusory births; within these illusions, there is neither sin nor merit. Great!

"Assembly, the former sages spoke thus; it is indeed extraordinary. Nevertheless, when examined from the standpoint of the monastic community, it is like suffering a heartache from overeating or a backache from sitting too long. He further addressed the assembly, saying: "A-he-he! What is this?"
Last night, sitting alone in the moonlight, I counted my old friends one by one from the beginning. Yet I recall that man who broke the hearth—what was he?
To even raise an eyebrow is already to have missed it. A monk asked: "What is it like when one plays the game upon meeting the occasion?"
It is said: "A black iron tortoise cast from a red furnace.
Imperial Teacher Wansong asked Shitou: "Setting aside concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people? Shitou replied: "In my place here, there are no servants;
what is there to set aside? Wansong asked: "How can this be understood? Shitou replied: "Can you even grasp the void?"
“Is it empty? he asked. [The monk] said, “If that is so, then I shall not depart from here today. Zhoutou asked, “I wonder, at what time did you come from that place?
[The monk] said, “I am no one from that place. Zhoutou said, “I have long known where you came from.
[The monk] said, “How can you, Master, frame me with false charges? Zhoutou said, “Your body is right here before me. [The monk] said, “Even though this is so, [it remains as it is]. He finished.
In the end, how did he instruct future generations? He replied, "Tell me, who is the 'future person'?
From this, Emperor Tiantai attained realization. Miaoxi said, "But tell me, what exactly did he realize?"

The Venerable Fu of Taiyuan was lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* at Xiaoxian Temple in Yangzhou. A practitioner of Chan was staying at the temple because of heavy snowfall and went to listen to the lecture.

When the discourse reached the "three causes of buddha-nature" and the "dharma-body of the three virtues," and the Venerable Fu extensively expounded upon the subtle principles of the dharma-body, the Chan practitioner could not help but laugh.
After the lecture concluded, Fu invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea and said to him, "My own aspirations have always been narrow-minded."

"Inferior! To rely on the literal text to explain the meaning has just earned you my laughter. I hope you will instruct me. The Chan practitioner said, "I truly laugh at you, Master of Commentaries, for not recognizing the Dharma-body.
Fufu said, "If this is how you explain it, where is it not correct? The practitioner said, "Please let the Master explain it once more.
Fufu said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, and horizontally it spans the ten directions."
It encompasses the eight directions and includes the two polarities of heaven and earth; responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade.

[Fufu] said, "I do not say that the Master of the Seat is wrong, but I am merely saying that he speaks of matters concerning the limits of the *dharmakāya*. In truth, he has not yet realized the *dharmakāya* itself.
Fufu said, "If this is so, then you, Virtuous Chan Master, should explain it for me. [The Master] asked, "Master of the Seat, do you believe it? Fufu replied, "How could I not?"
"How could I not believe it? he asked. [The Master] said, "If that is so, let the Head Preceptor suspend his lectures for ten days.
Sit upright in quiet meditation within your room, withdrawing the mind and gathering the thoughts, letting go of all conditions of good and evil at once. Trustingly rely upon what has been taught.

From the first watch of the night until the fifth watch, upon hearing the sound of drums and horns, he suddenly attained realization. He then went to knock on the door. The Chan practitioner said, "A!"
"Who are you? Hu replied, "I am so-and-so. The Chan practitioner rebuked him, saying, "I have instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and preach the Dharma on behalf of the Buddha.
Why did you come here last night drunk and lying in the street? Hu said, "Virtuous Chan Master, since I began lecturing on the sutras, I have been twisting the nostrils of my biological parents.
From this day forward, I shall never dare to act like this again. The Chan practitioner said, "Go for now; come back later."
They met daily. Fú subsequently ceased his lectures and traveled extensively through various regions. After spending a long time at Xuefeng, he acquired great renown.
Later, he returned to Yangzhou, where Minister Chen invited him to stay at his residence and provide for him.

One day, Fú said to the Minister, "Tomorrow I shall lecture on the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* once through as a way of repaying your kindness. When the Minister had finished preparing the vegetarian feast and tea, Fú ascended the seat.
After a long silence, he struck his ruler once and said, "Thus have I heard. He then summoned the Minister of State, who responded, "Yes.
Fufu said, "At one time the Buddha was staying... and immediately departed.
Yantou addressed the assembly, saying, "I once spent seven or eight years poring over the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.
Within it, there are two or three passages whose meaning somewhat resembles the talk of a patch-robed monk. He added, "Enough, enough! At that time, a monk said, "We request the Master to cite them."
The Master said: "The meaning of my teaching is like the three dots of the letter 'I' (𑖨).
The first dot is placed toward the east; it opens the eyes of all bodhisattvas. The second dot is placed toward the west; it sustains the life-force of all bodhisattvas.
The third dot is placed toward the zenith; it opens the crown of the heads of all bodhisattvas. This is from the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*."
The first meaning is as follows: It is further said, "The intent of my teaching is like that of Maheśvara;
he splits open his face and raises a single eye. This is the second meaning. It is further said, "The intent of my teaching is like a drum smeared with poison;
when struck once, all who hear it, whether far or near, perish. This is the third meaning. At that time, the Venerable Xiaoyan came forward and asked.
"What is the 'poison-coated drum'? Wuzu pressed his hands against his knees, leaned forward, and said, "Han Xin facing the throne.
Miaoxi, having finished citing this, shouted, "Withdraw your head!"
When Master Shoushan Nian ascended the hall, Master Fenyang Wude Zhaosheng came forward and asked, "What is the meaning behind Baizhang rolling up his mat?
[Shoushan] replied, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed. [Zhaosheng] said, "I do not yet understand what you mean, Master.

[Shoushan] replied, "Where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. At these words, Zhaosheng attained great enlightenment; he then lifted up his sitting cloth and looked out at the assembly.
He said: "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old azure pool—only after stirring it again and again does one begin to know it. He prostrated and returned to the assembly.

At that time, Master Xing of Ye County was serving as the Head Seat (Shouzuo). As soon as [Zhao] withdrew, Xing asked him, "Brother Zhao, what principle did you just perceive that you spoke in such a manner?
Zhao replied, "This is precisely where I let go of my body and surrender my life. Xing then ceased questioning.
Master Xing of Yechuan addressed the assembly, saying: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, a patch-robed monk is a man of penetration and transformation.

If he encounters various calamities such as boiling cauldrons and burning furnaces, how can he avoid them? If he cannot avoid them, what title can he bear but 'a man of penetration and transformation'?
What is the phrase that penetrates and transcends all such calamities? Is there anyone who has so penetrated and transcended?"
If you have attained it, try to express it before the assembly; I shall serve as your witness.
If you cannot penetrate through it, then ten thousand people will form a single tomb, and no one can take his place.
The Venerable Master Tang Ming-sōng was asked by a monk: "The ancients said, 'The eastern mountain and the western ridge are green.
What is the meaning of this? He replied: "The Persian’s nostrils are large. The monk said: "If that is so, then Kāśyapa in India and our Master here in the East [are one].
He replied: "Vajrapāṇi’s hand-board is wide. A monk asked: "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye? He replied: "The Buddha of Kaihua Temple claps his hands."
[The Master] laughed. [A monk said: "The Lady of Jin Temple understands singing. [The Master] asked: "When Linji pushed over Huangbo, why did the rector receive the staff?
He replied: "A dog that does not steal oil; a rooster carrying a lamp away."
When Master Xuefeng saw a monkey, he said, "This monkey each carries a mirror of antiquity upon its back.
Sansheng said, "Throughout kalpas it has been nameless; why do you designate it as a 'mirror of antiquity'? Xuefeng said, "A flaw has arisen.
Sansheng said, "As a teacher of fifteen hundred people, you do not even recognize the point of the discourse. Xuefeng said, "The affairs of this old monk’s abbacy are many."
Master Huanglong Xin addressed the assembly, saying: "Those of superior caliber who investigate the profound must investigate the living word; do not investigate the dead word. Why is this?
If you can attain realization within the living word, you will put all the patch-robed monks of the world to death.

If you can attain realization within the dead word, you will bring all the patch-robed monks of the world back to life. Now tell me: how would you speak a word that does not fall into either the living or the dead?"
The Taihu Lake spans thirty-six thousand qing. When the moon speaks from the heart of the waves, to whom does it speak?

A monk asked, "What are the four great poisonous snakes? He replied, "Earth, water, fire, and wind. The monk asked, "What are earth, water, fire, and wind? He replied, "The four great poisonous snakes.
The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master for an expedient means. He replied, "If one great element is thus, the other four are the same."
Master Qinglin Qian addressed the assembly, saying: "Under the gate of the Patriarchs, the bird-path is profound and subtle; when effort reaches its limit, it all turns back.
Without inquiry, it is difficult to clarify. You all must directly transcend mind, intellect, and consciousness to investigate, and leave the paths of ordinary and sage to study."
Only then can you be entrusted with the Dharma. If it is not so, you are not my child.
Miaoxi said: "Even if you were to transcend mind, intellect, and consciousness, penetrate thoroughly, leave the paths of ordinary and sage, and achieve mastery in study—"
This is also the bottom line of Xuefeng’s teaching.
When Minister Yang asked Guanghui Liai, he said: "I have heard the Master say that all sinful karma arises because of wealth and treasures;
you urge people to distance themselves from such riches. This is especially so for the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, who take wealth as their..."
[The Official] said, "In governing states, one gathers people through wealth; within the teachings as well, there are both the gift of wealth and the gift of Dharma.
How can you urge people to distance themselves from material riches? Lian said, "The iron dragon-head atop the banner pole. The Official said, "The stallion from Haitan is as large as a donkey.
Lian said, "A chicken of Chu is not a phoenix from Mount Dan. The Official said, "Two thousand years have passed since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa."
I, Qiu, am deeply ashamed.
Once, when a monk asked Master Wei of Qianzhou, "The essence and principle of the Three Vehicles and the Twelve Divisions of the Teaching have attained the wondrous;
are they the same as or different from the meaning of the Patriarchs? He replied, "One must discern beyond the six phrases; one must not turn according to sounds or forms. The monk—
He asked, "What are the six propositions? The Master said, "Speaking; silence; neither speaking nor silent; both speaking and silent;
all of these; none of these. What do you say to this? The monk was at a loss.
Master Guishan said to Master Yangshan, "You must personally turn the light back upon yourself and reflect inwardly.
Others do not know the extent of your understanding; try presenting your true realization to this old monk. Yangshan replied, "If you command me to look for myself..."
At this point, there is no stage of perfection, nor is there a single thing or a single understanding that can be offered to the Master.
Guishan said, "The place where there is no stage of perfection is precisely the place where you have formed your own conceptual understanding; you have not yet transcended mind and object.

Yangshan said, "Since there is no stage of perfection, where is there any dharma? What thing could one grasp to serve as an object? Guishan said, "Was it not just now that you were forming such an understanding?"
Yang said, "It is. Mian replied, "If it is so, this is the dharma of a fully present mind and object; you have not yet escaped the mind of 'mine.
Originally, there was someone who understood how to offer to me; I grant that your stage of faith is manifest, but your stage as a person remains hidden."
Deshan Yuanming addressed the assembly, saying: "Whenever National Teacher Jueyi was questioned or answered, he would simply raise a single finger.
When it is cold, heaven and earth are cold throughout; Xuedou says, 'Where did you see Old Jueyi? When it is hot, heaven and earth are hot throughout;
Xuedou says, 'Do not mistake the zero point on the scale. He further said: 'The myriad phenomena of the forest and the mountains penetrate through.'"
Below, one is solitary and precarious; above, the great earth, mountains, and rivers are all steep and impassable. Where can one find even a "finger-pointing" bit of Zen?
Miaoxi said, "One might say that you, sir, have a nobleman’s forgetfulness."
In the past, when Mañjuśrī arrived at the assembly place of the Buddhas, he encountered the Buddhas each returning to their respective abodes.

There was only one woman seated near that Buddha, having entered into samādhi. Mañjuśrī then addressed the Buddha, saying, "Why is it that this woman is permitted to sit near the Buddha, while I am not?
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī, "You need only awaken this woman and cause her to emerge from samādhi."
[The woman] emerged from her faint. "You ask it yourself," [the Buddha said]. Mañjuśrī circumambulated the woman three times, snapped his fingers once, and then lifted her up to the Brahma Heaven;

yet, even exhausting all his supernatural powers, he could not bring her back down. The World-Honored One said, "Even if there were hundreds of thousands of Mañjuśrīs, they would still be unable to emerge from this woman's samādhi.
Below, past lands as numerous as the sands of forty-two Ganges Rivers, there is a net...
Jālinīprabha was able to bring this woman out of her meditative absorption.

In an instant, the Great Being Jālinīprabha emerged from the earth, prostrated before the World-Honored One, and the World-Honored One commanded Jālinīprabha to depart. Jālinīprabha then returned to the woman's presence and snapped his fingers once.
The woman then emerged from her meditative concentration. Yunju You’s verse says: "A hundred thousand Mañjuśrīs could not have brought her forth;
Jālinīprabha did not expend the slightest effort. The setting clouds and the solitary wild goose fly together; The autumn waters and the vast sky share one color.
Tianyi Huai’s verse says: "Mañjuśrī entrusted her to the Brahma Heaven; Jālinīprabha lightly snapped his fingers. The woman—"
The Yellow-Faced Gautama watches another fall and rise.
When a monk asked Master Nantai An, "What is it like when all is silent and there is no dependence? he replied, "As for that which is silent."
There is a verse that says: Sitting in quietude on the Southern Terrace, a single incense burner; All day long, he remains unmoving, forgetting all myriad concerns.
It is not that he has stilled his mind to eliminate delusive thoughts, But simply because there is nothing to be pondered.
Miaoxi let out a shout.
When Master Linji arrived at Sanfeng, he asked Master Ping, "Where have you recently come from? Miaoxi said, "Last night, Golden Ox fell into the mire;
even until now, no trace is seen. Ping said, "The autumn wind blows through the jade flute; who is that?"
Zhaozhou said, "Directly penetrating ten thousand layers of barriers, not dwelling even beyond the azure heavens. Linji said, "This question is far too high.
Zhaozhou said, "A golden phoenix born from a dragon breaks through the emerald lapis lazuli. Linji said, "Sit and drink tea. Linji then sat.
Linji asked again, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Longguang. Linji said, "At Longguang recently..."
"What words? Jie then went down to enter the hall.
Master Lestam Zhun addressed the assembly, saying: "Identity and difference, formation and destruction, general and particular—three, four, five, six, seven, eight."
If you wish to follow the flow of the stream, there is nothing better than first understanding this Dharma. He then picked up his staff, struck it once, and said:
"This Dharma cannot be understood through conceptualization or discrimination. If you discriminate, you fall into the realm of sentient beings.
But tell me, what is it that is neither discriminated nor conceptualized? He then threw down the staff and said: "Miaozhan (Profoundly Clear)."
"The Dhāraṇī of the Immovable Honored One, the King of Śūraṅgama, is rare in this world. He further addressed the assembly, saying:
"It has rained incessantly for a long time, until the black clouds gather thickly over the peaks of Wulao; the white waves of Lake Dongting surge up to the heavens.
Yunmen Master, unable to restrain his impatience, burned incense within the Buddha Hall and joined his palms at the main gate to offer prayers."
He offered this prayer: "May the woman of Huangmei give birth to a son; may mother and child be reunited.
May the hornless iron ox of Shaoshi always find sweet water and grass. He gave a shout and said, "What connection is there?"
Master Yuntai Qin addressed the assembly, saying: "Is there anyone who can discern this? If you can discern it, what is it?

It is nothing but a worn-out straw sandal from a village. If you cannot discern it, it falls to the ground with a golden sound. A monk asked: "What is 'discussing the truth while opposing the mundane'?
The Master said: "You hired hand, what are you asking? The monk asked: "What is 'following the mundane while opposing the truth'? The Master said: "You hired hand, what are you asking?"
Zhaozhou said, "Go drink tea.
Zen Master Longtan asked Emperor Tianhuang, "Since I first arrived, I have not received instruction on the essential point of the mind from you, Master."
The Emperor said, "Since you arrived, there has never been a time when I have not pointed out the essential core of your mind. [The Master] asked, "Where did you point it out?
The Emperor replied, "When you brought me tea, I accepted it for you; when you brought me food, I received it for you; when you bowed in greeting, I lowered my head.
Where was I not pointing out the essential core of your mind? While Longtan stood reflecting on these words, the Emperor said:
"If you see, you see directly; if you hesitate to think, you have already missed it. Longtan attained immediate enlightenment. He then asked again, "How does one maintain this?
Huang said, "Roam freely according to your nature; relax and let go in accordance with conditions. Simply exhaust the ordinary mind; there is no separate 'sage's understanding'."
A monk asked Master Xuefeng, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? He replied, "Staring with wide eyes, one cannot see the bottom.
The monk asked, "And what of those who drink from it? He replied, "It does not enter through the mouth. When Zhaozhou heard the monk recount this, he said, "It does not enter through the mouth."
[The water] entered through his nostrils. The monk then asked, "What is it like when the ancient stream is a cold spring? Zhaozhou said, "Bitter.
[The monk] asked, "And what of those who drink from it? Zhaozhou said, "Dead. When Feng heard this, he remarked, "Zhaozhou is an ancient Buddha," and then prostrated himself toward him from afar.
From this point on, he did not answer questions.
Regarding the matter of repaying his debt of gratitude, Master Baoneng was asked by Fayan, "Whom have you seen? He replied, "I saw Master Qingfeng.
Fayan asked, "What words or phrases were exchanged? He said, "I once asked him, 'What is the student's own self?'"
Feng said, "The child of Bingding comes to seek fire. Yan asked, "How do you, the Senior Monk, understand this? He replied, "'Bingding' belongs to fire;
it is like seeking fire with fire, or seeking oneself with oneself. Yan said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can that suffice?
He asked, "I have only understood it this way; I do not know what your honorable intention is, Master. Yan said, "Then ask me."
I gave you the Way. You then asked, "What is the student's own self? Mazu replied, "A child of the Bing-ding trigram comes seeking fire.
At these words, he attained great enlightenment.
Xuansha and Tianlong were entering the mountains when they encountered a tiger. Long said, "The tiger, Master. Xuansha replied, "It is your tiger.
Upon returning to the monastery, Long requested instruction, saying, "Master, today you saw a tiger in the mountains; I wonder what your intention was?
He replied, "In this Sahā world there are four kinds of most grave matters. If a person can penetrate them, they will be able to transcend the realm of the five skandhas."
Miaoxi spoke on their behalf: "I know that the Master is earnest in his concern for others.
Master Baoning Yong’s verse says: "A fierce tiger stands in the path, alone displaying its majesty; Its claws and fangs are truly as sharp as needles.
Pitiful are those who, unaware, lose their lives; To gather up their shattered bones is truly a matter for lamentation."
Master Pang’s verse says: "The mind is as it is, and the objects of the senses are also as they are; There is neither reality nor emptiness. I care not for existence, nor am I bound by non-existence.
I am neither a sage nor a holy one, but a common man who has understood the matter. Easy indeed, easy! Within these very five aggregates lies true wisdom.
The world of the ten directions shares the same One Vehicle; How could there be two in the formless Dharmakāya? If one abandons afflictions and enters..."
"Bodhi. [The Master asked: "I do not know in which direction lies the Buddha-ground.
When the fundraising monk returned, Master Huanglong Nan ascended the seat and said: "There are five things that are difficult to do:

first, it is difficult for the donor; second, it is difficult for the fundraiser; third, it is difficult for one who transforms the raw into the cooked; fourth, it is difficult for one who sits upright while eating."
"Unchanging. Now tell me, who is this person of the fifth unchanging? After a long silence, he said, "Heh! and then descended from his seat.
At that time, Yiyan Zhen was serving as the Head Seat (Shouzuo). The Librarian asked Zhen, "Who is the one of the fifth unchanging?
Zhen replied, "One who sees the cheek behind the head—do not associate with such a person."
In the past, the Venerable Shigong was a hunter. While chasing a deer, he passed before Mazu’s hermitage and asked the Master, "Did you see a deer pass by?
Mazu replied, "Who are you? He said, "I am a hunter. Mazu asked, "With one arrow, how many do you shoot?
He replied, "One arrow shoots one animal. Mazu said, "You are not a skilled archer. He asked, "Does the Master know how to shoot? Mazu—
[The Master] said, "I am skilled at archery. [The Patriarch] asked, "When the Upādhyāya shoots an arrow, how many does it strike? The Patriarch said, "One arrow strikes a whole flock.
[The Master] said, "Since both parties possess life, why shoot a whole flock? The Patriarch said, "Since you know this, why do you not shoot yourself?
[The Master] said, "If you were to have me shoot myself, I truly would find no place to apply my hand. The Patriarch said, "This fellow has been so for kalpas past."
The affliction of ignorance was suddenly extinguished this day. At that time, the Master cast down his bow and arrows and entered the Patriarch’s lineage to leave the household life.
When Master Xuansha ascended the hall and the assembly had gathered, he took up his staff and drove them all away at once.
He then turned back to his attendant and said, "Today I have reached a realization; it was perilous, as if entering hell like an arrow shot. The attendant said, "How wonderful!"
"Dehe Shang (Master Dehe) has regained his human body. Cuiyan Zhi said, "Great and small Xuansha, the former does not reach the village and the latter does not reach the inn.

How can one speak of the path of transcendence? Daowu Zhen said, "Great and small Master Zhi is merely one-sided and withered. If it were Daowu, it would not be so; Xuansha and his attendant each possess [the Way]."
One Eye. Once Master Luoshan asked Shishuang, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied, "You must become like cold ashes and withered wood;
you must go for ten thousand years in a single thought; you must go in accord with the lid fitting the box; you must go entirely pure and free from a single speck. Luoshan...
It did not accord with his realization. He went back to Yantou and asked the same question as before. Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases?
At these words, Shishuang attained awakening. Later, Venerable Mingso of Tang asked Shoushan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Shoushan replied, "Chu."

To the east of the You River, by the side of the royal city, there was a hermitage where [Huangbo] attained a sudden realization that accorded with the Buddha’s intent. He then composed three verses on the Mysterious (Sanxuan):

"When the function is obtained, one must simply employ it; let not the mind and intellect be fixed or stirred. For three years the lion has roared, and throughout the ten directions the fox-lineage is cut off.
I possess the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā), which is like being hidden behind a curtain. Break open the gates of the six sense-doors, and the Vairocana shall manifest."
Lu Yin said, "My true bone is a vajra-body, fit for praise; a single stroke against the six dusts leaves them forever unobstructed.

The vast and empty world takes emptiness as its essence; within that essence, non-action is truly reaching home. When Shanshan heard this, he invited him to tea and asked, "Were these three verses composed by you?
He replied, "Yes. Shanshan said, "Suppose someone were to instruct you to manifest the thirty-two marks—would you do so?"
"How is it? he asked. Baizhang replied, "I am no wild fox spirit. Baizhang said, "Save your eyebrows. Baizhang asked, "How many have you lost, Master?
Baizhang struck him on the head with his bamboo staff and said, "This fellow will go on to cause chaos hereafter."
Yunmen once said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illness. First, there is the lack of clarity in all places, as if there were an object directly before one's face.
Second, even when one has penetrated through so that all phenomena are empty, there is still a lingering sense, as if some kind of thing were present."
This, too, is a case where light has not yet penetrated through. Furthermore, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illnesses.
First, having attained the Dharma-body, one fails to forget the attachment to dharmas; one's own views still persist, and one remains seated within the realm of the Dharma-body—this is the first.
Even if you manage to penetrate through to the Dharma-body, you must not let it pass unexamined. If you scrutinize it closely, what trace of breath remains? That, too, is an illness.
Miaoxi said, "Do not treat this as a Zen assembly; do not treat it as a discourse on the Way; do not engage in higher-level deliberation.
This is the old man Yunmen speaking according to reality. In my speaking thus, there is immeasurable offense.
If you can examine this through and through, I will grant that you possess the eye of discernment; if you cannot examine it, then..."
Investigate this within the "cloud-gate" tangles of Yunmen.
Once, when Attendant Kuò asked Master Dēshān, "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone? Dēshān said, "What? What?
Kuò said, "When the Emperor issues a decree for the flying dragon horse, the lame tortoise sticks out its head. Dēshān then ceased speaking.
The next day, after bathing and coming out, Guok passed the tea to Shanshan. Shanshan patted Guok on the back once and said, "What about yesterday's *gong'an*?
Guok replied, "This old fellow has only just begun to see clearly today. Shanshan then let the matter rest.
The monk Qi of Yandang was asked by a monk, "When the night moon spreads its light, why is there no reflection in the azure pool?

Qi replied, "A master at play with his own shadow. The monk then moved from east to west and stood there. Qi said, "Not only are you playing with your shadow; you are even terrified of your own head."
The monk asked Master Da’ning Kuan, “What is the white ox on the open ground? Kuan placed his fire tongs across the hearth and said, “Do you understand?
The monk said, “I do not. Kuan said, “The head is not lacking; the tail is not redundant.

A monk asked, “When Danxia burned the wooden Buddha, why did the temple manager’s eyebrows and beard fall out? Kuan said, “Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. The Master was present [at this time].
At Tong’an, he saw a monk pass away. The monk then asked, “Since you are Tong’an, why has this sick monk passed away?

He replied, “Giving alms is not as good as paying back one’s debts. The monk asked, “The Dharma is without taking or rejecting; why do you transmit it from one to another? He replied, “Transmission is without taking or rejecting.
The monk asked, “Mahākāśyapa possessed right view; why did he pick up the flower and then smile? He replied, “Unable to restrain his impatience.”
Jin asked, "Why is it that the Chan practitioners of the world cannot produce this circle (○)? He replied, "It is often like this.
Master Zifu Yuan asked Jingqing, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Jingqing said, "Everyone wants to know.
Yuan said, "In that case, the eyes of the multitude are difficult to deceive. Jingqing said, "Principle can subdue even a leopard."

If you wish to become Buddhas, you yourselves are already Buddhas; yet you run about in haste to other houses, like thirsty deer chasing a mirage."
"When will you attain the corresponding state and depart? You wish to become a Buddha;

however, if you were simply free from these many inverted,攀缘 (dependent), deluded, and evil thoughts—the defilements and impurities of the sentient being’s mind—then you would already be a Buddha of initial enlightenment.
Where else would you need to seek one? This is why I settled you at Mount Mí for over thirty years, letting you eat at Mount Mí..."
Eating rice, he defecates the dung of Mount Guishan, yet he does not study the Chan of Mount Guishan; he simply watches a single water buffalo.
If it strays onto the road or enters the grass, he pulls it out; if it trespasses upon the crops, he whips and subdues it. After a long time, this pitiable creature learns to obey human commands.
Now it has been transformed into a white ox in the open air, always present before one’s eyes, manifest throughout the entire day.
It stands far apart; even if you pursue it, you cannot catch it. You all possess within yourselves a priceless great treasure.

From the gateway of the eyes, it emits light that illuminates the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. From the gateway of the ears, it emits light that perceives and discerns all sounds, whether good or evil.
These six gateways constantly emit radiance day and night; this is also called the Samādhi of Emitting Light. Yet you yourselves do not recognize it, and so you grasp at [external things].
The shadow resides within the body composed of the four great elements; it is supported from both within and without, never allowed to lean or tilt.
It is like a person carrying a heavy burden across a single-plank bridge, never once losing their footing. Tell me, what thing is this? By being supported in such a manner, it remains thus.
If you seek it even for a hair’s breadth, you will not see it. Therefore, Master Zhigong said: "Seek it within and without."
Searching for it, there is nothing at all; yet within the realm of sensory objects, activity is vast and complete.
Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk replied, "I have. Zhaozhou said, "Go and drink tea.
Or, if he said, "I have not been here," Zhaozhou likewise said, "Go and drink tea. The head monk remarked, "Master, why do you tell those who have been here to go and drink tea?"
When someone said they had never been there, Zhaozhou replied, "Go drink tea. The monastery director said, "Director," and Zhaozhou responded, "Go drink tea.
Baofu remarked, "Zhaozhou is adept at seizing the opportunity."
When Master Duan Shizi was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the wild goat has not yet grown its horns? he replied, "I am afraid.
The monk said, "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra* (a spiritual friend), why are you afraid? He replied, "I have never seen such a strange beast. Furthermore, his "Song of Tending Cattle" says:
"Cattle! Cattle! Cattle! Rest! Rest! Rest! Do not pull the plow or drag the harrow; Let them pass through winter and summer as they will."
*Chunqiu* (Spring and Autumn): No cord, no rope; no standard, no hook. Brought forth this morning and sent off into the desolate wilds—far, far away, leaving no trace;
rest, and do not seek further.
Master Dalong was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "It is you. The monk asked, "How should one understand this? He said:
Furthermore, he even detested the lack of handles on his alms bowl.
Jia Shan addressed the assembly, saying: "Recognize the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses; recognize your own self in the midst of the bustling marketplace.
Yun Men said: "A frog drills into your nostrils; a venomous snake pierces your eyes. For now, you must seek recognition within these entanglements."
Zhaozhou took it up.
Miaoxi said, "Jiashan set a trap and drew an arrow upon himself; Yunmen mistook a thief for his own son.
Although this is so, those who recognize kindness are few, while those who betray it are many."

Master Huanglong Nan addressed the assembly, saying: "There is one person who studies the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* in the morning and the *Prajñāpāramitā* in the evening, diligent day and night without a moment’s rest.
There is another person who does not investigate Chan nor discuss doctrine, but simply takes up a tattered mat and sleeps in the sun.
When these two people arrive together at Huanglong—one with effort and the other without effort—how shall they be settled?"
"Which one is it? After a long silence, he said: "The Goddess of Fortune and the Lady of Darkness—the wise master accepts neither.
An ancient master once did not go to the hall; when an attendant came to invite him to the hall, the master said: "Today I am at the manor."
The monk had eaten his fill of oil-cakes. The other said, "The Master has not been in or out. Xiu said, "You simply go and ask the headman of the estate.
As soon as the monk stepped outside, he suddenly saw the headman returning to thank the Master for coming to the estate to eat oil-cakes.
When Du Xianggong asked Master Baotang, "I have heard from Master Jin about the Dharma-gate of the three phrases: 'no recollection,' 'no thought,' and 'do not be deluded.
Is this so? The Master replied, "It is. The Duke asked, "Are these three phrases one or three? The Master said, "'No recollection' is named precept;
'no thought' is named concentration; 'do not be deluded' is named wisdom. When the single mind does not arise, it fully possesses precept, concentration, and wisdom."
"It is neither one nor three. The Master asked, "In the latter phrase, does the character for 'delusion' (妄) mean delusion as derived from the 'heart' radical?
He replied, "It is that which is derived from the 'woman' radical. The Master asked, "Is there a scriptural authority for this? He replied, "The *Dharmapada* says:

'If one gives rise to a mind of striving, this is delusion, not true striving. If one can keep the mind free from delusion, striving will be boundless. Upon hearing this, the Master's doubts were completely dispelled.
Master Cheng served Master Xiu at Yuyuan in Jingnan. Later, as the two schools flourished, the disciples of Xiu frequently derided the Southern School, saying:
"Master Neng does not recognize a single character; what excellence does he possess?"
Xiu said, "He has attained teacherless wisdom and profoundly realized the Supreme Vehicle; in this, I am not his equal.

Furthermore, that my Fifth Patriarch personally entrusted me with the robe and the Dharma was certainly no mere formality. What I regret is that I could not travel far to attend upon him in person, thus receiving the bounty of the state in vain.
You should not remain here; you may go to Caoxi to resolve your doubts. When you return in the future, you shall still serve as my [successor]."
He spoke thus, and Cheng immediately paid his respects and took his leave. Upon arriving at Shaoyang, he joined the assembly for formal inquiries, yet did not mention where he had come from.

At that time, the Sixth Patriarch addressed the assembly, saying, "There is currently a thief of the Dharma hidden within this gathering. Cheng has come forth to pay his respects and has fully related his circumstances."

The Patriarch said, "How does your teacher instruct the assembly? He replied, "He constantly instructs the great multitude to dwell the mind in the observation of stillness and to sit long without lying down.
The Patriarch said, "To dwell the mind in the observation of stillness is a sickness, not Chan; to sit long and bind the body—what benefit is there for the principle?
Listen to my verse: "Since birth, sitting and never lying down; When dead, lying down and never sitting. It is originally but stinking bones."
Tou asked, "What constitutes establishing merit or fault? Cheng said, "I do not yet know by what Dharma the Master instructs people.
The Patriarch said, "If I were to say that I have a Dharma to give to others, I would be deceiving you. I simply follow the circumstances to untie their bonds; this is provisionally called samādhi."
"Listen to my verse: 'The self-nature precept is entirely without mind; the self-nature wisdom is entirely without obstruction. The self-Adamantine is neither increasing nor decreasing;
the coming and going of the body is fundamentally samādhi. Having truly heard this verse, he repented and apologized, then immediately took up his staff and returned home.
He then composed a verse, saying: 'The illusory body of the five aggregates—how can illusion reach its ultimate end? Turning toward True Suchness, the Dharma returns.'"
"Not pure. The Patriarch agreed with this. He soon returned to Yüquan.
Master Ch’ui-yen Chen addressed the assembly, saying: "Not seeing a single dharma is a great calamity.
Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars—form and emptiness, light and darkness—are not a single dharma. Raising his staff, he said: "Ordinary people see..."
To call a staff a staff: when a śrāvaka sees a staff, he recognizes it as inert emptiness and dismisses the staff as non-existent.
When a bodhisattva sees a staff, how could it ever have caught on his teeth? When hungry, he eats; when weary, he sleeps.
When cold comes, one turns toward the fire; when hot, one seeks coolness. Have you not heard it said that "the wisdom of all wisdoms is pure"?
To speak in such a manner would crack open the nostrils of the local earth-spirit. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "In the same pit, there is no different soil.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He replied, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing. The monk asked, "What is the Great Dharma of the Buddha?"
[The Master] said, "The five supernormal powers of the noble ones. [The student] said, "I, a learner, do not understand. [The Master] said, "The tongue reaches up to the Brahma Heaven.

[The student] asked, "What is the place where a learner turns his body? [The Master] said, "When one wall is built, a hundred walls are adjusted. [The student] asked, "What is the place where a learner exerts effort?
[The Master] said, "A thousand days of gathering firewood, burned in a single day. [The student] asked, "What is the place where a learner finds intimacy? [The Master] said, "Entirely..."
The family sent him to the ferryhead boat.
Huangbo served as the head seat (śrāmaṇera) under Nanquan. One day, he took up his alms bowl and sat upon Nanquan’s seat.

When Nanquan entered the hall and saw him, he asked, "Venerable Elder, for how many years have you been practicing the Way? Huangbo replied, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja. Nanquan said, "Even so..."
"This is the grandson of the Old Teacher Wang. [Baizhang] went down and sat in the second seat; Baizhang then moved over to the second seat. Baishui withdrew.
Guishan said, "He who deceives the enemy perishes. Yangshan said, "Not so. You must know that Huangbo possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers.
Guishan said, "The extent of your realization has reached such a height. Xuedou said, "What a pity for the Old Teacher Wang; he saw only the awl."

Touzi: "At that time, had I been Nanquan, I would have waited for him to say 'before King Wei-yin,' and then immediately taken the second seat, leaving Huangbo unable to rise for the rest of his life. Even so, I must still rescue Nanquan."
Miaoxi said: "Why wait to ask about his age or his practice? As soon as he entered the hall and saw him presiding at the head seat, he took up his bowl and sat in the second seat.
Even if Huangbo possessed the 'trap for tigers' strategy, where could he have applied it?"
Master Fojian addressed the assembly, citing a monk who asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'?
Zhaozhou made the gesture of flowing water with both hands, and the monk attained realization. Another monk asked Fayan, "'Do not grasp at appearances;
remain as such, unmoving. How does one not grasp at appearances while seeing the unmoving? Fayan replied, "The sun rises in the east."

The night falls in the west. That monk also attained realization. If you can see it here, only then will you know that the whirlwind overturning the mountains is fundamentally ever-still, and the rivers rushing in competition originally do not flow. If this is not yet so, I cannot help but speak further:
Heaven rotates to the left, Earth turns to the right; through how many cycles have they passed from antiquity to the present? The golden crow flies, the jade...
The hare runs; having just emerged from the gates of the sea, it falls once more behind the green mountains. The waves of the rivers and streams are vast and boundless;

the surges of the Huai and Ji are long and leisurely. It flows directly into the blue ocean, day and night. Then he raised his voice and said: "O Zen practitioners, do you see that which is suchness, unmoving?"
When Chan Master Huáng first visited the Fifth Patriarch, although he had consulted him on matters of doctrine, he followed a gradualist approach to practice.
Later, returning to north of the River, he built a hermitage and sat in long-term meditation; for more than twenty years, he never showed a look of indolence.

It was only when he encountered the Sixth Patriarch’s disciple, Chan Master Cè, who was traveling through the region north of the River, that he learned Huáng had once studied under the Fifth Patriarch at Huangméi and had resided in his hermitage for many years. He then considered himself [to have attained realization].
Zhengshou was observing and knew that Hui had not yet attained the "Unsurpassed" (Anāgamya) stage. He went to him and asked, "What are you doing sitting here?
Hui replied, "I am entering meditative absorption. Zhengshou said, "When you say you are entering absorption, is there a mind or is there no mind?
If there is a mind, then all wriggling creatures should be able to attain absorption. If there is no mind, then all grasses and trees should likewise be able to attain it."
[The Master] said, "When I am truly entering samādhi, I do not perceive a mind of existence or non-existence.

[The interlocutor] asked, "If you do not perceive a mind of existence or non-existence, this is constant samādhi; how could there be entering and exiting? If there were entering and exiting, it would not be the Great Samādhi."
Huang remained silent for a long while, then asked, "Whom do you follow as your teacher? He replied, "My teacher is the Sixth Patriarch of Caoxi.

He asked, "What does the Sixth Patriarch take to be meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*)? He replied, "My teacher said: 'The wondrous, profound, and perfectly quiescent nature is such that its essence and function are *tathatā* (suchness).

The five aggregates are fundamentally empty; the six sense-objects do not exist. There is no emerging and no entering; no fixity and no distraction. The nature of meditation has no abiding; it is free from abiding.'"

"Regarding meditative stillness (*dhyāna-śama*): the nature of meditation is non-arising; one departs from the conceptualization of arising in meditation. The mind is like empty space, yet it lacks even the measure of empty space.

Upon hearing this essential teaching, Huáng abandoned his hermitage and went to study under the Sixth Patriarch. The Patriarch, taking pity on him for having traveled such a great distance, bestowed upon him an opening instruction.
Under these words, Xiang attained a sudden and profound realization. The mind he had cultivated over the preceding twenty years left no trace whatsoever.
That night, lay devotees and commoners in Hebei suddenly heard a voice from the air saying, "Today, Chan Master Xiang has attained the Way.
Thereafter, he returned to Hebei to transform and guide the fourfold assembly.
Yantou went to visit Deshan; as soon as he stepped across the threshold, he asked, "Is this ordinary or is it holy? Deshan gave a shout, and Yantou immediately prostrated himself.
Later, a monk recounted this to Dongshan, who said, "Had it not been for Master Huo, it would have been very difficult to take charge of."
Touwen remarked, "Old man Dongshan does not recognize good from bad; he has wrongly applied these names and phrases.
At that time, I held one hand up while pressing down with the other.

Master Mingzhao addressed the assembly, saying: "To meet the full edge of the sword and overcome the victor—rarely is such a true知音 (one who understands) encountered. To die together and live together... [ten thousand...]

Not a single one exists within it. Following words and chasing phrases, their number is like the sands of the Ganges. Citing the past and citing the present, they seek to exterminate the lineage of the barbarians.
On the single path beyond, even "cracking and pecking" is still out of step. When Confucian scholars meet, they grasp their whips and turn their heads;
what the śramaṇas see is truly a bitter pity. Casting away true gold, they follow the crowd to gather clods of earth. I tell you, young children, do not waste your efforts in vain. Understand!
To obtain the profound mystery of others while still clutching tiles and rubble is not as good as casting it once to soar beyond the great void. Who would dare approach this sharp blade of spirit?
Only when you can withstand the incoming arrow do you truly merit the title of a man of honor; if you intend to swallow your voice in silence, a single blow from my mattock will suffice.
A monk asked Master Sanjiao, "What are the Three Jewels? He replied, "Rice, wheat, and beans. The monk said, "I do not understand.
He replied, "The assembly joyfully accepts and upholds them."
Zihu said: "For over thirty years I have lived at Zihu; my strength for the morning and evening meals of gruel and rice has been quite coarse.
When there is nothing to do, I go up the mountain for a stroll. I ask you people of this time: do you understand?"
Miaoxi said, "It must not be discussed as the Buddha-dharma; it must not be understood as worldly dharma. Do you all understand?
Nan-yuan asked a monk, 'Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, 'Xiangzhou. Nan-yuan asked, 'What have you come here for? The monk replied, 'I have come specifically for this.'"
The monk paid his respects to the Abbot. The Abbot said, "I happen to have met with Baoying's absence. The monk then gave a shout. The Abbot said, "I told you he was not here;
why do you shout again? The monk shouted once more. The Abbot struck him. The monk bowed. The Abbot said, "This staff was originally for you to strike me, but I shall strike you instead.
I want this story to circulate. You blind fellow! Go to the hall for practice."

Master Huanglong Nan addressed the assembly, citing Chan Master Yongjia: "Wandering through rivers and seas, traversing mountains and streams, seeking teachers and visiting paths for the sake of investigating Chan—since I recognized the road to Caoxi, I have known that birth and death are no longer relevant."
Venerable Elders, what are those mountains and rivers you travel through? What is that teacher you seek?
What is that Chan you investigate? What is that Way you visit? To seek teachers and inquire after the Way in Huainan, Liangzhe, Mount Lu, Mount Heng, Yunmen, and Linji;
to investigate Chan at Dongshan and Fayen—this is to run outward in pursuit. This is called...
"O outsider! If you take the self-nature of Vairocana as the ocean and the wisdom of prajñā-cessation as dhyāna, this is called 'seeking within.
If you seek outwardly, it will run away and kill you; if you dwell within the five aggregates and seek therein, it will bind and kill you.
Therefore, the practitioner of dhyāna is neither internal nor external, neither existent nor non-existent, neither real nor false. One does not see the path within, yet one sees."

Externally and internally, both are erroneous; the Way of the Buddha and the Way of Mara are both evil. To go thus in a fleeting instant—like the moon setting behind the western mountains—to seek further through sound and form, where could one find its name? It is remote beyond reach.

Mazu resided at the Chuanfa Temple and practiced seated meditation daily. Master Rang recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma and went to visit him, asking, "Virtuous One, what do you hope to achieve by sitting in meditation?
Mazu replied, "I hope to become a Buddha. Rang then took a brick and began polishing it on a stone slab in front of Mazu’s hut.
Mazu asked, "What are you doing? Rang said, "I am polishing it to make a mirror. Mazu remarked, "How can polishing a brick ever produce a mirror?"
Xie said, "Can one become a Buddha by practicing *zuo-chan* (sitting meditation)? The Patriarch asked, "What then is it? Xie replied, "It is like a person driving a cart.
If the cart does not move, do you strike the cart or do you strike the ox? The Patriarch had no reply. Xie spoke again, saying, "Do you study sitting meditation, or do you study sitting as a Buddha?
If you study sitting meditation, meditation is neither sitting nor lying down. If you study sitting as a Buddha, the Buddha is not..."

Regarding the characteristics of meditative concentration (*samādhi*): within the dharma of non-abiding, one should neither grasp nor reject. If you sit as a Buddha, that is precisely to kill the Buddha;
if you cling to the characteristic of sitting, you have not realized its principle. Upon hearing this instruction, the Patriarch was like one drinking clarified butter (*sarpis*).
He prostrated himself and asked: "How should I apply my mind so as to accord with the signless *samādhi*? Nanyue replied: "Your study of the Dharma-gate of the Mind-ground is like planting seeds."
The essential points of the Dharma I teach are like the rain from heaven; because your conditions have converged, you shall perceive the Way.
He asked again: "The Way has no form or characteristics; how can it be seen? He replied: "The Dharma-eye of the mind-ground can see the Way;
the same is true for signless samādhi. He asked: "Does it have arising and ceasing? He replied: "If one perceives the Way through arising and ceasing, or gathering and dispersing,"
"No, it is not so. Listen to my verse: 'The ground of the mind contains all seeds; when it meets moisture, they all sprout. The flower of samādhi is formless;

what could be destroyed, and what could be formed? Upon hearing this, the Patriarch attained awakening, and his mind became transcendent. He attended [the Master] for ten years, daily progressing toward the profound mysteries."
The Monk of Changsha sent a monk to ask his fellow practitioner, Master Hui, saying, "After you met Nanquan, what was it like?
Hui remained silent. The monk asked, "What was it like before you had met Nanquan? Hui replied, "It cannot be said that there was anything else. The monk returned and reported this to Changsha.

Changsha then presented a verse, which says: *Sitting atop a hundred-foot pole,* *If you can take another step forward,* *Then you will see the ancient buddhas.* *If you cannot take that step,* *You will surely fall into the pit of the common crowd.*
"Such a person, though they have gained entry, has not yet reached the truth. One must advance further from the top of a hundred-foot pole; the ten directions of the world are one's entire body.
A monk asked, "How does one advance from the top of a hundred-foot pole? The Master said, "Mounts of Langzhou, waters of Lingshou. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The four seas and five lakes are all within the Imperial Transformation."
Miaoxi said, "If you wish to see Changsha take another step forward, and if someone were to ask how to advance that one step,
I would wait and then entangle you in a web of complications."
When Master Fuyong Xun first visited Guizong, he asked, "What is the Buddha? Guizong said, "If I tell you, will you believe me?
Xun replied, "If the Master speaks the truth, how could I dare not believe? Guizong said, "You yourself are it. Xun asked, "How does one maintain this?
Guizong said, "A single film over the eye, and empty flowers fall in confusion. At these words, Xun attained realization.
Fayan said, "If there were no subsequent words, where would one seek the 'returning to the source'?
Master Zhenjing, upon ascending the hall to address the assembly, said: "Let the questioning cease for a moment.

You know only to ask about the Buddha and the Dharma, yet you do not realize the place from which the Buddha-Dharma comes. Tell me, from what place does it come? He then lowered one foot and said, "In the past..."

The Yellow Dragon personally issued this command. Not one of the Buddhas of the ten directions has dared to disobey it; not one of the ancestral masters of successive generations or all the worthy sages has dared to transgress it.
Regarding the infinite Dharma-gates and all subtle meanings, the tongues of the old monks throughout the land have been sealed from beginning to end by this single seal, none daring to differ.
Let us set aside for a moment the question of non-difference: where does this seal reside?
"Do you see it? If you see it, it is neither monk nor layperson, neither partial nor biased; I have entrusted it to each of you individually.
If you do not see it, I shall take it back myself. He then withdrew his foot and shouted: "The army follows the seal; the general pursues the talisman.

As for this old fellow from Shengyuan—whose hands are those of a Buddha and whose feet are those of a donkey—I shall give him thirty blows of the staff for his pains! Is there anyone in this assembly today who does not agree?"
"Mm? If it exists, how extraordinary! If it does not exist, then the new elder is deceiving you all.

Therefore, our Great Awakened World-Honored One, on the eighth day of the twelfth month in the kingdom of Magadha, at the moment the morning star appeared, suddenly and completely awakened to the Way.
All sentient beings of the great earth attained Buddhahood at once. Now there is the śramaṇa Kewen, a disciple of the Śākya."
On the thirteenth day of the sixth month, at the hour when the blazing sun appears, in the city of Jinyang in the Great Song dynasty of Eastern Zhendan—what else has been realized?
[The Master] drew a line with his whisk and said: "I do not dare to look lightly upon you;
you shall all become Buddhas."
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Where does a person who 'knows' go? Nanquan replied, "He goes to become a water buffalo at the house of a donor in front of the mountain.
Zhaozhou said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master. Nanquan said, "Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window.
Yunfeng Yue said, "Had it not been Nanquan, we would have ended up smashing our heads against a wall."
At Mount Zhou, National Teacher Wuye asked Mazu, "What is the patriarch’s secret transmission of the mind-seal that came from the West?

Mazu said, "Virtuous One, you are in the midst of a great commotion. Go now; come back at another time. As soon as the teacher had stepped out, Mazu called out, "Virtuous One! The teacher turned back.
The Master bowed his head. The Patriarch asked, "What is this? The Master suddenly attained realization and prostrated himself. The Patriarch said, "You dull-witted fellow!
Why do you prostrate yourself?"
Master Huìtáng addressed the assembly, saying: "If one clarifies only the self but does not awaken to what is before one's eyes, this person has eyes but no feet.
If one awakens to what is before one's eyes but does not clarify the self, this person has feet but no eyes.
According to these two types of people, throughout the twelve periods of the day, there is always something harbored within their chests. Since that thing is in the chest, they are ill at ease."
The mark is ever present before one’s eyes. Since it is already before one’s eyes, every path one encounters becomes an obstruction.

How can one attain peace and stability? The Patriarch did not say: "To grasp it is to lose the proper measure; one will inevitably enter a deviant path. To let go naturally, its essence has neither going nor staying."
The Sixth Patriarch was once discussing the wind and the banner with two monks. One said, "It is the wind that moves. The other said, "It is the banner that moves.
The Patriarch said, "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. It is you, O worthy ones, whose minds move. The two monks were struck with awe. Xuefeng said, "How great is the Master!
He has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. He deserves twenty blows of the staff. As Fuzhao the Elder stood in attendance, he gnashed his teeth. Xuefeng said:
If I speak in such a manner, I too deserve twenty blows. Miaoxi said:
"Do you wish to recognize Elder Fu? When the rhinoceros gazes at the moon, patterns form upon its horns. Do you wish to recognize Xuefeng?
When the elephant is startled by thunder, flowers enter its tusks."
Fayan asked Xiu, the Mountain Master: "A hair’s breadth of difference means heaven and earth are separated by a vast gulf. How do you understand this, brother?

Xiu said, "A hair’s breadth of difference means heaven and earth are separated by a vast gulf. Fayan said, "If you understand it in that way, how can it be right? Xiu said, "I simply understand it in this way; what about you, Master?
Fayan said, "A hair’s breadth of difference means heaven and earth are separated by a vast gulf. At these words, Xiu attained realization.
There is a realization here. Baoning Yong’s verse says: The Stone City asks his fellow practitioner with intimacy; Without speaking of east or west, he points directly south.
The two paths of light and dark, where they come and go, Are faintly winding through the mist and mists.
Master Fayun Gaoshan was asked by a monk: "What did Bodhidharma transmit when he came from the West? He replied: "The Zhou, Qin, Han, and Wei. [The monk] asked: "Monk, ask Yun..."
[The Master] asked, "What is the phrase for penetrating the Dharma-body? The Gatekeeper said, "Hiding one's body within the Big Dipper.
[The Master] asked, "What is the meaning of this? He replied, "A sincere heart, slice by slice. [The Master] said, "If it were me, a student, it would not be so. He asked, "And how about you?
He replied, "Last night I raised my head to look at the Big Dipper; it was vaguely like a piece of sugar-cake. [The Master] said, "Just mind your grass and water; there is nothing else."
Master Suzhi was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha of Fixed Light? He replied, "A duck swallows a snail.
The monk asked, "Does this allow the student to turn himself around? He replied, "The eyeballs protrude."
Master Xiangyan Duan addressed the assembly, saying: "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Beyond speech and silence, there is a matter.
This old monk’s mouth is too narrow; I cannot explain it to you. He then descended from his seat.
When a monk asked Master Tiantu Huì, "Before Bodhidharma came to this land, was there still the Buddha-dharma?
He replied, "Setting aside for a moment the time before he arrived, what is the matter right now? The monk said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for instruction.
He replied, "The eternal void of ten thousand ages; the wind and moon of a single day. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand? From your own side..."
"How is it? [The Master] said. "What does it matter whether that other one, Bodhidharma, has come or not? His coming was much like a fortune-teller.
Seeing that you did not understand, he pierced through for you. As soon as the lines of the divination appeared, good and bad fortune were entirely within your own sphere;

The Monk of Fenyang said: "One who expounds the Dharma must possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical to Reality.

If it is not centered, the feathers will break and the arrow cannot fly through the air. When the string is taut and the feathers are firm, the arrow pierces both the air and the target.
What is meant by "the ten wisdoms being identical with reality"? I shall point them out for you, venerable elders: first, they share the same substance; second, they share the same great matter.
Third, identical in total participation; fourth, identical in true wisdom; fifth, identical in universal pervasiveness; sixth, identical in full possession; seventh, identical in gain and loss;
eighth, identical in birth and death; ninth, identical in the roar of the voice; tenth, identical in entry. It is further asked: With what person is one identical in entry?
With whom is one identical in the roar of the voice? What is it that is identical in birth and death? What thing is identical in gain and loss? A.

Which one is identical to the Great Matter? What thing is identical in its single substance? Is there anyone who can point it out?
